They say the Most Merciful has taken a son. Exalted is He! Those they speak of are only honored servants. They do not speak before Him and act by His command. They speak only for those He approves, and they are full of fear of Him.

hardWords.m: things that make life easy and pleasant

148.title: Signs in Creation; Every Soul Tastes Death

paragraphs.text: If any of them claimed to be a deity besides Allah, his reward would be Hell. Have the disbelievers not seen that the heavens and earth were joined, and Allah separated them? He made every living thing from water. He set firm mountains on the earth so it would not shift, and made paths between them. He made the sky a protected roof. He created night and day, the sun and the moon, each swimming in its orbit.

No human before lived forever on earth. Every soul will taste death, and Allah tests people with bad and good. When disbelievers see the Prophet, they make fun of him. Man was created hasty, so he should not rush Allah's signs. They ask when the promise will come. If only they knew the time when they cannot push the Fire from their faces or backs! It will come suddenly and confuse them. Messengers before were also mocked, but the mockers were surrounded by what they laughed at.

Who can protect them night or day from the Most Merciful? Their false gods cannot even help themselves. Allah gave them and their fathers good things and long lives. Do they not see the land shrinking at its edges? The deaf do not hear the warning. But if even a breath of punishment touched them, they would cry, "We were wrongdoers!"

hardWords.m: the path something moves on in the sky
make someone unable to think clearly

149.title: Fair Scales, and Abraham Breaks the Idols

paragraphs.text: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will set up fair scales, and no soul will be wronged at all. Even a deed as small as a mustard seed will be brought forward. Allah gave Moses and Aaron the criterion, a light and a reminder for the righteous. They fear their Lord unseen and fear the Hour. This Qur'an is also a blessed reminder. Will they deny it?

Allah gave Abraham good judgement before. He asked his father and people, "What are these statues you are devoted to?" They said their fathers worshipped them. He said they and their fathers were clearly wrong. They asked if he was serious or joking. He said, "Your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and earth, who created them, and I am a witness to this."

He swore by Allah to plan against their idols. When they left, he broke them into pieces, except the biggest one, so they might return to it. The people asked who had done this. Some said they heard a young man named Abraham speak about them. They brought him before everyone. They asked, "Did you do this to our gods?" He said, "No, this biggest one did it. Ask them, if they can speak."

hardWords.m: a tool used to weigh things
a plant with very tiny seeds
something that shows right from wrong

150.title: The Fire Becomes Cool for Abraham

paragraphs.text: The people blamed themselves for a moment. Then they turned back and said, "You know these do not speak." Abraham said, "Then why worship, instead of Allah, what cannot help or harm you? Shame on you and on what you worship! Will you not think?" They shouted, "Burn him and support your gods!" But Allah said, "O fire, be cool and safe for Abraham." They wanted to harm him, but they became the greatest losers.

Allah saved Abraham and Lot and brought them to a land He had blessed. He gave Abraham Isaac and Jacob, and made all of them righteous. They were leaders who guided by Allah's command. They did good deeds, prayed, gave zakah and worshipped Allah. Lot was given judgement and knowledge, and was saved from a city of evil deeds. Allah took him into His mercy.
Noah called to Allah, who answered him and saved him and his family from the great flood. The people who denied the signs were all drowned.

David and Solomon judged a case about a field that a people's sheep entered at night. Allah gave Solomon understanding of the case, and gave both of them judgement and knowledge. The mountains and the birds praised Allah with David. Allah taught David to make armor to protect people in battle. Will you then be grateful?

hardWords.m: metal clothing that protects in war

151.title: Prophets Who Called Out and Allah Answered

paragraphs.text: Allah made the strong wind serve Solomon. It blew at his command toward the blessed land. Some devils dived for him and did other work, and Allah guarded them.

Job called to his Lord, saying that hardship had touched him. Allah answered him and removed his pain. He gave him back his family, and as many again, as a mercy. Ishmael, Idrees and Dhul-Kifl were all patient, and Allah let them into His mercy. The man of the fish left in anger. Then he called out from the darkness, "There is no deity except You. I have been one of the wrongdoers." Allah saved him from his distress, and He saves the believers in the same way. Zechariah asked not to be left without an heir. Allah gave him John and made his wife able to have a child. These people hurried to do good. They prayed in hope and fear and were humble before Allah. Allah also made Mary, who guarded her chastity, and her son a sign for the worlds.

Your religion is one religion, and Allah is your Lord, so worship Him. Yet people divided into groups, but all will return to Him. A believer's good effort will never be ignored, because Allah records it. Then Gog and Magog will be let loose and rush down from every high place. When the true promise comes near, the disbelievers will stare in horror. They will cry, "Woe to us! We were careless and wrong."

hardWords.m: a child who receives what a parent leaves

152.title: Hell, Paradise, and the Shaking of the Hour

paragraphs.text: The disbelievers and what they worship besides Allah will be fuel for Hell. If those false gods were real, they would not enter it. There they will groan and will not hear. But those promised the best reward will be kept far from Hell. They will not even hear its sound. They will live forever in what they desire. The greatest terror will not make them sad. Angels will meet them and say, "This is your promised Day."

On that Day, Allah will roll up the heaven like a written sheet. As He began the first creation, He will repeat it. This is His promise. In the Psalms, Allah wrote that His righteous servants will inherit the land.

Allah sent the Prophet only as a mercy to the worlds. He was told to say that there is only one God, so people should submit to Him. If they turn away, he has warned them all equally. He does not know if the promised punishment is near or far. Allah knows what people say and what they hide. Perhaps the delay is a test. The Prophet asked Allah, the Most Merciful, to judge with truth.

O mankind, fear your Lord! The shaking of the Hour is a terrible thing. On that Day, every nursing mother will forget her baby. People will look drunk though they are not, because Allah's punishment is severe.

hardWords.m: to make a deep sound of pain
a time of waiting before something happens

153.title: Creation, Resurrection, and Worshipping Allah on an Edge

paragraphs.text: Some people argue about Allah without knowledge. They follow every rebellious devil, who leads them to the punishment of the Blaze.

If you doubt the Resurrection, think about how Allah created you. He made you from dust, then a drop of fluid, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh. He keeps whom He wills in the womb for a fixed time. Then He brings you out as a baby, and you grow strong. Some die young. Others reach a weak old age and forget all they knew. The earth looks dry and dead. When Allah sends rain, it swells and grows every beautiful plant. This shows that Allah is the Truth and gives life to the dead. The Hour will surely come.

Some people argue about Allah with no knowledge or clear book. They turn away proudly to lead others from His way. They will have shame here and Fire later. Allah is never unjust to His servants. Some people worship Allah on an edge. When good touches them, they are content. When a trial strikes, they turn away and lose both worlds. They call on things that can neither harm nor help.

Allah will admit the believers who do good into gardens with rivers. On the Day of Resurrection, He will judge between all the religious groups. Everything in the heavens and earth bows to Allah. The disbelievers will wear garments of fire, with boiling water poured on their heads.

hardWords.m: rising from death to life again
the place inside a mother where a baby grows

154.title: Fire, Gardens, and the Call to Hajj

paragraphs.text: In Hell, boiling water will melt the disbelievers' insides and skins. Iron rods will strike them. Each time they try to escape in pain, they will be pushed back. But the believers who do good will enter gardens with rivers. They will wear bracelets of gold and pearls and clothes of silk. They were guided to good words and to the path of the Praiseworthy.

Some disbelievers block people from Allah's way and from al-Masjid al-Haram. This mosque is for all people, those who live near it and visitors. Whoever plans wrong there will taste painful punishment.

Allah showed Abraham the place of the House. He told him to associate nothing with Allah and to purify the House for those who walk around it and pray. Abraham was told to call people to Hajj. They would come on foot and on thin camels from far away. They would mention Allah's name over the animals He gave them, eat, and feed the poor. Then they should keep their vows and walk around the ancient House. Honoring Allah's symbols comes from piety of the heart. People must avoid idols and false speech. Whoever associates others with Allah is like someone falling from the sky.

Allah gave every nation a rite of sacrifice. Give good news to the humble, who fear Allah, stay patient, pray and spend. Camels and cattle are among Allah's symbols, so eat from them and feed the needy.

hardWords.m: fear and love of Allah shown in life

155.title: Allah Defends the Believers and Warns Proud Nations

paragraphs.text: The meat and blood of the animals do not reach Allah. What reaches Him is your piety. Allah defends the believers, and He does not like those who betray and are ungrateful. Permission to fight was given to those who were attacked and wronged. They were driven from their homes only for saying, "Our Lord is Allah." If Allah did not hold back some people by means of others, places of worship would be destroyed. These include monasteries, churches, synagogues and mosques. If Allah gives the believers power in the land, they pray, give zakah, command good and forbid wrong.

If people deny the Prophet, many nations denied their prophets before. These include the people of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, Abraham, Lot and Madyan. Even Moses was denied. Allah gave the disbelievers time, then seized them. Many cities now lie in ruins, with empty wells and tall palaces. It is not the eyes that are blind, but the hearts in the chests. A day with Allah is like a thousand years of our counting.

The Prophet is only a clear warner. Believers who do good will have forgiveness and noble provision. Satan tried to throw doubts into the message of every prophet. But Allah removes what Satan throws in and makes His verses firm. This becomes a test for those with sick or hard hearts.

hardWords.m: places where monks live and worship

156.title: Allah's Judgment, Signs, and Care for People

paragraphs.text: Those given knowledge will see that the Quran is the truth. Their hearts will become humble. But the disbelievers will stay in doubt until the Hour comes suddenly. On that Day, all sovereignty belongs to Allah, and He will judge. Believers who did good will be in the Gardens of Pleasure. Those who denied His signs will have a shameful punishment.

Some people left their homes for Allah's cause and were then killed or died. Allah will give them good provision and a place that pleases them. If someone is harmed and responds only equally, and is then treated unjustly, Allah will help him.

Allah makes the night enter the day and the day enter the night. Allah is the Truth, and what they call on besides Him is false. He sends rain, and the earth turns green. He made all on earth useful to you, and ships sail by His command. He holds the sky so it does not fall. He gives you life, causes you to die, and will give you life again. Yet mankind is ungrateful.

Allah gave every nation its rites of worship. So the Prophet should not let the disbelievers argue with him, but invite them to his Lord. If they dispute, Allah knows best what they do and will judge their differences. Everything is in a Record, and that is easy for Allah.

hardWords.m: food and things needed for life

157.title: A Weak Fly, True Striving, and Successful Believers

paragraphs.text: People worship things besides Allah without any proof or knowledge. When Allah's clear verses are recited, the disbelievers' faces show anger. They almost attack those who recite. But the Fire that Allah promised them is far worse.

Here is an example, so listen. Those you call on besides Allah could never create even a fly, even if they all worked together. If a fly stole something from them, they could not take it back. Both the seeker and the sought are weak. People have not truly valued Allah, who is Powerful and Mighty. He chooses messengers from angels and from people. He knows what is before them and after them.

O believers, bow, prostrate, worship your Lord and do good, so that you may succeed. Strive for Allah as He deserves. He chose you and put no hardship on you in religion. It is the religion of your father Abraham. Allah named you Muslims before and in this Quran. So pray, give zakah and hold firmly to Allah. He is the best protector and the best helper.

The believers have truly succeeded. They are humble in their prayer and turn away from bad talk. They give zakah and guard their private parts, except with their wives or those their right hands possess. Those who seek beyond that are transgressors. The believers keep their trusts and promises, and they carefully protect their prayers.

158.title: Paradise, Human Creation, and Noah's Call

paragraphs.text: These believers are the heirs who will inherit al-Firdaus. They will stay there forever.

Allah created man from an extract of clay. Then He placed him as a drop of fluid in a safe place. He made the drop into a clinging clot, and the clot into a lump of flesh. From the lump He made bones and covered them with flesh. Then He made him into another creation. Blessed is Allah, the best of creators. After that, you will die, and on the Day of Resurrection you will be raised.

Above you Allah made seven heavens, and He is never unaware of His creation. He sends rain from the sky in measure and keeps it in the earth. He could also take it away. With it He grows gardens of palm trees and grapes with many fruits. He also grows a tree from Mount Sinai that gives oil and food. In livestock there is a lesson. You drink from them, eat from them and get many benefits. You ride on them and on ships.

Allah sent Noah to his people. He told them to worship Allah alone and fear Him. But their leaders said he was only a man like them who wanted to be above them. They said Allah would have sent angels instead. They called him mad and told people to wait. Noah asked his Lord for help because they denied him.

hardWords.m: a part taken out of something
farm animals like cows and camels

159.title: Noah's Ship and Nations Who Denied Their Messengers

paragraphs.text: Allah told Noah to build the ship under His watch. When the command came and the oven overflowed, he was to bring two of every kind, and his family. Those already decreed to perish were left out. Noah was not to speak for the wrongdoers, because they would drown. On the ship, he should praise Allah for saving them from the wrongdoing people. He should ask Allah to let him land at a blessed place. In this story there are signs, and Allah always tests His servants.

After them, Allah raised another generation and sent them a messenger from among them. He also told them to worship Allah alone. Their rich leaders denied the Hereafter. They said he was only a man who eats and drinks like them. They said obeying him would make them losers. They mocked the promise of rising again after becoming dust and bones. They said there is only this life, and called him a liar. The messenger asked Allah for help. Allah said they would soon regret. Then a mighty shriek seized them, and they became like dry stubble.

Then Allah raised other generations. No nation can come before its fixed time or stay after it. Allah sent His messengers one after another. Each nation denied its messenger, so they were destroyed one after another and became only stories.

hardWords.m: people living at the same time
laughed at in an unkind way
dry, cut stems left in a field

160.title: Moses, Mary's Son, and Those Who Hurry to Good

paragraphs.text: Allah sent Moses and his brother Aaron with His signs and clear proof. They went to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but these people were arrogant. They said, "Should we believe two men like us, while their people serve us?" They denied them and were destroyed. Allah gave Moses the Scripture so that people might be guided. He also made the son of Mary and his mother a sign. He gave them shelter on high ground with flat land and flowing water.

Allah told the messengers to eat good food and do righteous work, because He knows what they do. Your religion is one religion, and Allah is your Lord, so fear Him. But people split their religion into sects, and each group is happy with what it has. So leave them in their confusion for a while. Do they think that their wealth and children mean Allah is rushing good things to them? No, they do not understand.

The true believers are afraid of their Lord. They believe in His signs and associate nothing with Him. When they give, their hearts are still fearful, because they will return to their Lord. These are the people who hurry to do good deeds, and they are first in reaching them.

hardWords.m: thinking you are better than others

161.title: Hearts Turned Away from the Clear Truth

paragraphs.text: Allah never places on any soul more than its capacity. He has a record that speaks the truth, and no one will be wronged. But the disbelievers' hearts are confused about this, and they keep doing evil deeds. When punishment seizes their wealthy people, they cry out for help. They will be told not to cry today, because no help will come. Allah's verses were recited to them, but they turned back. They were proud and spoke evil at night.

Have they not thought deeply about the Quran? Did they not know their Messenger? Do they say he is mad? No, he brought them the truth, but most of them hate the truth. If the truth followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would be ruined. The Prophet does not ask them for payment, because his Lord's reward is best. He invites them to a straight path, but those who reject the Hereafter leave the path.

Even if Allah showed them mercy and removed their trouble, they would continue wandering blindly in their wrongdoing. He touched them with suffering, but they did not humble themselves before their Lord. When a door of severe punishment opens, they will fall into despair. Allah gave you hearing, sight and hearts, but you are rarely grateful.

hardWords.m: how much someone can carry or do

162.title: Questions That Show Allah Owns Everything

paragraphs.text: Allah spread you through the earth, and to Him you will be gathered. He gives life and causes death. The change of night and day is His. Will you not think? Yet the disbelievers repeat what earlier peoples said. They ask how they can be raised after becoming dust and bones. They say this promise was made to their forefathers too. They call it old legends.

The Prophet is told to ask them questions. To whom do the earth and everyone in it belong? They will answer, "To Allah." Then will you not remember? Who is Lord of the seven heavens and the Great Throne? They will say, "Allah." Then will you not fear Him? In whose hand is the control of all things? Who protects, while no one can protect against Him? They will again say, "Allah." Then how are you fooled? Allah brought them the truth, but they are liars.

Allah has not taken any son, and there is no other deity with Him. If there were, each would take what it created, and they would fight one another. Allah is far above what they say. He knows the unseen and the seen.
The Prophet prays, "My Lord, if You show me what they are promised, do not place me among the wrongdoers." Allah is able to show him what He has promised them.

hardWords.m: family members who lived long ago
old stories that may not be true
the great seat of a king

163.title: Death, the Scales, and Regret in the Fire

paragraphs.text: The Prophet is told to push back evil with what is best. Allah knows well what they say. He should seek refuge in Allah from the whispers of the devils, and from their coming near him.

When death comes to a disbeliever, he says, "My Lord, send me back, so that I may do good in what I left." But these are only words. Behind them is a barrier until the Day they are raised. When the Horn is blown, family ties will not matter, and no one will ask about another. Those whose scales are heavy with good deeds will succeed. Those whose scales are light have lost themselves and will stay in Hell forever. The Fire will burn their faces.

They will be asked, "Were My verses not recited to you, and you denied them?" They will say their misery overcame them and they went astray. They will beg to be taken out and promise not to return to evil. Allah will say, "Stay there in shame, and do not speak to Me." Some of His servants used to pray for forgiveness and mercy. But the disbelievers mocked them and laughed at them, until they forgot to remember Allah. Today Allah has rewarded those servants for their patience, and they are the winners. Then Allah will ask how many years they stayed on earth.

hardWords.m: a tool used to weigh things

164.title: Life Is Short, and Surah an-Nur Begins

paragraphs.text: They will answer that they stayed only a day or part of a day. Allah will say that they stayed only a little, if only they had known. Did they think Allah created them for no purpose, and that they would not return to Him? Exalted is Allah, the true King. There is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne. Whoever calls on another deity without proof will face his Lord, and the disbelievers will not succeed. The Prophet is told to pray, "My Lord, forgive and have mercy. You are the best of the merciful."

Allah sent down this surah with clear verses and duties, so that people may remember. The unmarried woman and man found guilty of adultery are to receive a hundred lashes each, and believers should witness it. Those who accuse chaste women without four witnesses are to receive eighty lashes. Their testimony is never accepted again, unless they repent and reform.

A husband who accuses his wife with no other witnesses swears four times by Allah that he is truthful. The fifth time, he calls Allah's curse upon himself if he is lying. She is saved from punishment if she swears four times that he is lying, and the fifth time calls Allah's anger on herself if he is truthful. A group among the believers spread a lie. This turned out to be good for the believers. Each liar earns his share of sin.

hardWords.m: to say someone did something wrong

165.title: Guarding Against Slander and Entering Houses Politely

paragraphs.text: When the believers heard the lie, they should have thought well of one another. They should have said, "This is a clear lie." The slanderers brought no four witnesses, so in Allah's sight they are the liars. Without Allah's favor and mercy, a great punishment would have touched them. They passed the story on with their tongues without knowledge. They thought it was small, but to Allah it was very serious. They should have said, "It is not right for us to speak of this." Allah warns them never to do this again.

Those who love to spread indecency among the believers will have painful punishment. O believers, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Only by Allah's favor is anyone made pure. Those with wealth should not swear to stop helping relatives, the poor and emigrants. They should forgive and overlook. Would you not like Allah to forgive you?

Those who falsely accuse innocent, believing women are cursed in this world and the next. On that Day, their tongues, hands and feet will witness against them. Good people are declared free of what the slanderers say, and they will have forgiveness.

O believers, do not enter other people's houses until you ask permission and greet the people inside. If no one is there, do not enter. If you are told to go back, then go back. That is purer for you.

hardWords.m: people who spread lies to hurt others
to choose not to punish a mistake

166.title: Modesty, Marriage, and the Light of Allah

paragraphs.text: There is no blame in entering empty buildings that are useful to you. Believing men should lower their gaze and guard their private parts. Believing women should do the same. They should not show their beauty except what normally appears. They should cover their chests with their head covers, except before close family and those listed in the verse. All believers should turn to Allah in repentance. Help the unmarried to marry, because Allah can make the poor rich. Those who cannot marry should stay chaste. Slaves who seek freedom should be given a contract and some wealth, and no one should force them into sin.

Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light is like a lamp in a niche. The lamp is inside glass that shines like a bright star. It is lit from a blessed olive tree whose oil almost glows by itself. Light upon light! Allah guides to His light whom He wills. In mosques, men praise Him morning and evening. Trade does not distract them from prayer and zakah.
The deeds of disbelievers are like a mirage that a thirsty man thinks is water. Or they are like layers of darkness in a deep sea, under waves and clouds. Whoever Allah gives no light has no light.
Everything in the heavens and earth praises Allah, even birds in flight. Allah drives the clouds, sends rain and hail, and changes night and day. He created every living creature from water.

hardWords.m: the way you look at things
a small hollow space in a wall
something seen in the desert that looks like water but is not

167.title: Obeying Allah and His Messenger in Every Matter

paragraphs.text: Allah sent down clear verses, and He guides whom He wills. The hypocrites say they believe and obey, but then some of them turn away. When called to the Messenger for judgment, they refuse, unless the right is on their side. Is there a disease in their hearts? True believers say, "We hear and we obey." Those who obey Allah and His Messenger and fear Him are the successful.

The hypocrites swear strong oaths that they would go out if ordered. But true obedience is what matters. Obey Allah and the Messenger. His duty is only to deliver the message clearly. Allah promised the believers who do good that He would give them power in the land. He would make their religion firm and replace their fear with security, while they worship Him alone. So pray, give zakah and obey the Messenger.

Servants and young children should ask permission before entering at three private times. These are before dawn prayer, at noon rest, and after night prayer. When children grow up, they should always ask permission. Older women may put aside outer garments without showing beauty, but modesty is better. There is no blame on the blind, the lame, the sick, or anyone eating in relatives' or friends' houses. When you enter houses, greet one another with peace.
True believers do not leave a shared meeting with the Messenger without his permission.

hardWords.m: to bring and give to someone

168.title: The Criterion Sent Down and the Disbelievers' Objections

paragraphs.text: Do not call the Messenger the way you call one another. Allah knows those who slip away secretly. Those who go against his order should beware of trial or painful punishment. Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah. He knows your state and will tell people what they did.

Blessed is Allah, who sent down the Criterion to His Servant as a warner to the worlds. The heavens and earth are His. He has no son and no partner. He created everything and set its exact measure. Yet people worship gods who create nothing and were created themselves. They have no power over harm, benefit, death, life or resurrection.

The disbelievers say the Quran is a lie he made up with help from others. They call it old legends written down for him. But it was sent by the One who knows every secret of the heavens and the earth. They ask why this messenger eats food and walks in markets. Why was no angel or treasure sent to him? They say he is a man under magic. They have gone astray. If Allah wills, He can give him gardens and palaces.

They deny the Hour, so a Blaze is ready for them. They will hear its angry roar from far away. Chained in a narrow place, they will cry for destruction. Is that better, or the eternal Garden promised to the righteous?

hardWords.m: something that shows right from wrong
one who shares something with another
a large store of gold or wealth

169.title: Regret on Judgment Day and the Quran's Gradual Revelation

paragraphs.text: In the Garden, the righteous will have whatever they wish forever. This is a promise from their Lord. On the Day of gathering, Allah will ask the false gods, "Did you mislead My servants, or did they stray?" They will answer, "Glory be to You! We could not take allies besides You. You gave them comforts until they forgot the message." So the false gods will deny the disbelievers, and they will find no help.

Every messenger before the Prophet ate food and walked in markets. Allah made some people a test for others, to see who is patient. Those who do not expect to meet Allah ask why angels were not sent to them. They have become very proud. When they see the angels, there will be no good news for the criminals. Their deeds will become like scattered dust. The people of Paradise will have a better home and resting place.

On that Day, the sky will split open with clouds, and the angels will come down. True rule will belong to the Most Merciful. The wrongdoer will bite his hands in regret. He will say, "I wish I had followed the Messenger's way! I wish I had not taken that person as a friend. He led me away from the reminder."
The Messenger will say his people abandoned the Quran. Every prophet had enemies, but Allah is enough as a guide and helper. The Quran came in parts to strengthen the Prophet's heart.

hardWords.m: left alone and not cared for

170.title: Destroyed Nations, Desire as a God, and Allah's Signs

paragraphs.text: Whenever the disbelievers bring an argument, Allah gives the Prophet the truth and the best explanation. Those dragged on their faces to Hell are in the worst place and the farthest from the right way.

Allah gave Moses the Scripture and made his brother Aaron his helper. Those who denied His signs were completely destroyed. The people of Noah denied the messengers, so Allah drowned them and made them a sign for mankind. 'Aad, Thamud, the people of the well, and many generations between them were also destroyed. The disbelievers have passed by the town that received a rain of evil. Yet they do not expect to be raised again.

When they see the Prophet, they mock him. They say he almost turned them away from their gods. When they see the punishment, they will know who was truly lost. Have you seen the one who takes his own desire as his god? Most of them are like cattle, or even more lost.

Look at how your Lord stretches out the shadow. If He willed, He could make it stay still. He made the sun a guide for it, then He draws it back slowly. He made the night like a covering, sleep for rest, and the day for rising. He sends the winds as good news before His mercy. He sends pure water from the sky to bring dead land to life. It gives drink to animals and people.

hardWords.m: a dark shape made when something blocks light

171.title: The Two Seas and the Most Merciful's Servants

paragraphs.text: Allah spreads the rain among people so they may remember, but most refuse and only disbelieve. If He willed, He could have sent a warner to every city. So the Prophet should not obey the disbelievers, but strive against them with the Quran.

Allah let two seas flow side by side. One is fresh and sweet, and the other is salty and bitter. He placed a barrier between them. He created human beings from water and gave them family ties through birth and marriage. Yet people worship what can neither help nor harm them. The Prophet was sent only to give good news and to warn. He asks no payment, only that people take a way to their Lord. Trust in the Ever-Living, who never dies. Allah created the heavens and earth in six days, then rose above the Throne. When told to bow to the Most Merciful, the disbelievers ask, "Who is the Most Merciful?" This makes them turn away more. Allah placed great stars, a burning lamp and a shining moon in the sky. He made night and day follow each other for those who want to remember or be thankful.

The servants of the Most Merciful walk on the earth gently. When foolish people speak rudely to them, they reply with peace. They spend the night bowing and standing in prayer. They ask Allah to keep away the punishment of Hell. When they spend, they are neither wasteful nor stingy, but moderate.

hardWords.m: not wanting to spend or give
in the middle, not too much or too little

172.title: Repentance, Righteous Families, and Surah ash-Shu'ara Begins

paragraphs.text: The servants of the Most Merciful do not call on another deity with Allah. They do not kill a soul that Allah has made sacred, except by right, and they do not commit adultery. Whoever does these things will face a doubled punishment and stay in disgrace. But those who repent, believe and do good are different. Allah will change their bad deeds into good ones. Whoever repents and does good truly turns back to Allah.

These servants do not give false witness. When they pass by bad talk, they walk on with dignity. When reminded of Allah's verses, they do not act deaf and blind. They pray, "Our Lord, give us joy in our wives and children, and make us an example for the righteous." They will be given the high Chamber in Paradise for their patience. There they will be greeted with peace and stay forever. Allah would not care for people if not for their prayers. Those who deny will face the result.

Ta, Seen, Meem. These are the verses of the clear Book. The Prophet almost harmed himself with grief because the people would not believe. If Allah willed, He could send a sign that would force their heads to bow. But whenever a new reminder comes from the Most Merciful, they turn away. Soon the news of what they mocked will reach them. Have they not looked at the earth and the many fine plants Allah grows in it?
In the earth and its plants there is a sign, but most people do not believe. Your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.

Allah called Moses and told him to go to the wrongdoing people of Pharaoh. Would they not fear Allah? Moses said, "My Lord, I fear they will deny me." He said his chest would feel tight and his tongue would not be fluent, so he asked Allah to send Aaron too. He also feared they would kill him, because they held a crime against him. Allah said, "No! Go, both of you, with Our signs. We are with you, listening." They were to tell Pharaoh that they were messengers of the Lord of the worlds. They were to ask him to let the Children of Israel go with them.

Pharaoh reminded Moses that he grew up in Pharaoh's house as a child. He had lived among them for many years. Then he did that deed and was ungrateful. Moses replied that he did it when he was lost. Then he ran away out of fear. After that, his Lord gave him wisdom and made him a messenger. Moses asked if this was the favor Pharaoh spoke of, while Pharaoh had enslaved the Children of Israel. Pharaoh asked, "What is the Lord of the worlds?" Moses answered that He is the Lord of the heavens and earth and all between them, if only they would be sure.

hardWords.m: a kind act done for someone

174.title: Moses Shows Signs, and Pharaoh Calls the Magicians

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh turned to the people around him and said, "Do you not hear this?" Moses continued, "He is your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers." Pharaoh said, "Your messenger is mad!" Moses replied, "He is Lord of the east and the west and all between them, if you would only think." Pharaoh became angry. He threatened that if Moses took any god other than Pharaoh, he would put him in prison. Moses asked, "Even if I bring you a clear proof?" Pharaoh told him to bring it, if he was telling the truth.

Moses threw his staff, and at once it became a real serpent. Then he drew out his hand, and it was shining white for all who watched. Pharaoh told his chiefs that Moses was a skilled magician. He claimed Moses wanted to drive them out of their land with his magic. He asked them for advice. They told him to delay the matter of Moses and his brother. They said he should send men to the cities to gather every skilled magician.

So the magicians were brought together on a fixed, well-known day. The people were asked to gather too, so they could follow the magicians if they won. When the magicians came, they asked Pharaoh if they would get a reward if they were the winners.

hardWords.m: a place where people are locked up
a person who does magic tricks

175.title: The Magicians Believe and Moses Leaves at Night

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh promised the magicians a reward and said they would be close to him. Moses told them to throw whatever they would throw. They threw their ropes and staffs. They said, "By the might of Pharaoh, we will surely win." Then Moses threw his staff, and it swallowed up all their false tricks. At once the magicians fell down, bowing to Allah. They said, "We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron."

Pharaoh was furious. He said, "You believed in him before I gave you permission! He must be your leader who taught you magic. You will soon see. I will cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you all." The magicians were not afraid. They said, "There is no harm. We will return to our Lord. We hope our Lord will forgive our sins, because we were the first to believe."

Allah inspired Moses to travel by night with His servants, because they would be chased. Pharaoh sent men to the cities to gather his army. He told them that the believers were only a small group who made them angry. He said his people were careful and ready. So Allah removed Pharaoh's people from their gardens and springs, their treasures and their honored places.

hardWords.m: to kill by hanging on a wooden cross
places where water comes out of the ground

176.title: The Sea Parts, and Abraham Questions the Idols

paragraphs.text: Allah gave those gardens, springs and treasures to the Children of Israel as an inheritance. Pharaoh's army followed Moses and his people at sunrise. When the two groups saw each other, the companions of Moses were afraid. They said, "We will surely be caught!" But Moses was calm and sure. He said, "No! My Lord is with me, and He will guide me." Then Allah inspired Moses to strike the sea with his staff. The sea split apart, and each part stood like a huge, tall mountain. Allah brought the chasing army close. He saved Moses and everyone with him, all together. Then He drowned the others. In this there is a clear sign, but most of them did not believe. Your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.

The Prophet is told to recite the news of Abraham to the people. Abraham asked his father and his people, "What do you worship?" They answered, "We worship idols, and we stay devoted to them." Abraham asked them simple questions. Do these idols hear you when you call on them? Can they bring you any benefit, or can they cause you harm? The people had no real answer. They only said, "We found our fathers doing the same." So Abraham asked them to think carefully about what they had been worshipping all this time.

177.title: Abraham Describes His Lord and Prays for Mercy

paragraphs.text: Abraham told his people that the idols worshipped by them and their ancient forefathers were his enemies. He would have nothing to do with them. Only the Lord of the worlds was different. Abraham then described his Lord with love. He is the One who created him and guides him. He gives him food and drink. When he is sick, it is Allah who heals him. Allah will cause him to die and then bring him back to life. Abraham hoped that Allah would forgive his sins on the Day of Judgment.

Then Abraham made a beautiful prayer. He asked his Lord to give him wisdom and to join him with the righteous. He asked for an honored name among the people who would come after him. He asked to be one of those who inherit the Garden of Pleasure. He asked Allah to forgive his father, because his father had gone astray. He also asked not to be put to shame on the Day when all people are raised.

On that Day, wealth and children will not help anyone. Only a person who comes to Allah with a sound and pure heart will be saved. Paradise will be brought close to the righteous. Hellfire will be shown clearly to those who went astray. Then they will be asked, "Where are the things you used to worship?"

hardWords.m: a painful feeling after doing wrong

178.title: Regret in Hell and Noah's Message to His People

paragraphs.text: The people of Hell will be asked whether the things they worshipped besides Allah can help them now. Can they even help themselves? Then the false gods and those who went astray will be thrown into Hellfire. The soldiers of Iblees will be thrown in together with them. While arguing inside the Fire, the people will confess their mistake. They will say, "By Allah, we were clearly in error. We made you equal to the Lord of the worlds. Only the criminals led us astray." They will cry that now they have no one to speak for them. They also have no close friend to help them. They will wish they could go back to the world and become believers. In this there is a sign, but most of them did not believe. Your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.

The people of Noah also denied the messengers. Their brother Noah spoke to them kindly. He asked, "Will you not fear Allah?" He told them he was a trustworthy messenger sent to them. So they should fear Allah and obey him. He did not ask them for any payment for his message. His reward would come only from the Lord of the worlds.

hardWords.m: to admit that you did wrong

179.title: Noah Is Saved, and Hud Comes to 'Aad

paragraphs.text: Noah again told his people to fear Allah and obey him. But they said, "Should we believe you, when only the lowest people follow you?" Noah answered that he did not know what those followers used to do. Their account is only with his Lord, if the people could understand. He said he would never drive away the believers. He was only a clear warner. The people threatened him. They said, "If you do not stop, O Noah, you will surely be stoned."

Noah turned to his Lord. He said, "My Lord, my people have denied me. So judge between me and them with a final judgment. Save me and the believers who are with me." Allah answered his prayer. He saved Noah and those with him in the fully loaded ship. Then He drowned all the rest who remained behind. In this there is a sign, but most of them did not believe. Your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.

Then the people of 'Aad also denied the messengers. Their brother Hud came to them with the same message. He asked, "Will you not fear Allah?" He told them that he was a trustworthy messenger sent to them. So they should fear Allah and obey him.

hardWords.m: a record of deeds to be judged

180.title: Hud Warns 'Aad, and Salih Comes to Thamud

paragraphs.text: Hud told his people that he asked them for no payment. His reward would come only from the Lord of the worlds. Then he warned them about their behavior. They built a tall sign on every high place just to amuse themselves. They made palaces and strong fortresses, as if they would live forever. When they attacked others, they attacked like cruel tyrants. So Hud told them again to fear Allah and obey him. He reminded them to fear the One who gave them everything they knew. Allah gave them grazing animals and children, gardens and springs. Hud said he feared for them the punishment of a terrible day.

But the people did not listen. They said, "It is all the same to us whether you advise us or not. This is only the custom of the people before us. We will not be punished." So they denied Hud, and Allah destroyed them. In this there is a sign, but most of them did not believe. Your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.
Then the people of Thamud also denied the messengers. Their brother Salih came to them. He asked, "Will you not fear Allah?" He told them that he was a trustworthy messenger sent to them.

hardWords.m: to do something only for fun
an old way of doing things

181.title: The She-Camel Sign and a Proud People

paragraphs.text: The messenger told his people again to fear Allah and obey him. He made it clear that he wanted no payment from them, because his reward comes only from the Lord of the worlds. Then he asked them a question to make them think. Did they believe they would be left secure forever in what they had? They lived among gardens and springs, with fields of crops and palm trees whose fruit was soft and ripe. They also carved homes out of the mountains with great skill. Although they had all these blessings, they did not turn to their Lord. So he called them once more to fear Allah and follow him. He warned them not to obey the orders of the transgressors, who spread corruption in the land and never try to set things right.

The people did not accept his message. They said that he was only someone under the effect of magic. They also said he was just a man like them, so he should bring a sign if he was truly honest. He answered by showing them a she-camel. She would have her own time to drink, and they would have theirs, each on a known day. He warned them not to touch her with any harm, because then the punishment of a terrible day would take them. But they wounded her legs, and afterwards they became regretful. Then the punishment seized them. This story is a clear sign, although most of them were not believers. Truly, the Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
After this, a new story begins. The people of Lot also denied the messengers, which shows that they followed the same path as the nations who came before them.

hardWords.m: cut a shape out of something hard
people who go beyond the limits
feeling sorry for what you did

182.title: Lot Saved, and Shu'ayb Calls His People

paragraphs.text: Lot spoke to his people as their brother. He asked them why they did not fear Allah, and he told them that he was a trustworthy messenger sent to them. He called them to fear Allah and obey him. Like the messengers before him, he did not ask for any payment, because his reward comes only from the Lord of the worlds. Then he spoke against their sin. They went to men with desire and left the wives whom their Lord had created for them. He told them plainly that they were a people who had crossed the limits.

Instead of listening, the people threatened him. They said that if he did not stop, he would surely be thrown out of the town. Lot replied that he truly hated what they were doing. Then he turned to his Lord in prayer and asked Him to save him and his family from the result of their deeds. So Allah saved him and all his family, except an old woman who stayed behind with the others. Then Allah destroyed the rest of them. He sent down upon them a rain of stones, and terrible was the rain that fell on those who had been warned. In this story there is a sign, although most of them did not believe. Indeed, the Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

Next, the story moves to another nation. The companions of the thicket, which was a place of thick trees, also denied the messengers. Their messenger Shu'ayb came to them and asked them the same important question: "Will you not fear Allah?" He began his call in the same way as the messengers who came before him.

hardWords.m: a place with many trees and bushes close together

183.title: Fair Weights, the Black Cloud, and the Quran

paragraphs.text: Shu'ayb told his people that he was a trustworthy messenger, so they should fear Allah and obey him. He asked them for no payment, because his reward was only from the Lord of the worlds. Then he gave them clear commands about trade. They must give full measure and must not be among those who cause others loss. They must weigh things with a fair and even balance. They must not cheat people out of what belongs to them, and they must not spread corruption on the earth. He also reminded them to fear the One who created them and the generations who lived before them.

His people answered with the same words that earlier nations had used. They said he was only someone affected by magic and only a man like them. They even said they thought he was a liar. Then they challenged him to make pieces of the sky fall upon them, if he was telling the truth. Shu'ayb simply answered that his Lord knows best what they do. They kept denying him, so the punishment of the day of the black cloud seized them, which was the punishment of a terrible day. In this there is a sign, but most of them were not believers. And the Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

After these stories, the surah speaks about the Quran itself. It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit brought it down onto the heart of the Prophet Muhammad, so that he would be one of those who warn people. It came in a clear Arabic language, which makes its message plain and easy to follow for those who hear it.

hardWords.m: the amount of something you give or get
to be dishonest to get something
a message sent down from Allah

184.title: Proof of the Quran and a Sudden Punishment

paragraphs.text: The Quran is also mentioned in the scriptures of the peoples who came before. This should be a clear sign for the disbelievers, because the scholars of the Children of Israel recognize it. Allah then explains how stubborn the deniers are. Even if He had revealed it to a person who was not an Arab, and that person had recited it to them perfectly, they would still not have believed in it.

In this way, disbelief has been placed in the hearts of the criminals. They will not believe in the message until they see the painful punishment with their own eyes. It will come to them suddenly, while they do not expect it at all. Then they will ask whether they may be given a little more time. Yet, strangely, they are impatient for Allah's punishment now. Allah asks us to think about this: suppose He let them enjoy life for many years, and then the promised punishment came to them. All that enjoyment would not help them in any way, because what they were given cannot save them from what they were promised.

Allah never destroyed any city without first sending warners to it. These warnings were a reminder for the people, and Allah is never unjust to anyone. The surah then makes clear where the Quran came from. The devils did not bring this revelation down. It is not allowed for them, and they would not even be able to do it, since they have been kept far away from hearing it.

hardWords.m: to know something when you see it

185.title: Warn Your Family, and Rely on Allah

paragraphs.text: The Prophet is told not to call upon any other deity along with Allah, because then he would be among those who are punished. He is also told to warn his closest relatives. He should be gentle and humble toward the believers who follow him, which is described as lowering his wing for them. If they disobey him, he should say that he has nothing to do with what they are doing. He must place his trust in the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. Allah sees him when he stands up in prayer, and He sees his movements among those who bow down in prostration. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.

Next, the surah tells us upon whom the devils come down. They come down upon every sinful liar. These liars pass on things they have heard, and most of them do not tell the truth. The poets are also described here. Only people who have gone astray follow them. They wander in every valley, and they say things that they do not actually do. However, there is an exception. Some poets believe, do good deeds and remember Allah often, and they defend the Muslims after they have been wronged. As for the wrongdoers, they will soon know what kind of end they are going to.

A new surah begins with the letters Ta and Seen. These are the verses of the Quran and of a clear Book. It was sent as guidance and as good news for the believers, so that they may find the right way and feel hope.

hardWords.m: putting the forehead on the ground in prayer
something that is different from the rule

186.title: Moses at the Fire, Solomon and the Ant

paragraphs.text: The believers are those who establish prayer, give zakah and are certain about the Hereafter. But for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, Allah has made their own deeds seem pleasing to them, so they wander about blindly. They will have the worst punishment, and in the Hereafter they will be the biggest losers. The Prophet receives the Quran from One who is Wise and Knowing.

Moses once told his family that he had seen a fire, and he hoped to bring back news or a burning torch to warm them. When he reached it, a voice called out, blessing those at the fire and around it, and said, "It is I, Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise." He was told to throw down his staff, and when it moved like a snake, he ran away in fear. Allah told him not to be afraid, because messengers do not fear in His presence. Whoever does wrong and then replaces evil with good will find Him Forgiving and Merciful. Moses put his hand into his garment, and it came out white without any illness. These were among nine signs for Pharaoh and his people. Although they were sure inside that the signs were true, they rejected them out of pride and called them magic.

Allah gave knowledge to David and Solomon, and they praised Him for His favor. Solomon inherited from David and said that they had been taught the language of birds. His army of jinn, men and birds marched in rows. When they reached the valley of the ants, an ant warned the others to enter their homes so that Solomon's soldiers would not crush them unknowingly. Solomon smiled at her words and prayed to be grateful and to do good deeds which please his Lord.

hardWords.m: a stick with fire at one end

187.title: The Hoopoe, the Queen of Sheba, and a Letter

paragraphs.text: Solomon checked on the birds and noticed that the hoopoe was missing. He said he would punish the bird severely unless it brought a clear excuse. The hoopoe returned and said that it knew something Solomon did not know. It had come from Sheba with certain news. A woman was ruling the people there, and she had been given plenty of everything, including a great throne. However, she and her people were bowing down to the sun instead of Allah. Satan had made their deeds seem good to them and turned them away from the right path. They did not bow to Allah, who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and who knows what people hide and what they show. There is no deity except Him, Lord of the Great Throne.

Solomon said he would find out whether the hoopoe was telling the truth. He gave it a letter to deliver to them and told it to watch for their answer. The queen told her chiefs that a noble letter had reached her. It was from Solomon, and it began, "In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful." It told them not to be proud, but to come to him in submission.

The queen asked her chiefs for advice, because she did not decide any matter without them. They answered that they were strong and ready for war, although the final command was hers. She said that when kings enter a city, they ruin it and humble its honored people. So she decided to send a gift instead and wait for the reply. When her messengers arrived, Solomon said that what Allah had given him was better than their wealth, and that it was they who were delighted with their gift.

hardWords.m: a reason given for not doing something
the special chair of a king or queen
to take something to a person

188.title: The Queen's Throne and the Plot Against Salih

paragraphs.text: Solomon sent the messengers back and said he would come with soldiers whom they could never resist. Then he asked his assembly who could bring the queen's throne before her people arrived. A powerful jinn offered to bring it before Solomon rose from his seat. But a man with knowledge from the Scripture said he could bring it before Solomon's eye could blink. When Solomon saw it in front of him, he said this was a favor from his Lord to test whether he would be grateful. Whoever is grateful benefits himself, and his Lord is Free of need and Generous. He had the throne changed a little to test the queen, and she said it seemed to be hers. What she had worshipped besides Allah had kept her away, because she came from a disbelieving people. When she entered the palace, she thought its glass floor was water. Then she admitted that she had wronged herself, and she submitted with Solomon to Allah.

Allah sent Salih to Thamud, telling them to worship Allah, but they split into two quarrelling groups. He asked why they were rushing toward evil instead of seeking forgiveness. They called him a bad omen, but he replied that their omen was with Allah and that they were being tested. Nine leaders in the city made a secret oath to kill him and his family at night. They planned, and Allah also planned, while they did not realize it. So Allah destroyed them and their people, and their empty houses remain as a sign. He saved those who believed and feared Him.

hardWords.m: a group of people gathered together
a sign of good or bad luck

189.title: Is There Any Deity with Allah?

paragraphs.text: Lot spoke to his people about their shameful deeds, which they did openly. They approached men with desire instead of women, and he called them a people acting in ignorance. Their only answer was to say, "Drive Lot's family out of your city, because they keep themselves pure." So Allah saved him and his family, except his wife, who stayed behind. Then a rain of stones fell upon those who had been warned.

The Prophet is told to praise Allah and to send peace upon His chosen servants. Then come a series of strong questions. Who created the heavens and the earth and sent down rain to grow beautiful gardens, which people could never grow by themselves? Who made the earth steady, placed rivers and firm mountains in it, and set a barrier between the two seas? Who answers the desperate person when he calls, removes harm, and makes people inheritors of the earth? Who guides people through the darkness of land and sea, and sends the winds as good news before His mercy? Who begins creation, repeats it, and provides for everyone? After each question comes the same challenge: is there any deity with Allah? Those who say so are asked to bring their proof.

No one in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen except Allah, and people do not know when they will be raised up again. Their knowledge of the Hereafter has failed; they are in doubt and blind about it. The disbelievers ask whether they and their forefathers will really come out of the earth after becoming dust. They say these are only old stories. The Prophet is told to tell them to travel and see the end of the criminals, and not to grieve over their plots.

hardWords.m: something that keeps two things apart
what people cannot see or know

190.title: The Clear Truth and the Blowing of the Horn

paragraphs.text: The disbelievers ask when the promised punishment will come, if the Prophet is telling the truth. He is told to answer that some of what they are rushing for may already be close behind them. The Lord is full of kindness toward people, although most of them are not thankful. He knows what their hearts hide and what they show. Nothing is hidden anywhere in the heavens or the earth without being written in a clear record.

This Quran explains to the Children of Israel most of the matters in which they disagree. It is guidance and mercy for the believers. The Lord will judge between them with wisdom, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. So the Prophet should rely on Allah, because he stands on the clear truth. He cannot make the dead hear, nor can he make the deaf hear a call when they turn their backs. He cannot guide the blind out of their error. Only those who believe in the verses of Allah will truly listen and submit.

When the promised word comes true, Allah will bring out a creature from the earth that will speak to the people, because they were not certain about His verses. On that Day, a group from every nation who denied His signs will be gathered and driven in rows. Allah will ask them why they denied His signs without understanding them. Because of their wrongdoing, the judgement will fall on them, and they will not be able to speak. People should reflect on how Allah made the night for rest and the day for seeing. Then the Horn will be blown, and everyone in the heavens and the earth will be terrified, except those whom Allah wills, and all will come to Him humbled.

191.title: The Mountains Pass, and Baby Moses in the River

paragraphs.text: People see the mountains and think they are fixed, although one day they will pass away like clouds. This is the work of Allah, who made everything perfect, and He knows what people do. Whoever comes with a good deed will receive better than it and will be safe from the terror of that Day. But those who bring evil will be thrown face down into the Fire, and they will only be repaid for what they did. The Prophet says that he was commanded to worship the Lord of this sacred city, to be a Muslim and to recite the Quran. Whoever accepts guidance helps himself, and whoever goes astray should know that the Prophet is only a warner. Allah will show people His signs, and they will recognize them.

A new surah begins with the letters Ta, Seen, Meem. It tells the true story of Moses and Pharaoh for people who believe. Pharaoh raised himself high in the land and divided its people into groups. He oppressed one group, killing their newborn sons and keeping their females alive. Allah wanted to favor these oppressed people, to make them leaders and to settle them in the land.

Allah inspired the mother of Moses to nurse her baby and, if she feared for him, to place him in the river without grief, because He would return him to her. Pharaoh's family picked him up, although he would later become their enemy. Pharaoh's wife said he would be a comfort for them both and asked them not to kill him. His mother's heart became empty of everything else, and she almost revealed the secret, but Allah made her heart firm. She sent his sister to follow him secretly.

hardWords.m: put an idea into someone's heart
something that makes you feel happy and calm

192.title: Moses Returns to His Mother, Then Flees

paragraphs.text: Allah had already stopped Moses from feeding from any nurse. So his sister offered to show them a family who would take good care of him. In this way, Allah returned him to his mother so that she could be happy and know that His promise is true. When Moses grew up and became mature, Allah gave him wisdom and knowledge.

One day Moses entered the city and found two men fighting, one from his own people and one from his enemy. When his man called for help, Moses struck the other, and the man died, although Moses had not meant to kill him. He said this was the work of Satan, and he asked his Lord to forgive him, and Allah forgave him. He promised never to help criminals. The next day, the same man called for help again, and Moses told him that he was clearly a troublemaker. When Moses was about to strike their enemy, the man said Moses wanted to be a tyrant. Then someone ran to warn Moses that the chiefs were planning to kill him, so he left the city in fear, praying to be saved.

Moses travelled toward Madyan, hoping that Allah would guide him. At a well, he saw two women holding back their animals, waiting until the shepherds had finished, because their father was very old. He watered their flocks and then rested in the shade, telling his Lord that he needed any good He sent. Later, one of the women came shyly and invited him to meet her father, who comforted him. She advised her father to hire Moses, since he was strong and trustworthy. The father offered him a daughter in marriage if he worked eight years, or ten as a favor, and Moses agreed.

hardWords.m: fully grown in body and mind
to give someone a job for pay

193.title: Moses at the Mountain, Pharaoh's Proud Tower

paragraphs.text: After Moses finished his term of work, he travelled with his family and saw a fire near the mountain. He told them to wait while he brought news or a burning piece of wood to warm them. When he reached it, he was called from a tree in a blessed place: "O Moses, I am Allah, Lord of the worlds." He threw down his staff, and when it moved like a snake, he ran away. Allah told him to come back without fear, because he was safe. His hand came out white without disease, and these were two proofs for Pharaoh. Moses feared they would kill him, so he asked for his brother Aaron, who spoke more clearly, to support him. Allah promised to strengthen him through his brother and give them both power.

When Moses brought the clear signs, Pharaoh's people called them invented magic that their forefathers never knew. Moses replied that his Lord knows best who brings true guidance. Pharaoh told his chiefs that he knew of no deity for them except himself. He ordered Haman to build a tall tower so he could look for the One whom Moses worshipped, although he thought Moses was lying. Because Pharaoh and his soldiers were arrogant, Allah threw them into the sea, and a curse follows them.

Allah gave Moses the Scripture as light, guidance and mercy. The Prophet Muhammad was not present when Allah gave Moses the command, and he did not live among the people of Madyan. Yet this knowledge reached him because Allah sent it.

hardWords.m: thinking you are better than others

194.title: Those Who Believe, and Those Who Follow Desires

paragraphs.text: The Prophet was not at the side of the mountain when Allah called Moses. Instead, he was sent as a mercy from his Lord to warn a people who had received no warner before him. Otherwise, if a disaster struck them for their sins, they might complain that no messenger had come. But when the truth did come, they asked why he was not given signs like those of Moses. Yet they had already rejected Moses, calling both messages magic. The Prophet is told to challenge them to bring a scripture from Allah that guides better than both. If they do not respond, they are only following their desires, and no one is more lost than such a person.

Some of those who had received the Scripture before believe in the Quran. When it is recited to them, they say it is the truth from their Lord and that they had already submitted to Him. They will receive their reward twice, because they were patient, they push away evil with good, and they spend from what Allah has given them. When they hear foolish talk, they turn away calmly and say, "Peace be upon you." The Prophet cannot guide whomever he loves; only Allah guides whom He wills.

Some feared that following guidance would get them driven from their land. Yet Allah had given them a safe sanctuary, where fruits of every kind are brought as provision. Many cities proud of their easy lives were destroyed, leaving their homes empty. Allah never destroys cities until a messenger has recited His verses to them, and only when their people are wrongdoers. Everything in this world is temporary enjoyment, while what is with Allah is better and lasts longer. On the Day of Resurrection, He will ask where their false partners are.

hardWords.m: food and things needed for life

195.title: Night and Day as Mercy, and Qarun's Pride

paragraphs.text: On the Day of Judgement, the leaders who misled others will admit that they led them astray, just as they themselves had gone astray. They will declare to Allah that they are free from those followers. The people will be told to call their false partners, but no one will answer them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had followed guidance! When they are asked how they answered the messengers, they will be too confused to speak. But whoever repented, believed and did good deeds is promised a place among the successful.

Allah creates and chooses whatever He wills, and the choice does not belong to people. He knows what hearts hide and what they show. There is no deity except Him, all praise belongs to Him, and everyone will return to Him. Then He asks two powerful questions. If He made the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, who could bring light? And if He made the day continue without end, who could bring a night for rest? Out of His mercy, He made night for resting and day for seeking His bounty, so that people may be thankful. From every nation a witness will be brought, and the false beliefs they invented will disappear.

Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he treated them badly. Allah gave him so much treasure that even its keys were heavy for a group of strong men. His people told him not to be boastful, to seek the Hereafter with his wealth, to do good and not to spread corruption. But he claimed his wealth came from his own knowledge. When he appeared in his finery, some people wished for his fortune, but those with knowledge said that Allah's reward is better.

hardWords.m: to say something clearly and openly

196.title: The End of Qarun, and Faith Is Tested

paragraphs.text: Allah made the earth swallow Qarun and his home. No group could help him against Allah, and he could not defend himself. Those who had wished for his position the day before now said that Allah gives provision generously to whom He wills and limits it for others. They realized that if Allah had not been kind to them, He could have made the earth swallow them too. The home of the Hereafter is for those who do not seek to rise high on earth or to cause corruption. Whoever brings a good deed will receive better than it, while evil is repaid only by what was done.

The One who gave the Quran to the Prophet will bring him back to a place of return. The Prophet had not expected to receive the Book; it came as a mercy from his Lord. So he must never support the disbelievers or let them turn him away from Allah's verses. He should invite people to his Lord and never call upon another deity. Everything will perish except His Face.

A new surah opens with the letters Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think they will be left alone simply for saying "We believe," without being tested? Allah tested those who came before, and He will make clear who is truthful and who is lying. Those who do evil cannot escape Him. Whoever hopes to meet Allah should know that the appointed time is coming. Whoever strives, strives for his own good, because Allah does not need anyone. People are commanded to be good to their parents. However, if parents push them to worship others besides Allah, they must not obey them in that. Believers who do good will have their sins removed and will join the righteous.

197.title: Noah's Long Call and Abraham Against the Idols

paragraphs.text: Some people say they believe in Allah, but when they are harmed because of their faith, they treat the trouble caused by people as if it were Allah's punishment. Yet when victory comes, they say they were with the believers all along. Allah knows what is in every heart, and He will make the believers and the hypocrites clear. The disbelievers tell the believers to follow their way and promise to carry their sins for them. They are lying, because they will not carry any of those sins. Instead, they will carry their own heavy loads along with other loads, and they will be questioned about their lies.

Allah sent Noah to his people, and he stayed among them for nine hundred and fifty years. Then the flood took them while they were wrongdoers. Allah saved Noah and those on the ship, and He made it a sign for all people.

Abraham told his people to worship Allah and fear Him. He explained that their idols could not provide anything for them, so they should seek provision from Allah and be grateful. Many nations before them had also denied, and a messenger's duty is only to deliver the message clearly. People are invited to travel and see how Allah began creation, because bringing it back is easy for Him. No one can escape Allah, and those who deny His signs have lost hope of His mercy.

Abraham's people shouted that he should be killed or burned, but Allah saved him from the fire. Abraham told them that their love for idols would turn into cursing one another on the Day of Resurrection. Lot believed him, and Abraham decided to emigrate for the sake of his Lord.

hardWords.m: a lot of water covering the land
to leave your home to live in another place

198.title: Many Nations Destroyed, and the Spider's Weak Home

paragraphs.text: Allah gave Abraham Isaac and Jacob, and He placed prophethood and scripture among his descendants. Lot warned his people about a shameful sin that no one had done before. They also blocked the roads and did evil in their meetings, yet they dared him to bring Allah's punishment. When Allah's messengers came to Abraham with good news, they told him they would destroy Lot's city. Abraham reminded them that Lot lived there, and they replied that they would save Lot and his family, except his wife. When they reached Lot, he was upset and worried for them, but they comforted him and announced that punishment would fall from the sky. Its remains are a clear sign for people who think.

Shu'ayb told the people of Madyan to worship Allah, to expect the Last Day and to stop spreading corruption. They denied him, so an earthquake struck them and left them lying dead in their homes. Aad and Thamud were also destroyed, and their ruined homes can still be seen. Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman were arrogant, although Moses had brought them clear proofs. Each nation was punished for its sin, some by a storm of stones, some by a blast, some by being swallowed by the earth and some by drowning. Allah did not wrong them; they wronged themselves.
Those who take protectors other than Allah are like a spider that builds a home, and the spider's home is the weakest of all homes. Only people of knowledge truly understand such examples.

hardWords.m: a sudden shaking of the ground
a small creature with eight legs

199.title: Prayer, Patience, and Trust in Allah's Provision

paragraphs.text: Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth, and this is a sign for the believers. The Prophet is told to recite the Book and establish prayer, because prayer stops shameful deeds and wrongdoing, and remembering Allah is even greater. Believers should argue with the People of the Scripture only in the best way, except with those among them who do wrong. They should say that they believe in what was revealed to both groups, and that the One they all worship is the same, to whom they submit. Before the Quran, the Prophet did not read any book or write one with his hand. Otherwise, the liars would have had a reason to doubt. The Quran is preserved in the hearts of those given knowledge.

The disbelievers ask why signs are not sent to him. He is told to answer that signs are only with Allah, and he is only a clear warner. Is it not enough that the Book is recited to them? Allah is enough as a Witness. They ask him to hurry the punishment, and if a fixed time had not been set, it would already have come. It will come suddenly, covering them from above and below.

Allah tells His believing servants that His earth is wide, so they should worship only Him. Every soul will taste death and then return to Him. Those who believe and do good will live forever in high rooms in Paradise with rivers flowing beneath. This is the reward of those who are patient and rely on their Lord. Many creatures cannot carry their own food, yet Allah provides for them and for people.

hardWords.m: able to wait calmly without complaining

200.title: Who Sends the Rain? The Byzantines Will Win

paragraphs.text: If the disbelievers were asked who created the heavens and the earth and who controls the sun and the moon, they would surely answer, "Allah." So how are they turned away from the truth? Allah gives plenty of provision to whom He wills and gives less to others, and He knows all things. If they were asked who sends down rain and brings the dead earth back to life, they would again say, "Allah." Still, most of them do not think properly. This worldly life is only play and amusement, whereas the home of the Hereafter is the true life, if only they knew.

When people sail on a ship and fear danger, they call upon Allah with complete sincerity. But as soon as He brings them safely to land, they start associating others with Him again. Allah made Makkah a safe place, while people all around them are being seized, and yet they still believe in falsehood. No one is more unjust than a person who invents a lie about Allah. But those who strive for His sake will be guided to His ways, because Allah is with those who do good.

A new surah begins with the letters Alif, Lam, Meem. The Byzantines have been defeated in a nearby land, but after their defeat they will win again within three to nine years. All command belongs to Allah, before and after. On that day the believers will be happy with Allah's help, because He gives victory to whom He wills. This is Allah's promise, and He never breaks His promise.
Many people know only the outer side of worldly life, while they ignore the Hereafter. They should think deeply about themselves, since Allah created everything in truth and for a fixed time.

hardWords.m: being honest and pure in intention

201.title: Among His Signs: Dust, Mates, and Lightning

paragraphs.text: People are asked to travel through the earth and see what happened to earlier nations. Those nations were stronger, they farmed the land and built more than people do now, and messengers came to them with clear proofs. Allah did not wrong them; they wronged themselves. Because they denied His signs and mocked them, their end was the worst. Allah begins creation, repeats it, and everyone returns to Him. When the Hour comes, the criminals will lose all hope, and their false partners will not speak for them. On that Day people will be separated.
