Believers who did good will be delighted in a garden, while those who denied will be brought into punishment.

So Allah should be glorified in the evening and in the morning, at night and at noon, and all praise in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. He brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living, and He gives life to the earth after it has died. In the same way, people will be brought out of their graves.

The surah then lists some of His signs. He created people from dust, and then they spread across the earth. He created spouses for them from among themselves so they could find peace, and He placed love and mercy between them. The creation of the heavens and the earth and the variety of languages and colors are signs for those who know. Sleep at night and in the day, and seeking His bounty, are signs for those who listen. Lightning brings both fear and hope, and rain revives the land. The heavens and earth stand by His command, and when He calls, people will come out at once.

hardWords.m: laughed at in an unkind way

202.title: The Natural Faith, and Giving for Allah's Sake

paragraphs.text: Everyone in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, and all obey Him. He begins creation and then repeats it, which is even easier for Him. Allah gives an example from people's own lives. They would never accept their servants as equal partners in their wealth, so how can they make partners for Allah? Those who do wrong simply follow their desires without knowledge, and no one can guide those whom Allah lets go astray.

Believers are told to turn their faces sincerely toward the religion and hold on to the fitrah, which is the natural way upon which Allah created all people. His creation should not be changed, and this is the correct religion, although most people do not know it. They should turn back to Him, fear Him, establish prayer and not divide their religion into separate groups, each happy with what it has. When hardship touches people, they call on their Lord, but after He shows them mercy, some of them associate others with Him again. When good comes, they rejoice, but when trouble comes because of their own deeds, they quickly lose hope.

Allah gives more provision to some and less to others. So people should give relatives their rights, and also help the needy and the traveler, seeking the face of Allah. Money given on interest does not grow with Allah, but zakah given for His sake is multiplied. Allah created people, provides for them, will cause them to die and will bring them back to life. Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what people have done, so that they may taste some of its results and return to the right path.

hardWords.m: as Allah made it from the start
extra money charged on a loan

203.title: Winds, Rain, and the Stages of Life

paragraphs.text: People should turn to the correct religion before a Day comes from Allah that no one can push back. On that Day, people will be divided into groups. Whoever disbelieves will carry the result of his disbelief, and whoever does good is preparing a good place for himself. Allah will reward the believers out of His bounty, although He does not like the disbelievers. Among His signs are the winds that bring good news, so that ships may sail and people may seek His bounty. Messengers came to earlier nations with clear proofs, and Allah punished the criminals and helped the believers.

Allah sends the winds, which move the clouds and spread them across the sky. Then rain comes out of them, and people become joyful, although they had been without hope before it fell. People are asked to look at the effects of Allah's mercy, since He gives life to the dead earth, and in the same way He will give life to the dead. Yet if a harmful wind turned their crops yellow, they would become ungrateful. The Prophet cannot make the dead or the deaf hear. Allah created people weak, then gave them strength, and then made them weak again with white hair.

When the Hour comes, the criminals will swear that they stayed in the world only one hour. But people of knowledge and faith will tell them that they stayed as long as Allah decreed, until this Day of Resurrection. Excuses will not help the wrongdoers then. The Quran gives every kind of example, but disbelievers still call the believers liars, and in this way Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know.

hardWords.m: to promise strongly that something is true

paragraphs.text: The Prophet is told to be patient, because Allah's promise is true, and not to let people with weak faith shake him.

A new surah begins with the letters Alif, Lam, Meem. These are verses of the wise Book, sent as guidance and mercy for those who do good. They establish prayer, give zakah and are certain about the Hereafter, which is why they are rightly guided and successful. Some people buy entertaining talk to lead others away from Allah's path, and they make fun of it. When the verses are recited to such a person, he turns away proudly, as if his ears were deaf, so he will face a painful punishment. But those who believe and do good will live forever in the Gardens of Pleasure. Allah created the heavens without pillars that people can see and set firm mountains in the earth so that it would not shake. He spread every kind of creature on it and sent rain to grow fine plants. Those who worship others cannot show anything those others have created.

Allah gave Luqman wisdom and told him to be grateful. Luqman advised his son never to associate anything with Allah, since that is a great injustice. Allah commands people to care for their parents, especially the mother, who carried her child through weakness upon weakness and nursed him for two years. If parents push their child to worship others besides Allah, he must not obey them, but he should still treat them kindly in this world. Luqman added that even a wrong as small as a mustard seed, hidden in a rock or anywhere, will be brought out by Allah.

hardWords.m: fun to listen to or watch
tall, strong posts that hold something up
told someone what is best to do
a plant with very tiny seeds

205.title: Luqman's Wise Words and Allah's Endless Words

paragraphs.text: Luqman continued advising his son. He told him to establish prayer, to call to what is right, to forbid what is wrong, and to be patient with whatever trouble came to him, because these things need real determination. He warned him not to turn his face away from people in pride, and not to walk on the earth with arrogance, since Allah does not love anyone who is boastful. He also told him to walk at a moderate pace and to lower his voice, because the ugliest sound is the braying of donkeys.

Allah has placed everything in the heavens and the earth in people's service, and He has given them His favors fully, both seen and unseen. Still, some argue about Allah without knowledge or a clear Book. When they are told to follow what Allah has revealed, they say they will follow the ways of their fathers, even if Satan is calling them to the Blaze. Whoever submits to Allah while doing good has grabbed the firmest handhold. The Prophet should not be saddened by disbelievers, because they will return to Allah.

If asked who created the heavens and the earth, they would say "Allah." If all the trees on earth were pens and the sea were ink, plus seven more seas, the words of Allah would still not run out. Creating and raising all people again is as easy for Him as one soul. He makes night enter day and day enter night, and the sun and moon run for a fixed time. When huge waves cover people on ships, they call on Allah sincerely, but once safe, only some remain moderate in faith. So people should fear a Day when no parent can help a child, and they must not be deceived by the Deceiver.

hardWords.m: a strong will to keep going
not too much and not too little
something you hold on to for support
a colored liquid used for writing

206.title: Five Things Only Allah Knows, and Creation from Clay

paragraphs.text: Only Allah knows when the Hour will come. He sends down the rain, and He knows what is inside the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in which land it will die. Truly, Allah is Knowing and Aware of everything.

A new surah begins with the letters Alif, Lam, Meem. This Book, beyond doubt, comes from the Lord of the worlds. Some claim the Prophet invented it, but it is the truth from his Lord, so that he may warn a people who had no warner before him. Allah created the heavens and the earth and everything between them in six days, and then He rose above the Throne. People have no protector or intercessor besides Him. He arranges every matter from the heaven to the earth, and it rises to Him in a Day equal to a thousand years of our counting. He knows the unseen and the seen. He made everything He created excellent, and He began the creation of man from clay. Then He made his children from a weak liquid, shaped him, breathed life into him, and gave people hearing, sight and hearts, yet they are rarely grateful.

The disbelievers ask whether they will really be created again after disappearing into the earth. The angel of death will take their souls, and then they will return to their Lord. On that Day, the criminals will hang their heads and beg to be sent back so they can do good. They will be told to taste the punishment because they forgot this meeting. The true believers, however, fall down in prostration when reminded, praise their Lord without pride, leave their beds to pray in fear and hope, and spend from what He has given them.

hardWords.m: the part of a mother where a baby grows
one who speaks to help another
to ask again and again with great need

207.title: Hidden Joys, the Torah, and Trust in Allah

paragraphs.text: No soul knows what joy has been kept hidden for the believers as a reward for their deeds. A believer and a person who openly disobeys Allah are not equal. Those who believed and did good will stay in the Gardens of Refuge as a welcome for what they did. But the home of the disobedient is the Fire. Every time they try to come out, they will be pushed back and told to taste the punishment they used to deny. Allah will let them taste a smaller punishment in this life before the greater one, so that perhaps they will return to Him. No one is more unjust than one who turns away after being reminded of his Lord's verses.

Allah gave Moses the Scripture and made the Torah a guidance for the Children of Israel. From them He chose leaders who guided by His command, because they were patient and certain of His signs. On the Day of Resurrection, the Lord will judge between them in their disagreements. People should notice how many generations were destroyed before them, whose homes they walk among. Allah drives water to dry land and grows crops for people and their animals. The disbelievers ask when the final victory will come, but on that Day their late belief will not help them. So the Prophet should turn away and wait.

A new surah begins with a command to the Prophet to fear Allah and not obey the disbelievers and hypocrites. He must follow what is revealed to him and rely on Allah, who is enough as a Guardian. Allah has not given any man two hearts. Wives whom husbands declare unlawful do not become their mothers, and adopted sons do not become true sons, because these are only words spoken by mouths.

hardWords.m: people living at the same time in history
one who protects and takes care
taken into a family as one's own child

208.title: Armies Attack, and the Best Example

paragraphs.text: Adopted children should be called by their fathers' names, which is more just in Allah's sight. If their fathers are unknown, they are still brothers in religion. There is no blame for honest mistakes, only for what hearts intend. The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are like their mothers. Allah took a firm covenant from the prophets, including Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary, so that He may question the truthful about their truth.

The believers are reminded of Allah's favor when armies came to attack them. He sent a wind against the enemy and armies they could not see. The enemy came from above and below, eyes moved wildly in fear, and hearts seemed to reach the throats. At that time, the believers were tested and shaken severely. The hypocrites and those with sick hearts said that Allah and His Messenger had promised only illusions. Some told the people of Yathrib to go home, and others asked permission to leave, claiming their houses were unprotected, although they only wanted to run away. They had promised Allah never to flee, but running from death will not help them, since no one can protect them from Allah.

Allah knows those who hold others back from fighting. They are unwilling to help the believers, and when fear comes, their eyes roll like someone about to die. But once the danger passes, they attack the believers with sharp tongues. Their deeds have become worthless. Even after the enemy left, they wished they were far away in the desert. In the Messenger of Allah there is an excellent example for anyone who hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Him often.

hardWords.m: to plan or mean to do

209.title: True Believers, and the Prophet's Household

paragraphs.text: When the true believers saw the enemy armies, they said that this was what Allah and His Messenger had promised, and it only made their faith and acceptance stronger. Some of them kept their promise to Allah until death, while others are still waiting, and they never changed their commitment. Allah will reward the truthful, and He may punish the hypocrites or accept their repentance. He turned back the angry disbelievers without any gain and was enough for the believers in battle. He also brought down from their fortresses those People of the Scripture who had supported the enemy, and He gave the believers their land, homes and wealth.

The Prophet is told to give his wives a choice. If they wanted worldly life and its beauty, he would provide for them and release them kindly. But if they wanted Allah, His Messenger and the Hereafter, a great reward awaited them. Because their position is special, their punishment for a clear wrong would be doubled, and their reward for obedience would be given twice. They are told to speak in a proper way, to stay in their homes, to establish prayer and to obey Allah, who wants to purify the Prophet's household.

Allah has prepared forgiveness and a great reward for Muslim men and women who believe, obey, are truthful, patient, humble, charitable and fasting, who guard their chastity and remember Him often. When Allah and His Messenger decide a matter, believers have no other choice. The Prophet had told Zayd to keep his wife, while hiding something Allah would reveal. Later, Allah married her to the Prophet, so that believers would face no difficulty about the former wives of adopted sons.

hardWords.m: a promise to stay true to something
keeping oneself pure from wrong relations

210.title: The Last of the Prophets, a Shining Lamp

paragraphs.text: Allah praises those who deliver His messages and fear only Him. Muhammad is not the father of any of their men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the last of the prophets. Believers must remember Allah often and to glorify Him morning and evening. He sends His blessing upon them, and His angels pray for them, so that He may bring them out of darkness into light. Their greeting when they meet Him will be "Peace," and a noble reward is waiting for them. Allah sent the Prophet as a witness, a bringer of good news, a warner, one who invites people to Allah by His permission, and a lamp that gives light. He should neither obey nor harm the disbelievers and hypocrites, and should rely on Allah.

If believers marry women and divorce them before touching them, there is no waiting period, and the women should be given a gift and released kindly. The surah then lists the women who were made lawful for the Prophet, and some of these permissions were only for him. Allah gave him freedom in arranging time with his wives so that they would feel content and satisfied. After this, no more women were lawful for him.

Believers must not enter the Prophet's houses unless invited for a meal, and after eating they should leave without staying to chat, because this troubled the Prophet, although he was too shy to say so. They should ask his wives for things from behind a screen, which is purer for everyone's hearts. They must never harm the Messenger or marry his wives after him. Allah knows everything people show or hide. There is no blame on the women before their close family members, and they should fear Allah, who witnesses all things.

hardWords.m: something that covers or hides from view

211.title: Blessings on the Prophet, Regret, and the Trust

paragraphs.text: Allah blesses the Prophet, and His angels ask Him to do so. The believers are told to ask Allah to bless the Prophet and to grant him peace. Those who insult Allah and His Messenger are cursed in this world and in the Hereafter, and a humiliating punishment is ready for them. People who hurt believing men and women for something they did not do carry the weight of a lie and a clear sin.

The Prophet is told to ask his wives, his daughters and the believing women to draw part of their outer garments over themselves. This makes it easier for them to be known, so that they will not be harmed. If the hypocrites, the people with sick hearts and those who spread rumors in Madinah do not stop, they will not stay as neighbors for long. This has always been the way of Allah with earlier peoples, and His way never changes.

People ask about the Hour, but only Allah knows when it will come, although it may be near. The disbelievers will stay forever in a Blaze, without any protector or helper. When their faces are turned over in the Fire, they will wish that they had obeyed Allah and the Messenger. They will blame their masters and leaders, who led them away from the right path, and they will ask for double punishment for them.

The believers should not be like those who hurt Moses with their words, because Allah cleared him and he was honored. They must fear Allah and speak just words, so that He will correct their deeds and forgive their sins. Allah offered the Trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, but they were afraid and refused it. Man accepted it, although he was unjust and ignorant.

hardWords.m: making someone feel low and ashamed
stories that people pass around, often untrue
people who pretend to believe but do not
showed that someone did no wrong

212.title: Allah's Knowledge, David, Solomon, and Saba'

paragraphs.text: The Trust was given so that Allah would punish the hypocrites and those who join partners with Him, and so that He would accept the repentance of the believing men and women. Allah is always Forgiving and Merciful.

All praise belongs to Allah, who owns everything in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Wise, the Aware. He knows what goes into the earth and what comes out of it, and what comes down from the sky and what rises up to it. The disbelievers say that the Hour will never come, but it will surely come. Not even the weight of an atom is hidden from Allah, because everything is written in a clear record. He will reward those who believe and do good, while those who fight against His verses will have a painful punishment. The disbelievers mock the idea of a new creation after death, calling the Prophet a liar or a madman. Do they not look at the sky and the earth around them? Allah could make it swallow them.

Allah gave David a great favor: the mountains and the birds repeated praises with him, and iron became soft in his hands so that he could make coats of armor. Solomon was given control of the wind, a spring of melted copper, and jinn who worked for him by Allah's permission. They built high rooms, statues and huge bowls for him. When Solomon died, the jinn did not know it until a small creature ate his staff and he fell. This showed that they did not know the unseen.
The people of Saba' had two gardens as a sign, and were told to eat and be thankful. They turned away, so Allah sent a flood that left only bitter fruit and a few trees.

hardWords.m: turning back to Allah and being sorry for sins
metal clothing that protects in battle
a lot of water that covers the land

213.title: Saba' Scattered, False Partners, and Blame on Judgement Day

paragraphs.text: Allah punished the people of Saba' because they were ungrateful, and He punishes only those who are ungrateful. He had placed towns between them and the blessed cities so that they could travel safely by night or day. However, they asked for longer distances between their journeys and wronged themselves, so they became only stories and were scattered everywhere. Iblees found that his opinion about them was true, and they followed him, except a group of believers. He had no real power over them; it was only a test to show who believes in the Hereafter and who doubts it.

The Prophet is told to challenge the people to call on the false gods they worship besides Allah. These gods do not own even an atom's weight in the heavens or the earth, and they are not His partners or helpers. No one can speak for another before Allah unless He allows it. Allah is the One who provides from the sky and the earth. In the end, Allah will bring everyone together and judge between them with truth, because He is the Knowing Judge.

The Prophet was sent to all of mankind to give good news and to warn, although most people do not know this. The disbelievers ask when the promised Day will be, but it has a fixed time which no one can delay or bring forward. On that Day the weak followers will blame the arrogant leaders, saying, "Without you, we would have believed." The leaders will answer that the followers were criminals themselves. Then all of them will hide their regret, and chains will be put on the necks of the disbelievers.

hardWords.m: not thankful for what you were given
to ask someone to prove something
thinking you are better than others
feeling sad about something you did

214.title: Wealth Does Not Bring People Nearer to Allah

paragraphs.text: Every time Allah sent a warner to a town, its rich people rejected him. They said they had more wealth and children, so they would not be punished. The Prophet is told to answer that Allah gives plenty to whom He wills and gives less to whom He wills, but most people do not understand this. It is not money or children that bring people closer to Allah, but faith and good deeds. Those who believe and do good will receive a double reward and will live safely in high rooms of Paradise. Whatever a person spends for Allah, He will replace it, because He is the best of providers.

On the Day of Judgement, Allah will gather everyone and ask the angels whether these people used to worship them. The angels will declare that Allah is far above that, and that He is their protector. They will say that the people actually worshipped the jinn. On that Day no one will be able to help or harm another, and the wrongdoers will taste the Fire they used to deny.

When the clear verses were recited to the disbelievers, they said that the Prophet only wanted to turn them away from their fathers' religion. They called the message a lie and obvious magic, although they had never been given any book before. Earlier nations, who were much stronger, also denied the messengers and were punished. The Prophet invites them to stand for Allah, alone or in pairs, and think carefully, because their companion is not mad. He asks for no payment, since his reward comes only from Allah. The truth has come, and falsehood can do nothing. If he is guided, it is through what his Lord reveals to him.

hardWords.m: those who give what others need
to say something clearly and openly

hardWords.bn: তিলাওয়াত করা হলো / পাঠ করা হলো

215.title: Allah Opens Mercy and Sends Life to the Earth

paragraphs.text: If you could see the disbelievers when they are terrified on that Day, you would see that they have no escape. They will suddenly say that they believe, but it will be too late, because they rejected the truth before and spoke about the unseen without knowledge. A barrier will be placed between them and what they wish for, just as happened with people like them in the past.

All praise belongs to Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, who made angels as messengers with two, three or four wings. When Allah opens His mercy to people, no one can stop it, and when He holds it back, no one can release it. People are reminded of His favors, because there is no other creator who provides for them. If the Prophet is denied, earlier messengers were denied too. The promise of Allah is true, so people should not be fooled by worldly life or by the Deceiver. Satan is an enemy, so he must be treated as an enemy. He only calls his followers to the Fire.

Allah sends the winds, which move the clouds, and He brings dead land back to life with rain; this is how the dead will be raised. All honor belongs to Allah, and good words rise up to Him. He created people from dust, then from a drop, and made them in pairs. No woman becomes pregnant or gives birth without His knowledge, and every lifespan is written in a record. From both fresh and salty water people eat tender meat and take ornaments, and ships sail through them. Allah makes the night enter the day and controls the sun and moon, while false gods own nothing, not even the thin skin of a date seed.

hardWords.m: carrying a baby inside the body
pretty things worn to look nice

216.title: People Need Allah; the Blind and Seeing Differ

paragraphs.text: The false gods that people call upon cannot hear their prayers, and even if they heard, they could not answer. On the Day of Resurrection, they will deny that anyone worshipped them. All people need Allah, while Allah needs no one and is worthy of all praise. If He wished, He could remove them and bring a new creation, and that would not be hard for Him. No soul will carry the burden of another, even if a close relative asks for help. A warning only helps those who fear their Lord unseen and keep up prayer. Whoever purifies himself does so for his own good.

The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are darkness and light, nor shade and heat. The living and the dead are not the same either. Allah makes whom He wills hear, but the Prophet cannot make those in the graves hear him. He is only a warner, sent with the truth to bring good news. Every nation has had a warner. Earlier peoples also denied their messengers, who came with clear proofs and a Scripture that gave light, so Allah seized those who disbelieved.

Allah sends rain from the sky and brings out fruits of many colors. The mountains have paths of white and red in different shades, and some are very black. People, animals and cattle also come in various colors. Among His servants, only those who have knowledge truly fear Allah. Those who recite His Book, pray and spend secretly and openly can hope for a trade that will never fail. Allah will give them their full reward and more, because He is Forgiving and Appreciative.

hardWords.m: different light and dark forms of a color
showing thanks for what is done

217.title: Three Kinds of Inheritors and Allah's Unchanging Way

paragraphs.text: The Book revealed to the Prophet is the truth and confirms the books that came before it. Allah gave this Book to the servants He chose. Some of them wrong themselves, some are in the middle, and some race ahead in good deeds by Allah's permission, which is a great bounty. They will enter gardens forever, wearing gold bracelets, pearls and silk. They will praise Allah for removing their sadness and for settling them in a lasting home, where they feel no tiredness.

The disbelievers will be in the fire of Hell, where they will neither die nor have their pain made lighter. They will cry out, asking to be taken out so that they can do good. They will be reminded that they had a long enough life to remember, and a warner had come to them. Allah knows the unseen and what is inside hearts. He made people successors on the earth, and disbelief only increases its people in loss.

The Prophet asks the disbelievers to show what their false partners have created. They have no proof; they only promise each other lies. Allah holds the heavens and the earth so that they do not fall apart. The disbelievers swore that they would follow a warner better than any nation, but when one came, they only turned further away because of pride and evil plans. Yet evil plans only trap the people who make them. The way of Allah never changes. Earlier nations were stronger, and nothing can escape Allah. If He punished people at once for what they earn, no creature would be left on earth, but He delays them for a fixed time.
Surah Ya Seen begins with an oath by the wise Qur'an.

hardWords.m: people who come after others and take their place
made a strong promise by Allah's name
to catch so that one cannot escape

218.title: Ya Seen: A Warning and Messengers to a Town

paragraphs.text: The Prophet is truly one of the messengers, on a straight path. The Qur'an is sent down by the Mighty, the Merciful, so that he may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned and who are unaware. The word has come true for most of them, so they do not believe. It is as if chains were placed around their necks up to their chins, so their heads are forced up. A barrier is in front of them and behind them, and they are covered, so they cannot see. Whether they are warned or not, they will not believe. A warning only helps the one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful without seeing Him. Such a person should be given good news of forgiveness and a noble reward. Allah gives life to the dead and records everything people do and leave behind, which He has counted in a clear register.

The Prophet is told to give the example of a town to which messengers came. Allah sent two, and when the people denied them, He made them stronger with a third. The messengers said that they were sent to them. The people replied that they were only humans like them and were lying. The messengers answered that their Lord knows they are truthful, and that their only duty was to deliver the message clearly. The people said that the messengers brought bad luck, and they threatened to stone them if they did not stop. The messengers replied that their bad luck was with themselves, because they were a people who crossed limits. Then a man came running from the far end of the town and told his people to follow the messengers.

hardWords.m: the lowest part of the face, below the mouth
a book where things are written and kept
to bring or give to someone

219.title: The Believing Man and Signs in Creation

paragraphs.text: The man told his people to follow those who ask for no payment and who are rightly guided. He asked why he should not worship the One who created him, to whom they will all return. If the Most Merciful wanted to harm him, false gods could not help him or save him. To worship them would be a clear mistake. He declared that he believed in their Lord and asked them to listen. He was told to enter Paradise, and he wished that his people could know how his Lord had forgiven him and honored him.

After him, Allah did not need to send an army from the sky against his people. There was only one loud shout, and they were silent and finished. How sad it is for people who mock every messenger who comes to them. Do they not see how many generations before them were destroyed and will never come back? Yet all of them will be brought before Allah.

The dead earth is a sign for people, because Allah brings it to life and brings out grain from it to eat. He places gardens of palm trees and grapevines in it, and makes springs burst out, so that they may eat its fruit. Their own hands did not make this, so they should be grateful. Allah is far above any fault, the One who created all things in pairs: plants of the earth, people themselves, and things they do not know. The night is also a sign, because when Allah removes the daylight from it, they are left in darkness.

hardWords.m: given respect and a high place
groups of people living in the same time

220.title: Sun, Moon, the Ship, and the Horn

paragraphs.text: The sun moves on its course toward its resting point, as decided by the Mighty, the Knowing. Allah set phases for the moon until it becomes like an old, curved date stalk. The sun cannot catch the moon, and the night cannot overtake the day, because each one swims in its own orbit. Another sign is that Allah carried the forefathers of people in a loaded ship, and He made for them other things like it to ride. If He wished, He could drown them, and no one would answer their cry or save them, except as a mercy from Him and an enjoyment for a time.

When the disbelievers are told to be careful of what is in front of them and behind them so that they may receive mercy, they turn away. They turn away from every sign of their Lord. When they are asked to spend from what Allah has given them, they ask the believers why they should feed someone whom Allah could feed if He wished. They ask when the promise will come, but they are only waiting for one blast that will seize them while they are arguing. Then they will not be able to leave any instructions, and they will not return to their families.

The Horn will be blown, and at once people will rush from their graves to their Lord. They will cry, "Woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleeping place?" They will be told that this is what the Most Merciful promised, and that the messengers spoke the truth. It will be only one blast, and all of them will be brought before Allah. On that Day no soul will be treated unjustly, and each will be paid only for what it did.

hardWords.m: the changing shapes of the moon
to catch up with and pass
the path one thing follows around another
words telling someone what to do

221.title: Joy in Paradise and Witnesses Against the Criminals

paragraphs.text: On that Day, the people of Paradise will be busy with happy activities. They and their spouses will sit in the shade, leaning on decorated couches. They will have fruit and whatever they ask for. They will also be greeted with the word "Peace," which comes from a Merciful Lord.

Then the criminals will be told to stand apart from the others. Allah will remind them that He had commanded the children of Adam not to worship Satan, because he is their clear enemy, and to worship Allah alone, which is the straight path. Satan had already misled a great number of people, so why did they not use their minds? Now they will be shown the Hellfire that they were promised, and they will be told to burn in it today because they used to deny it.

On that Day, Allah will seal their mouths. Then their hands will speak to Him, and their feet will bear witness about what they used to do. If He wished, He could have wiped out their eyes, so that they would rush to find the path but could not see it. If He wished, He could have changed their shape and frozen them in their places, so they could neither go forward nor go back. Also, whoever is given a long life is turned back to weakness in his body. Will they not understand?

Allah did not teach the Prophet poetry, and poetry is not suitable for him. What he brings is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an, which is meant to warn those who are alive and to prove the word true against the disbelievers. Do they not see that Allah created grazing animals for them, which they now own?

hardWords.m: to tell what one has seen
words written in a special rhythm

222.title: Who Gives Life to Bones? Allah Says "Be"

paragraphs.text: Allah made the grazing animals easy to control, so people ride some of them and eat others. They also get other benefits and drinks from them, so they should be grateful. Yet some people take false gods besides Allah, hoping that these gods will help them. Those gods cannot help them at all, although their worshippers stand ready to serve them like soldiers. The Prophet should not let their words make him sad, because Allah knows what they hide and what they show.

Does man not think about how Allah created him from a small drop? Then suddenly he becomes an open opponent. He gives an example and forgets how he himself was created. He asks, "Who will give life to bones after they have rotted away?" The answer is that the One who made them the first time will bring them to life again, because He knows every kind of creation. He is the One who made fire for people from the green tree, and from it they light their fires. Surely the One who created the heavens and the earth is able to create people like them again. Yes, He is the Knowing Creator. When He wants something, He only says to it, "Be," and it is. So He is far above every fault, the One in whose hand is the control of all things, and to Him everyone will return.

A new surah begins with oaths by the angels who stand in rows, by those who drive the clouds, and by those who recite the message. The oath declares that Allah is One. He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, of everything between them, and of the places where the sun rises.

hardWords.m: someone who argues or fights against you
became old and broken into pieces
the power to rule or direct

223.title: Stars Guard the Heavens; the Day of Judgement Comes

paragraphs.text: Allah has made the nearest heaven beautiful with stars. They also protect it from every rebellious devil, so that the devils cannot listen to the high assembly of angels. The devils are driven away and hit from every side, and they will have a punishment that never ends. If one of them manages to steal a few words by theft, a bright burning flame, sharp and piercing, quickly chases him away.

The Prophet is told to ask the disbelievers whether they are harder to create than the other things Allah has made. Allah created humans from sticky clay. The Prophet is amazed, while they only make fun. When they are reminded, they do not take the lesson. When they see a sign, they laugh at it and call it clear magic. They ask in surprise whether they will really be raised again after they die and become dust and bones, and whether their forefathers will also be raised. The Prophet must answer, "Yes, and you will be humbled." On that Day, there will be only one single shout, and at once they will all be standing up and looking around.

Then they will cry, "Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense." They will be told, "This is the Day of Judgement which you used to deny." After that, the angels will be ordered to gather those who did wrong, together with others like them, and the things they used to worship.

hardWords.m: a group of beings gathered together
holding on to things, like glue

224.title: Leaders and Followers Blame Each Other

paragraphs.text: The wrongdoers and the things they worshipped instead of Allah will be led to the road of the Hellfire. Then the angels will be told to stop them, because they must be questioned. They will be asked why they do not help one another now. But on that Day, they will give up completely and will not be able to do anything.

They will turn to one another, blaming each other. The followers will say to their leaders, "You used to come to us from the right side." The leaders will answer that the followers themselves were never believers. They will add that they had no power over them, and that the followers were a people who crossed the limits. They will admit that the word of their Lord has come true for all of them, and that they will all taste the punishment. They will say, "We misled you because we ourselves were astray." So on that Day, all of them will share in the punishment together, the leaders and the followers. This is how Allah deals with the criminals.

When these people were told that there is no deity except Allah, they became proud and refused. They used to say, "Should we leave our gods because of a mad poet?" Rather, the Prophet came with the truth and confirmed the messengers who came before him. So the disbelievers will taste the painful punishment, and they will be paid back only for what they used to do in their lives.

hardWords.m: saying someone else caused the wrong
to say that something is true, often unwillingly
led someone in the wrong way

225.title: Joys of the Chosen and a Friend in Hell

paragraphs.text: The painful punishment described before is not for everyone. The chosen servants of Allah are kept apart from it. Instead, they will receive a provision which has already been decided for them, including many kinds of fruits, and they will be treated with honor. They will live in gardens of pleasure and sit on thrones, facing one another as friends. A cup filled from a flowing spring will be passed around among them. The drink will be white and delicious for everyone who tastes it. It will not cause any bad effect, and it will not make them lose their minds. With them will be women who lower their eyes and have large, beautiful eyes. They will be as pure as delicate eggs which are carefully protected.

While they enjoy this, the people of Paradise will turn to one another and ask each other about their lives. One of them will say that on earth he had a companion who used to question his faith. This companion would ask him whether he was really one of those who believed. He would also ask whether, after they died and became dust and bones, they would truly be brought back and paid back for their deeds. The speaker will then ask the others whether they would like to look down. When he looks, he will see his old companion in the middle of the Hellfire. Then he will call out to him, "By Allah, you almost destroyed me."

hardWords.m: food and other things that are given
a friend who stays with you

226.title: The Great Success and the Tree of Zaqqum

paragraphs.text: The believer in Paradise will continue speaking to his old companion in the Fire. He will say that if it had not been for the favor of his Lord, he too would have been among those brought into Hell. Then he will ask his friends in Paradise with joy whether it is true that they will never die again, except for the first death they already tasted, and that they will never be punished. He will declare that this is truly the great success. For something like this, all those who work should work hard.

Then a question is asked: is Paradise a better place to stay, or the tree of zaqqum? Allah has made this tree a torment for the wrongdoers. It is a tree which comes out from the very bottom of the Hellfire. Its fruit looks like the heads of devils. The people of the Fire will eat from it until their stomachs are full. After that, they will be given a mixture of boiling water to drink on top of it. Then their return will be to the Hellfire once again.

These people found their fathers going the wrong way, and they hurried to follow in the same footsteps. Before them, most of the earlier peoples had also gone astray in the same manner. Allah had already sent warners among those peoples to call them back to the truth. So look at what happened in the end to the people who were warned but did not listen.

hardWords.m: getting what is good and hoped for
the parts of the body where food goes
the steps or path that someone walked

227.title: Peace upon Noah; Abraham Questions His People

paragraphs.text: The earlier peoples who were warned came to a bad end, but this was not the case for the chosen servants of Allah. They are named again as an exception, just as they were named before.

Noah once called out to Allah for help, and Allah is the best of those who answer. He saved Noah and his family from the great distress that came upon them. He made Noah's descendants the ones who remained on the earth after that, and He left for him a good name among the later generations. Then come the words, "Peace upon Noah among the worlds." Allah says that this is how He rewards those who do good, because Noah was one of His believing servants. After saving Noah and his family, Allah drowned the others, the people who had disbelieved.

Abraham was among those who were of the same kind as Noah. He came to his Lord with a sound heart. He asked his father and his people, "What do you worship?" He asked them whether they really wanted false gods other than Allah, which were only a lie. Then he asked them, "What do you think about the Lord of the worlds?" After that, Abraham took a look at the stars and said that he was about to become ill. So his people turned away from him and left, departing from him, while he stayed behind. What he did after they left is told in the next verses.

hardWords.m: someone or something not included in a rule
children, grandchildren and those after them

228.title: Abraham Breaks the Idols; His Son's Great Test

paragraphs.text: Abraham went to his people's idols and said to them, "Do you not eat? Why do you not speak?" Then he turned on them and struck them hard with his right hand. His people came rushing toward him. He asked them, "Do you worship what you carve with your own hands, while Allah created you and what you make?" They said, "Build a furnace for him and throw him into the burning fire." They made a plan against him, but Allah made them the lowest and the losers.

Then Abraham said that he would go to where his Lord ordered him, and that his Lord would guide him. He prayed, "My Lord, give me a child from among the righteous." So Allah gave him good news of a gentle and patient boy.

When the boy was old enough to work and walk with his father, Abraham said to him, "O my son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice you, so tell me what you think." The son answered, "O my father, do what you are commanded. If Allah wills, you will find me among the patient." When both of them had submitted to Allah's command, and Abraham had laid his son down on his forehead, Allah called to him, "O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision." This is how Allah rewards those who do good. This was truly a clear test, and Allah saved the son by giving a great sacrifice in his place.

hardWords.m: to cut wood or stone into a shape
to give up something precious for Allah

229.title: Peace upon Abraham, Moses, and Aaron; Elias Calls

paragraphs.text: After Abraham's great test, Allah left a good name for him among the later generations. Then come the words, "Peace upon Abraham." Allah says once more that this is how He rewards those who do good, because Abraham was one of His believing servants. Allah also gave Abraham good news of another son, Isaac, who would be a prophet from among the righteous. He blessed both Abraham and Isaac. However, their descendants are not all the same. Among them there are people who do good, and there are also others who are clearly unjust to themselves.

Allah also gave His favor to Moses and to his brother Aaron. He saved both of them and their people from the great distress that they faced. He supported them, so they were the ones who overcame their enemies in the end. He gave them the clear Scripture, which explained things plainly, and He guided them on the straight path. Then He left a good name for them among the later generations, and the words come, "Peace upon Moses and Aaron." Again Allah says that this is how He rewards those who do good, because both of them were among His believing servants.

Next comes Elias, who was also one of the messengers sent by Allah. He spoke to his people and asked them, "Will you not fear Allah?" With this question he called them to be mindful of their Lord. What he said to them after that is told in the following verses.

hardWords.m: won against a problem or enemy
in a clear and simple way

230.title: Elias, Lot, and Jonah Among the Messengers

paragraphs.text: Elias asked his people, "Do you call upon Ba'l and leave the best of creators?" He reminded them that Allah is their Lord and also the Lord of their earliest forefathers. But his people denied him, so they will be brought for punishment, except the chosen servants of Allah, who are kept safe from it. Allah left a good name for Elias among the later generations, and the words come, "Peace upon Elias." Allah says again that this is how He rewards those who do good, because Elias was one of His believing servants.

Lot was also one of the messengers. The listeners are told to remember when Allah saved him and all of his family, except his wife, who was among those who stayed behind. Then Allah destroyed the others. The listeners are reminded that they themselves pass by those destroyed people in the morning and at night as they travel. So the question is asked: will they not use their reason and think about it?

Jonah was also one of the messengers. The listeners are told to remember when he ran away to a ship which was fully loaded. On board, he drew lots with the others, and he was among the losers. Then the fish swallowed him, and at that time he was blameworthy for what he had done. What happened to him inside the fish, and after that, is told in the next verses.

hardWords.m: family members who lived long ago
took into the mouth and down the throat

231.title: Jonah Is Saved; False Claims About Allah

paragraphs.text: If Jonah had not been one of those who glorify Allah, he would have stayed inside the belly of the fish until the Day of Resurrection. But Allah threw him out onto an open shore while he was ill. Then He caused a gourd vine to grow over him. After that, Allah sent him to a people of a hundred thousand or more. Those people believed, so Allah allowed them to enjoy their lives for a time.

The Prophet is told to ask the disbelievers a question: does Allah have daughters, while they themselves have sons? Did Allah create the angels as females while they were there as witnesses to see it? It is only out of their own lies that they say Allah has a child, and they are clearly liars. Why would He choose daughters over sons? What is wrong with them, and how do they judge in this way? Will they not think and be reminded? Or do they have some clear authority for what they say? If they do, they should bring out their scripture, if they are really telling the truth.

They have also claimed a family relation, or lineage, between Allah and the jinn, which they invented. But the jinn already know that those who say such things will be brought for punishment. Allah is exalted, far above everything that they describe about Him.

hardWords.m: the land at the edge of the sea
a plant with a large, hard fruit
to say what something is like

232.title: The Angels' Ranks and Victory for the Messengers

paragraphs.text: The chosen servants of Allah do not share in the false sayings of the disbelievers. The disbelievers are told that neither they nor the things they worship can tempt anyone away from Allah. They can only lead away the one who is already going to enter and burn in the Hellfire.

Then the angels speak about themselves. They say that there is not one of them who does not have a known place and position. They line up in rows for prayer, and they are the ones who constantly glorify and exalt Allah.

The disbelievers used to say that if they had received a reminder like the one given to the earlier peoples, they would surely have been the chosen servants of Allah. However, when the message did come to them, they refused to believe in it. So they are going to know. They will soon learn the truth of what they rejected.

Allah's word was already given long ago to His servants, the messengers. He promised that they would be helped to victory, and that His soldiers would be the ones who overcome. So the Prophet is told to turn away from the disbelievers for a while. He should watch them, and soon they will see for themselves what happens to them. Then a question is asked: are they really impatient for Allah's punishment?

hardWords.m: to try to make someone do wrong

233.title: Peace on the Messengers; Pride of the Disbelievers

paragraphs.text: When the punishment comes down into the territory of the disbelievers, the morning of those who were warned will be very bad. So the Prophet is told again to leave them for a while and watch, for they will see. Your Lord, the Lord of might, is exalted above what they say about Him. Peace be upon the messengers, and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Surah Sad begins with an oath by the Qur'an, which contains a reminder. Yet the disbelievers are full of pride and are against the truth. Allah destroyed many generations before them, and those people cried out for help, but it was no longer a time to escape. The disbelievers are surprised that a warner has come from among themselves, and they call him a magician and a liar. They ask in amazement whether he has turned all their gods into only one, calling this a very strange thing. Their leaders went out telling the people to continue and to stay patient in defending their gods, saying that this was something intended. They said they had never heard of this in the latest religion and that it was only a made-up story. They asked why the message had been sent down to him alone out of all of them. In truth, they are in doubt about Allah's message, because they have not yet tasted His punishment.

Do they own the treasures of the mercy of the Lord, the Mighty, the Giver? Or do they rule the heavens, the earth and what is between them? If so, they should climb up by any way they can. In fact, they are only an army that will be defeated there, among the other groups who opposed the truth.

hardWords.m: the land that belongs to a people
great wealth that is kept safe

234.title: Earlier Nations Denied; David Judges Between Two Men

paragraphs.text: Before these disbelievers, many peoples denied their messengers: the people of Noah, the tribe of 'Aad, Pharaoh who owned the stakes, the tribe of Thamud, the people of Lot and the companions of the thicket. Because they all denied the messengers, Allah's punishment came upon them justly. The present disbelievers are only waiting for one blast, which will not be delayed. Yet they mockingly ask their Lord to hurry their share before the Day of Account.

The Prophet is told to be patient with what they say and to remember Allah's servant David. He was strong, and he always turned back to Allah. The mountains praised Allah with him in the afternoon and after sunrise, and the birds gathered and repeated praises with him. Allah made his kingdom strong and gave him wisdom and clear judgement in speech.

Two men in a dispute climbed into David's prayer room and frightened him, then asked him to judge fairly. One said that his brother had ninety-nine sheep while he had only one, yet his brother demanded that one too and beat him in argument. David said that the brother had wronged him, and that many partners treat each other unfairly, except the few believers who do good. David then understood that Allah had tested him, so he asked forgiveness, bowed down and repented. Allah forgave him and gave him nearness and a good return. He made David a successor on earth, to judge with truth and not follow desire.

Allah did not create the heavens and the earth without purpose. Only the disbelievers think so, and woe to them because of the Fire. Those who believe and do good will never be treated like those who spread corruption, and the righteous will not be treated like the wicked.

hardWords.m: a place thick with trees and bushes
in a fair and right way
felt sorry and turned back to Allah

paragraphs.text: The Qur'an is a blessed Book sent down to the Prophet so that people may reflect upon its verses, and so that those with understanding may take a reminder.

Allah gave Solomon to David. He was an excellent servant who always turned back to Allah. One afternoon, fine racehorses standing ready were shown to him. He said that he had loved good things more than the remembrance of his Lord, until the sun was hidden. He asked for the horses to be brought back, and he began to strike their legs and necks. Allah tested Solomon and placed a body on his throne, and then Solomon turned back. He prayed, "My Lord, forgive me and give me a kingdom that no one after me will have, because You are the Giver." So Allah made the wind obey him, blowing gently wherever he wished. Also, devils of the jinn served him, some as builders and some as divers, while others were tied in chains. Allah told him that this was His gift, which he could give or keep without account. He was granted nearness to Allah and a good place of return.

The Prophet is also told to remember Job, who called to his Lord that Satan had touched him with hardship and pain. He was told to strike the ground with his foot, and there was cool water for bathing and drinking. Allah gave his family back to him, with as many more, as a mercy and a reminder. Job was told to take a bunch of grass and strike with it, so that he would not break his oath. Allah found him patient, an excellent servant who always turned back to Him. Finally, the Prophet is told to remember Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, who had strength and vision.

hardWords.m: those who go deep under water
a very hard and painful time

236.title: Chosen Servants, a Good Return, and an Evil One

paragraphs.text: Allah chose Abraham, Isaac and Jacob for a special quality: they always remembered the home of the Hereafter. They are among the chosen and the best. The Prophet is also told to remember Ishmael, Elisha and Dhul-Kifl, who are all among the best.

This is a reminder. For the righteous there is a good place of return: gardens that last forever, with their doors open for them. They will lean back inside them and ask for plenty of fruit and drink. With them will be women who lower their eyes and are of the same age. This is what the righteous are promised for the Day of Account. It is Allah's provision, and it will never run out.

But for those who cross the limits there is an evil place of return. It is Hell, where they will burn, and it is a miserable place to rest. They will taste boiling water and foul pus, and other punishments of the same kind. When a new group of followers rushes into the Fire, the leaders will say, "There is no welcome for them, because they will burn in the Fire." The followers will reply, "No, there is no welcome for you! You brought this upon us, and what a terrible place to stay it is." They will pray, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, give him double punishment in the Fire." Then they will ask each other, "Why do we not see the men whom we used to count among the worst people?"

hardWords.m: a good thing that is part of someone
a large amount; more than enough
a kind greeting for someone who arrives

237.title: The Creation of Adam and Iblees's Pride

paragraphs.text: The people of the Fire will wonder whether they were wrong to mock those men, or whether their eyes simply cannot find them. This arguing among the people of the Fire is true, and it will surely happen.

The Prophet is told to say that he is only a warner. There is no deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing, the Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything between them, the Mighty, the One who forgives again and again. This message is great news, yet people turn away from it. The Prophet had no knowledge of the high assembly of angels when they were disputing. It is only revealed to him that he is a clear warner.

When Allah told the angels that He was going to create a human being from clay, He commanded them to bow down to him in prostration after He had shaped him and breathed into him a soul. So all the angels bowed down together, except Iblees. He was arrogant and became one of the disbelievers. Allah asked him what had stopped him from bowing down to what He had created with His hands, and whether he had become proud or was already among the haughty. Iblees answered, "I am better than him. You created me from fire, and You created him from clay." Allah said, "Then get out of Paradise, because you are cast out. My curse is upon you until the Day of Recompense." Iblees asked his Lord to give him more time until the Day when people are raised from the dead.

hardWords.m: the One who has power over everything
putting the forehead on the ground in worship
very proud and looking down on others
being sent away from Allah's mercy

238.title: Iblees Is Given Time; Worship Allah Sincerely

paragraphs.text: Allah gave Iblees time until a well-known Day. Iblees swore by Allah's might that he would mislead all people, except Allah's chosen servants. Allah declared that He would surely fill Hell with Iblees and all those who follow him. The Prophet is told to say that he asks for no payment and does not pretend to be what he is not. The Qur'an is only a reminder to the worlds, and people will know its truth after a time.

Surah Az-Zumar begins by saying that the Qur'an is sent down from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. The Book was revealed with truth, so the Prophet should worship Allah sincerely. Pure religion belongs to Allah alone. Some take protectors besides Him, saying they worship them only to come closer to Allah. Allah will judge between them in what they disagree about, and He does not guide a lying disbeliever. If Allah had wanted a son, He could have chosen from His creation, but He is far above that, the One, the Prevailing.

He created the heavens and the earth with truth. He wraps the night over the day and the day over the night, and the sun and moon run for a fixed time. He created people from one soul and made its mate from it, and He gave them eight mates of cattle. He forms people in their mothers' wombs, stage after stage, within three darknesses. If people disbelieve, Allah does not need them, yet He does not approve of disbelief, while He approves of gratitude. No one will carry another's burden. When trouble touches a person, he calls on his Lord, but when he is given a favor, he forgets and sets up equals to Allah. Such a person is told to enjoy his disbelief for a little while.

hardWords.m: truly and honestly, from the heart
to act as if something false is true
the place inside a mother where a baby grows

239.title: Those Who Know and the Best Speech

paragraphs.text: Is a person who stays obedient during the night, bowing and standing in prayer, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for his Lord's mercy, the same as one who does not? Are those who know equal to those who do not know? Only people of understanding take the reminder. The believers are told to fear their Lord. Those who do good in this world will have good, the earth of Allah is wide, and the patient will be given their reward without measure.

The Prophet is told to say that he was commanded to worship Allah sincerely and to be the first of the Muslims. He fears the punishment of a great Day if he disobeys his Lord. He worships Allah alone, while the others may worship what they like. The real losers are those who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Layers of fire will be above them and below them, and with this Allah warns His servants.

Those who avoid Taghut and turn back to Allah have good news. They listen to speech and follow the best of it; Allah has guided them. No one can save a person who deserves punishment. But those who fear their Lord will have high rooms built above one another, with rivers flowing beneath.

Allah sends rain, makes it flow as springs, and brings out crops of different colors, which later turn yellow and become broken pieces. A heart which Allah has opened to Islam is upon light, but woe to hard hearts. Allah sent down the best speech, a consistent Book. The skin of those who fear Him shivers, then softens at His remembrance. Earlier peoples denied, and punishment came from where they did not expect.

hardWords.m: the same throughout, with no conflict
shakes because of fear or cold

240.title: Allah Is Sufficient; He Takes the Souls

paragraphs.text: Allah made the earlier deniers taste disgrace in this life, but the punishment of the Hereafter is greater. The Qur'an gives every kind of example so that people may remember. It is an Arabic Qur'an with nothing crooked in it, so that people may fear Allah. One example is a slave owned by partners who quarrel with each other, compared with a slave who belongs to one man only. Are they equal? Praise be to Allah, but most people do not know. The Prophet will die, and they will die too, and they will argue before their Lord on the Day of Resurrection.

No one is more unjust than a person who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him; Hell is a home for the disbelievers. But the one who brought the truth and those who believed in it are the righteous. They will have whatever they wish with their Lord, and Allah will remove their worst deeds and reward them for their best.

Is Allah not sufficient for His Servant? No one can guide those whom Allah leaves astray, and no one can mislead those whom He guides. If the disbelievers are asked who created the heavens and the earth, they will say, "Allah." Yet the false gods they call on cannot remove any harm He sends or hold back His mercy. So the Prophet says that Allah is enough for him, and those who trust should trust Him. A disgracing and lasting punishment will come to some. Whoever is guided benefits himself, and the Prophet is not responsible for them.
Allah takes souls at death and during sleep, keeping some and returning others for a fixed time.

hardWords.m: having the duty to look after something

241.title: Do Not Despair of Allah's Mercy

paragraphs.text: Some people have taken intercessors other than Allah, even though those helpers own nothing and cannot even think. The Prophet is told to say that all intercession belongs to Allah alone, because the kingdom of the heavens and the earth is His, and everyone will be brought back to Him. When Allah is mentioned alone, the hearts of those who reject the Hereafter shrink with dislike, yet they become cheerful as soon as the others they worship are named. The believer is taught to call on Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, who knows both the hidden and the seen, and who will judge between His servants in their disagreements.

On the Day of Resurrection, the wrongdoers would gladly offer everything on earth, and twice as much, as a ransom to save themselves from the terrible punishment. Their bad deeds will become clear. They will be surrounded by the very thing they used to mock. When hardship touches a person, he cries out to Allah; however, when Allah grants him a blessing, he claims that he earned it through his own knowledge. In truth, it is a test, although most people do not realize it. Earlier peoples said the same, and it did not help them. Allah gives plenty of provision to whom He wills and limits it for others, and in this there are signs for believers.

Allah calls to His servants who have wronged themselves through sin and tells them never to lose hope in His mercy, because He forgives all sins and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. They are urged to turn back to their Lord, submit to Him and follow the best of what was revealed before the punishment suddenly arrives. Otherwise a soul may cry out in deep regret for neglecting its duty to Allah and for mocking the truth. Another may blame its lack of guidance or wish for one more chance. But Allah replies that His verses did come to them, and they denied them with arrogance.

hardWords.m: asking for help or pardon on behalf of someone else
a price paid to set someone free
a time of trouble or pain
a sad feeling about something you did or did not do
not taking care of something you should do
the feeling of being better than others

242.title: The Horn, the Judgement, and Two Groups

paragraphs.text: On the Day of Resurrection, those who told lies about Allah will be seen with darkened faces, and Hell is a fitting home for the arrogant. Allah will rescue those who feared Him; no harm or sorrow will touch them. Allah is the Creator of everything and the One who manages all affairs. The keys of the heavens and the earth belong to Him, while those who reject His verses are the real losers. The Prophet is told to ask the ignorant whether they order him to worship other than Allah. It was already revealed to him, and to the prophets before him, that if anyone associates partners with Allah, all his deeds become worthless. Therefore, he must worship Allah alone and be among the grateful.

People have not valued Allah as He truly deserves. On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth will be in His grip, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. The Horn will be blown, and everyone in the heavens and on earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills. When it is blown a second time, they will suddenly stand up, looking around. The earth will shine with the light of its Lord, the record of deeds will be set out, and the prophets and witnesses will be brought forward. Every soul will be judged fairly and paid in full for what it did. The disbelievers will be driven to Hell in groups, and its keepers will ask whether messengers had not warned them. They will admit it. Those who feared their Lord will be led to Paradise in groups, and its keepers will greet them with peace. They will praise Allah, who kept His promise and let them settle wherever they wish. The angels will surround the Throne, glorifying their Lord, and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
A new surah begins with the letters Ha, Meem, and it declares that this Book is sent down from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.

hardWords.m: joins others with someone as equals or partners
a tight hold in the hand
people who saw something and tell about it
praising someone as great and perfect

243.title: The Angels Pray for the Believers

paragraphs.text: Allah forgives sin and accepts repentance, yet He is severe in punishment and owns great bounty. There is no deity except Him, and to Him everyone will return. Only disbelievers argue against Allah's signs, so their free movement in the land should not fool anyone. The people of Noah and later groups also denied. Every nation planned to seize its messenger and argued with falsehood to defeat the truth, but Allah seized them instead, and His penalty was terrible. So Allah's word came true: the disbelievers will be companions of the Fire.

The angels who carry the Throne, and those around it, glorify their Lord and pray for the believers, saying that His mercy and knowledge cover everything. They ask Him to forgive those who repent and follow His way, to protect them from Hellfire, and to admit them into everlasting gardens together with their righteous fathers, spouses and children. Being protected from evil that Day is mercy and the great success.

The disbelievers will be told that Allah's hatred for them was even greater than their own hatred of themselves, because they refused faith when invited. They will confess that Allah made them lifeless twice and gave them life twice, and they will ask for a way out. But they had disbelieved whenever Allah alone was called upon, and believed when partners were added. Judgement belongs to Allah, the Most High.

Allah shows His signs and sends provision from the sky, yet only those who turn to Him take heed. So the believers should call on Allah sincerely, even though the disbelievers dislike it. Raised above all ranks, He sends revelation to whom He wills to warn of the Day of Meeting. Then nothing will be hidden from Allah, and all kingship will be His, the One, the Prevailing. Every soul will be repaid fairly, for Allah is quick in account. On that approaching Day, hearts will rise to the throats in terror, and the wrongdoers will have no friend or intercessor. Allah knows the tricks of the eyes and the secrets of the heart.

hardWords.m: something that is not true; lies
to say openly that you did wrong

244.title: A Believing Man in Pharaoh's Family

paragraphs.text: Allah judges with truth, while the things people call on besides Him cannot judge at all; He is the Hearing, the Seeing. Have people not travelled through the land and seen what happened to those before them? Those earlier nations were stronger and left greater marks on the earth, but Allah seized them for their sins, and nobody could protect them. This was because they rejected the clear proofs of their messengers.

Allah sent Moses with His signs and clear authority to Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun, but they called him a magician and a liar. When he brought the truth, they ordered the believers' sons killed and their women kept alive, but their plan only failed. Pharaoh even announced that he would kill Moses, claiming he feared Moses would change the people's religion or spread corruption. Moses answered that he sought refuge in his Lord from every arrogant person who does not believe in the Day of Account.

Then a believing man from Pharaoh's own family, who had kept his faith secret, spoke up. He asked why they would kill a man simply for saying, 'My Lord is Allah,' after he brought clear proofs. If Moses were lying, the lie would harm only him; but if he were truthful, some of the promised punishment would strike them. Their power in the land, he said, would not protect them from Allah. Pharaoh, however, insisted that he was guiding them to the right way. He feared for them a fate like that of the people of Noah, 'Aad and Thamud, and warned of the Day of Calling, when they would flee with no protector.

Joseph had come before with clear proofs, but they stayed in doubt, and after his death they claimed Allah would never send another messenger. Those who argue about Allah's signs without any authority are hated by Allah and the believers, and Allah seals the heart of every arrogant tyrant. Yet Pharaoh asked Haman to build a tower to reach the ways of the heavens.

hardWords.m: the right or power to do something; strong proof
bad and harmful behavior that spoils things
said something strongly and would not change

245.title: The Believer's Advice and Pharaoh's End

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh hoped to look at the deity of Moses, though he called Moses a liar. In this way, his evil deeds were made to look attractive to him, he was turned away from the right path, and his plan led only to ruin.

The believing man asked his people to follow him to the right way. Worldly life, he explained, is a brief enjoyment, but the Hereafter is the lasting home. An evil deed is repaid only with its equal, but any believer, male or female, who does good will enter Paradise and receive provision without limit. He asked why he was calling them to salvation while they were calling him to the Fire. They wanted him to disbelieve and to worship partners he knew nothing about, whereas he was inviting them to the Exalted in Might, the Forgiver. What they called to could not answer prayers in this world or the next. Finally, he said they would remember his words, and he trusted his affair entirely to Allah, who sees His servants.

So Allah protected him from their evil plots, while the people of Pharaoh were surrounded by the worst punishment. They are shown the Fire morning and evening, and when the Hour comes they will enter the severest punishment. In the Fire, the weak will beg their arrogant leaders, whom they followed, to take away part of their suffering. The leaders will reply that all are in it, for Allah has judged. They will even beg the keepers of Hell to ask Allah to lighten the punishment for one day. The keepers will ask whether messengers had come with clear proofs, when they admit it, they will be told to pray themselves, though such prayers are useless.

Allah promises to support His messengers and the believers in this life and on the Day when witnesses stand. On that Day, excuses will not help the wrongdoers; they will have the curse and the worst home. Earlier, Allah had given Moses guidance and made the Children of Israel inherit the Scripture.

hardWords.m: being saved from harm or punishment
to make less heavy or less hard

246.title: Call Upon Me, I Will Respond

paragraphs.text: The Scripture given to Moses was guidance and a reminder for people of understanding. The Prophet is told to be patient, because Allah's promise is true, to ask forgiveness for his sin, and to praise his Lord evening and morning. Those who argue about Allah's signs without any proof have only pride in their hearts, a greatness they will never reach, so he should seek refuge in Allah, the Hearing, the Seeing. Creating the heavens and the earth is greater than creating people, though most do not know it. The blind and the seeing are not equal, and neither are believers who do good and evildoers. The Hour is certainly coming, yet most people do not believe. Allah says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you," while those too proud to worship Him will enter Hell in disgrace.

Allah made the night for rest and the day for seeing, and He is generous to people, although most are not grateful. He is the Creator of everything, with no deity except Him, so how can people be turned away? He made the earth a place to live and the sky a ceiling, shaped human beings in the best form, and provided them with good things. He is the Ever-Living, so people should call on Him with pure faith and give all praise to Him, Lord of the worlds.

The Prophet is told to announce that he has been forbidden to worship anything besides Allah, and that he is commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds. Allah created people from dust, then from a drop of fluid, then from a clinging clot. He brings them out as children, lets them grow to full strength, and then to old age, although some die earlier. All reach a fixed term so that they may think. He gives life and causes death, and when He decides a matter, He only says "Be," and it is. How strange are those who argue about His signs and deny the Book; soon they will know.

hardWords.m: a feeling that you are more important than others
great shame and loss of respect
giving a lot, more than needed
the top cover of a room

247.title: Chains for the Proud, Signs in Animals

paragraphs.text: The disbelievers will have collars and chains around their necks, and they will be dragged through boiling water and then burned in the Fire. They will be asked where the partners they worshipped are. They will answer that those partners have disappeared, and they will even claim that they never called on anything before. In this way Allah leaves the disbelievers astray. They will be told that this is because they used to rejoice on earth without right and behave proudly, so they must enter the gates of Hell to stay forever, a terrible home for the arrogant.

Once again, the Prophet is told to be patient, since Allah's promise is true. Whether Allah shows him part of what was promised to them or takes his soul first, they will all return to Allah. Many messengers were sent before him; Allah has told him the stories of some, but not of others. No messenger could bring a sign without Allah's permission, and when Allah's command comes, the matter will be decided in truth, and those who follow falsehood will lose.
