Allah made grazing animals for people, so that they can ride some of them and eat others. These animals bring other benefits as well, and they help people reach what they need, just as ships carry them across the sea. Allah keeps showing His signs, so which of them can anyone deny?

Earlier nations were more numerous and stronger, and they left deeper marks on the land, yet their achievements did not help them. When their messengers came with clear proofs, they were pleased with their own knowledge, and the very thing they mocked surrounded them. When they finally saw Allah's punishment, they declared belief in Allah alone and rejected their partners. However, faith at that moment did not benefit them. This has always been Allah's way with His servants, and the disbelievers were the losers.
A new surah then begins with Ha, Meem, a revelation from the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

hardWords.m: pulled along the ground by force
things a person has gained by hard work

248.title: Creation in Six Days and Two Warnings

paragraphs.text: This Book has verses explained in detail, an Arabic Qur'an for people who know. It brings good news and warning, but most people turn away and do not listen. They say their hearts are covered, their ears are deaf, and a barrier stands between them and the Prophet, so each side should do its own work. The Prophet is told to reply that he is only a man like them, but it has been revealed to him that they have only one deity. So they should go straight to Him and ask His forgiveness. Woe to those who associate others with Allah, who do not give zakah and deny the Hereafter. But those who believe and do good will have a reward that never ends.

How can people disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days and still set up equals with Him? He placed firm mountains on the earth, blessed it, and measured out its food in four days. Then He turned to the sky, which was smoke, and commanded the sky and the earth to come willingly or unwillingly, and they replied that they came willingly. He completed seven heavens in two days, gave each its command, and decorated the nearest heaven with lamps for beauty and protection.

If people turn away, the Prophet should warn them of a thunderbolt like the one that struck 'Aad and Thamud. Messengers came to them, calling them to worship Allah alone, but they said Allah would have sent angels instead. 'Aad acted proudly and asked who was stronger than they, forgetting that their Creator was far stronger. So Allah sent a screaming wind against them during unlucky days, and they tasted disgrace in this life, while the punishment of the Hereafter is even more shameful. Thamud were guided, but they preferred blindness to guidance, so a humiliating thunderbolt seized them. Allah saved those who believed and feared Him. One Day the enemies of Allah will be gathered to the Fire in rows.

hardWords.m: something that blocks the way between two things
a flash of lightning with loud thunder

249.title: Skins Will Speak; Repel Evil with Good

paragraphs.text: When they reach the Fire, their own hearing, eyes and skins will testify against them about what they did. They will ask their skins why they spoke against them, and their skins will answer that Allah, who makes everything speak, gave them speech. Allah created them the first time, and to Him they return. They never hid themselves from their own bodies, because they assumed Allah did not know much of what they did. That wrong belief about their Lord ruined them and made them losers. Whether they are patient or ask to be excused, the Fire will be their home. Allah gave them companions who made their sins look attractive, so the word came true against them, as it did against earlier nations of jinn and men.

The disbelievers tell one another not to listen to the Qur'an and to make noise while it is recited, hoping to win. But Allah will make them taste severe punishment and repay them for their worst deeds. The Fire will be their eternal home, because they rejected His verses. In the Fire they will ask Allah to show them the jinn and men who misled them, so that they can trample them underfoot.

Those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then stay firm on the right path will receive angels who tell them not to fear or grieve, and who bring them good news of the promised Paradise. The angels say they are their allies in this world and in the Hereafter. There they will have whatever their souls desire, as a welcome from the Forgiving, the Merciful.

No one speaks better than a person who invites others to Allah, does good, and says he is one of the Muslims. A good deed and a bad deed are not equal, so evil should be pushed back with what is better; then an enemy may become like a close friend. Only patient people, who have a great share of good, are given this. If Satan whispers an evil suggestion, one should seek refuge in Allah, the Hearing, the Knowing.

hardWords.m: to tell what you know as a witness
to step heavily on something and crush it
an idea put into someone's mind

250.title: Signs in the Sky, Earth and Self

paragraphs.text: Among Allah's signs are night and day, the sun and the moon. People must not bow down to the sun or the moon, but to Allah who created them. Even if some are too proud, those near Allah glorify Him night and day without getting tired. Another sign is the dry, still earth that stirs and grows when rain falls. The One who revives it will revive the dead. Those who twist His verses are not hidden from Him. Is a person thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes safely on the Day of Resurrection?

The Qur'an is a mighty Book, untouched by falsehood, sent down by the Wise, the Praiseworthy. The Prophet hears only what earlier messengers heard, and his Lord both forgives and punishes. Had the Qur'an been in a foreign language, the people would have complained that its verses were unclear. For believers it is guidance and healing, but for unbelievers it is like deafness and blindness. Moses also received a Scripture, and people disagreed about it. Whoever does good helps himself, and whoever does evil harms himself, for Allah is never unjust.

Only Allah knows when the Hour will come. No fruit comes out of its cover, and no female becomes pregnant or gives birth, without His knowledge. When He asks where His so-called partners are, no one will bear witness to them. Those they used to call on will vanish, and they will know there is no escape.

A person never tires of asking for good things, but when harm touches him he loses all hope. When Allah gives him mercy after hardship, he says he deserves it, doubts that the Hour will come. Yet Allah will inform the disbelievers of their deeds and make them taste a heavy punishment. When blessed, a person turns away proudly; when troubled, he prays at length. Allah will show His signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear that the Qur'an is the truth, and Allah is Witness over everything.

hardWords.m: to change the meaning in a wrong way
carrying a baby inside the body
the far lines where the sky meets the earth

251.title: One Religion Given to All the Prophets

paragraphs.text: The disbelievers doubt they will meet their Lord, yet Allah encompasses all things.

A new surah opens with Ha, Meem, Ayn, Seen, Qaf. In the same way, Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, has sent revelation to the Prophet and to those before him. Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him, the Most High, the Most Great. The heavens almost break apart from above, while the angels glorify their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on earth, for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Allah watches over those who take other protectors, and the Prophet is not responsible for them.

Allah revealed an Arabic Qur'an to warn Makkah, the Mother of Cities, and those around it about the Day of Assembly, when one group will be in Paradise and another in the Blaze. If Allah had willed, He could have made all people one nation, but He admits whom He wills into His mercy, while the wrongdoers have no protector. Allah alone is the Protector who gives life to the dead. Whenever people disagree, the final judgement belongs to Him, and the Prophet relies on Him. He created the heavens and earth and made mates for people and cattle; nothing is like Him. He holds the keys of the heavens and the earth and gives provision as He wills.

Allah set for the believers the same religion He gave to Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus: to establish the religion and not split into groups. This call is hard for those who associate partners with Allah. People became divided only after knowledge came to them, out of jealousy among themselves; if not for Allah's earlier word delaying judgement, the matter would have been settled. The Prophet is told to keep inviting, to stay on the right course, and not to follow their desires. He should declare his belief in Allah's revelation, his duty to be just, and that each side has its own deeds, with no need to argue. Those who argue about Allah after His call is answered have an empty argument and face severe punishment.

hardWords.m: having the duty to take care of something
an unhappy feeling when others have something you want

252.title: The Harvest of This World and the Next

paragraphs.text: Allah sent down the Book in truth together with the balance, and perhaps the Hour is near. Those who do not believe in it want it to come quickly, but the believers are afraid of it because they know it is true, and those who dispute about it are far astray. Allah is gentle with His servants and gives provision to whom He wills. Whoever wants the harvest of the Hereafter will receive more, while whoever wants only the harvest of this world will be given some of it but will have no share in the Hereafter. Some people follow a religion that Allah never approved, and they will face painful punishment. The wrongdoers will fear what they earned, while the righteous will enjoy green gardens with whatever they wish near their Lord.

This is the good news Allah gives to believers who do good. The Prophet asks no payment for his message, only good will because of family ties. Whoever does a good deed receives even more good, because Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative. Some accuse him of inventing lies about Allah, but Allah could seal his heart if He willed, and He wipes out falsehood and confirms the truth. He accepts repentance, pardons bad deeds, answers the prayers of believers and gives them more from His bounty.

If Allah gave His servants too much provision, they would act unjustly on earth, so He sends down what He wills in measure. He sends rain after people lose hope, spreading His mercy. The heavens, the earth and the creatures scattered through them are His signs, and He can gather them whenever He wills. Whatever disaster strikes people is because of what their own hands earned, yet He forgives much. Nobody can escape Allah or find another helper. The ships on the sea, standing like mountains, are also His signs; if He willed, He could still the wind and leave them motionless. In this there are signs for everyone who is patient and grateful.

hardWords.m: the crop that is gathered; the result of work
agreed that something is good or allowed

253.title: Qualities of Believers and Patient Forgiveness

paragraphs.text: Allah could also destroy the ships because of what people earned, but He forgives much, and those who argue about His signs will learn that they cannot escape. Whatever people are given here is only enjoyment of worldly life, while what is with Allah is better and lasts longer for believers who rely on their Lord. These believers avoid major sins and shameful deeds, and they forgive when they are angry. They answer their Lord, keep up prayer, decide their affairs by consulting one another, and spend from what Allah gave them. When they are treated unjustly, they defend themselves.

The payment for a harmful act is a harm equal to it, but whoever pardons and makes peace will receive his reward from Allah, who does not like wrongdoers. A person who defends himself after being wronged is not to blame. Blame falls only on those who oppress people and act unjustly on earth, and they will have a painful punishment. Still, being patient and forgiving is one of the matters that need great determination.

Whoever Allah leaves astray has no protector. Seeing the punishment, the wrongdoers will ask for a way back. They will be brought before the Fire, bowed down in shame and looking with secret glances. The believers will say that the real losers are those who lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. They will remain in lasting punishment without allies. People should answer their Lord before a Day comes that cannot be turned back, when there will be no shelter and no denial. If they turn away, the Prophet is not their guardian; his only duty is to deliver the message. A person rejoices when Allah lets him taste mercy, but when evil strikes him because of his own deeds, he becomes ungrateful.

The kingdom of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, and He creates what He wills. He gives daughters to some, sons to others, or both sons and daughters, and He leaves some without children, for He is Knowing and Competent.

hardWords.m: to treat people cruelly and unfairly
to bring or pass something on

254.title: Revelation, the Clear Book, and Riding Animals

paragraphs.text: Allah does not speak to any human being except through revelation, from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger who reveals by His permission what He wills; He is Most High and Wise. In this way, Allah revealed to the Prophet an inspiration by His command. Before it, he did not know what the Book or faith was, but Allah made it a light to guide whom He wills, and the Prophet guides to a straight path: the path of Allah, who owns everything in the heavens and the earth. All matters return to Him.

A new surah begins with Ha, Meem, and an oath by the clear Book. Allah made it an Arabic Qur'an so that people might understand, and in the Mother of the Book it is high and full of wisdom. Should Allah stop sending the reminder just because people go beyond limits? Many prophets were sent to earlier peoples, but every one of them was mocked. Allah destroyed nations far more powerful than these, and the example of the earlier peoples has already passed.

If they are asked who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. He made the earth a resting place and laid out roads on it so people can find their way. He sends rain from the sky in measured amounts and brings dead land back to life; in the same way, people will be brought forth. He created all the kinds of creatures, and He made ships and animals for people to ride. When they sit on them, they should remember their Lord's favor and say: Exalted is He who made this serve us, because we could not have controlled it ourselves, and to our Lord we will surely return. Yet people have given Him a share from among His own servants, and humans are clearly ungrateful.

hardWords.m: a cloth or screen that covers or hides
a serious promise or swearing by something
lines or rules that should not be crossed
carefully set to the right amount

255.title: Following Fathers Blindly, and Abraham's Lasting Word

paragraphs.text: The disbelievers claim that Allah has daughters while they keep sons for themselves. Yet when one of them hears news of the birth of a girl, the very thing he attributes to the Most Merciful, his face darkens and he hides his grief. They give Him one who is raised among ornaments and is unclear in argument. They also call the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their claim will be written down, and they will be questioned about it. They even say that if the Most Merciful had willed, they would not have worshipped these beings, but they have no knowledge and are only guessing.

Allah asks whether He gave them a book before the Qur'an that they hold on to. In fact, their only argument is that they found their fathers following a religion and are walking in their footsteps. The same was said by the wealthy people of every town to which a warner was sent. When each warner offered better guidance than their fathers' ways, they rejected it, so Allah punished them. See how the deniers ended!

Abraham told his father and his people that he had nothing to do with what they worshipped, except the One who created him, who would guide him. He left this as a lasting word among his descendants so that they might return to it.

Allah let these people and their fathers enjoy life until the truth and a clear Messenger came to them. But when the truth arrived, they called it magic and rejected it. They asked why the Qur'an was not sent to some great man from one of the two cities. Do they divide the mercy of the Lord? It is Allah who divides their living in this world and raises some above others in rank, so that they may employ one another. Still, the mercy of the Lord is better than all the wealth they gather.

hardWords.m: saying something without knowing it is true
the marks or path left by someone walking

256.title: Silver Houses, Evil Companions, and Moses' Signs

paragraphs.text: If it were not that all people might become one community of disbelief, Allah would have given the houses of those who deny the Most Merciful roofs and stairways of silver, silver doors and couches to lean on, and decorations of gold. Yet all of that is only the enjoyment of worldly life, while the Hereafter with the Lord is for the righteous.

Whoever turns blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful is given a devil as a constant companion. Such devils block people from the right way while those people think they are rightly guided. When that person finally comes before Allah, he will wish there were the distance of east and west between himself and his companion, a miserable friend indeed. On that Day it will not help the wrongdoers at all that they share the punishment together.

The Prophet cannot make the deaf hear or guide the blind or those in clear error. Whether Allah takes him in death first or shows him what was promised to them, Allah will surely punish them, because He is perfect in ability. So the Prophet must hold firmly to what was revealed to him, since he is on a straight path. The Qur'an is a reminder for him and his people, and they will all be questioned about it. He may ask the earlier messengers whether Allah ever appointed other deities to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful.

Allah sent Moses with His signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and Moses announced that he was the messenger of the Lord of the worlds. But when he showed them the signs, they laughed at them. Each sign Allah showed them was greater than the one before, and He seized them with hardship so that they might return. Then they said to Moses, "O magician, call on your Lord for us by the promise He made you, and we will be guided."

hardWords.m: chose or set someone for a job

257.title: Pharaoh's Boasting and Jesus as an Example

paragraphs.text: But as soon as Allah removed the hardship, they broke their promise. Pharaoh then called out to his people, boasting that the kingdom of Egypt and the rivers flowing beneath him belonged to him. "Do you not see?" he asked them. He asked whether he was not better than Moses, whom he called insignificant and barely able to speak clearly. He mocked Moses, asking why he had no golden bracelets and why no angels came with him. In this way Pharaoh fooled his people, and they obeyed him, because they were themselves defiantly disobedient. When they angered Allah, He punished them and drowned them all, making them a lesson and an example for later generations.

When the son of Mary was presented as an example, the Prophet's people laughed aloud. They asked whether the things they worshipped were better than he, but they only said this for the sake of argument, because they love to quarrel. Jesus was nothing more than a servant on whom Allah bestowed His favor, and Allah made him an example for the Children of Israel. If Allah willed, He could have placed angels on the earth to succeed one another instead of humans. Jesus is a sign for knowing the Hour, so there should be no doubt about it. People should follow the straight path and never let Satan turn them away, since he is a clear enemy.

When Jesus came with clear proofs, he said he had brought wisdom and would explain some of their disagreements. He told them to fear Allah and obey him, because Allah is his Lord and their Lord, and worshipping Him is the straight path. However, the groups among them disagreed and split, so woe to the wrongdoers from the punishment of a painful Day. What are they waiting for, except the Hour, which will come upon them suddenly while they do not even notice it?

hardWords.m: to come after and take the place of

258.title: Gold Plates in Paradise, Despair in Hell

paragraphs.text: On that Day, close friends will become enemies to one another, except for the righteous. Allah will call to His servants, those who believed in His verses and were Muslims, and assure them that there is no fear for them that Day and that they will never grieve. They will be invited to enter Paradise together with their kind, full of joy. Plates and cups of gold will be passed around among them, and they will have whatever their souls desire and whatever pleases their eyes, living there forever. This Paradise is given to them as an inheritance because of their deeds, and in it there is much fruit, more than enough, from which they will eat.

The criminals, however, will remain in the punishment of Hell forever. It will never be eased for them, and they will be in complete despair. This punishment is not unfair, because Allah did not wrong them in any way; rather, it was they who were the wrongdoers. They will call out to Malik, begging that their Lord put an end to them, but he will answer that they will remain there. Allah had certainly brought them the truth, yet most of them disliked the truth and turned from it.

Have the disbelievers decided on some plan against the truth? If so, Allah too is making a plan. Do they think He does not hear their secrets and private talks? He certainly does, and His messengers stay with them, writing everything down. The Prophet is told to say that if the Most Merciful had a son, he would be the first to worship him. But the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Lord of the Throne, is exalted far above what they describe. So the Prophet should leave them to chatter and play until they meet the Day they have been promised.

hardWords.m: something received from someone who came before
to say what something is like
to talk a lot about useless things

259.title: The Only Deity and the Blessed Night

paragraphs.text: Allah alone is the deity in the heaven and the only deity on the earth, and He is the Wise, the Knowing. Blessed is He who owns the heavens and the earth and everything between them; He alone has knowledge of when the Hour will come, and to Him all will be returned. The ones people call upon besides Him have no power to intercede, except those who bear witness to the truth with knowledge. If the disbelievers are asked who created them, they will surely answer, "Allah," so how can they be so deluded and turned away from worshipping Him? Allah takes note of the Prophet's words when he complained, "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe." He is told to turn away from them and say, "Peace," because they will soon know the truth.

A new surah opens with Ha, Meem, and an oath by the clear Book. Allah sent this Book down during a blessed night, because He has always intended to warn mankind. On that night every precise matter is set apart, as a command from Allah. He was going to send a messenger as a mercy from the Lord, the Hearing, the Knowing. He is Lord of the heavens, the earth and all that lies between them, if only people would be certain of it. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death, and He is their Lord and the Lord of their earliest forefathers.

Yet the disbelievers remain in doubt, amusing themselves and not taking the message seriously. So the Prophet is told to watch and wait for a coming Day, when the sky will bring forth a smoke that everyone can see. It will spread over the people and cover them, and it will be a painful torment for them.

hardWords.m: to speak to someone to help another person
said that something was wrong or unfair
people of one's family who lived long ago
with real attention, not as a joke

260.title: The Smoke, and Pharaoh's People Leave Everything

paragraphs.text: When the smoke covers them, the people will cry out to their Lord, begging Him to take the torment away and insisting that they are now believers. But how can a reminder benefit them at such a late time? A Messenger who made everything clear had already come to them, yet they turned their backs on him, claiming that he had only been taught by others and that he was a madman. Allah says He will remove the torment for a little while, yet they will surely return to their disbelief. Then comes the Day when Allah will strike with the greatest assault, and on that Day He will certainly take retribution.

Long before these people, Allah had already tested the people of Pharaoh, and a noble messenger came to them. He asked them to hand over the servants of Allah to him, explaining that he was a trustworthy messenger. He also warned them not to raise themselves proudly above Allah, since he had come to them with clear authority. He said he had sought refuge in his Lord and their Lord from being stoned by them, and if they would not believe him, they should simply leave him alone. Finally, he called out to his Lord, saying that these were a criminal people.

Allah then commanded him to travel by night with His servants, warning him that they would be chased. He was told to leave the sea calm and still behind them, because Pharaoh's army was an army destined to be drowned. Think of how much they left behind: gardens and flowing springs, fields of crops and noble places, and the comfortable life in which they had taken such delight! That is how it ended, and Allah made another people inherit all of it.

hardWords.m: places where water comes up from the ground

261.title: No Tears for Pharaoh, and the Tree of Zaqqum

paragraphs.text: When Pharaoh's people were destroyed, neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them, and they were not given any extra time to escape their end. Allah rescued the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment that they suffered under Pharaoh, who was a proud man and one of those who went beyond all limits. With full knowledge, Allah chose the Children of Israel above the worlds, and He gave them many signs, in which there was a clear test for them.

Now the disbelievers among the Prophet's people keep repeating that there is nothing beyond their first death and that they will never be raised again. Then they challenge the Prophet and the believers to bring their forefathers back to life if he is really telling the truth. But are they any better than the people of Tubba' and the nations who came before them? Allah destroyed those peoples, because they were criminals.

Allah did not create the heavens, the earth and everything between them as a game or for amusement. He created them only in truth and for a real purpose, although most people do not understand this. The Day of Judgement is the appointed time for all of them. On that Day no relative will be able to help another relative in the slightest way, and no one will receive any help, except those on whom Allah has mercy. He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

After this, the passage describes the terrible food that awaits the people of Hell. The tree of zaqqum, it says, will be the food of the sinful. That food is like murky, dirty oil, and once the sinful have eaten it, it will boil and churn inside their bellies.

hardWords.m: to ask someone to prove something

262.title: Scalding Water and Gardens of Silk

paragraphs.text: The zaqqum boils in the bellies of the sinful in the same way that scalding water boils and bubbles. Then a harsh command will be given about each of them: seize the sinner, drag him into the middle of Hellfire, and pour scalding water over his head as punishment. He will be told mockingly to taste it, because in the world he thought of himself as honored and noble. This, he will be reminded, is exactly the punishment he used to doubt and argue about during his life.

The righteous, in contrast, will be in a place of safety, among gardens and springs. They will wear clothes of fine silk and rich brocade, sitting face to face with one another. Allah will marry them to fair women with large, beautiful eyes. There they may ask for any kind of fruit they like, and it will be brought to them while they feel safe and secure. They will never taste death again after the first death, and Allah will have protected them from the punishment of Hellfire. All this comes as a generous bounty from the Prophet's Lord, and it is truly the great success.

Allah has made the Qur'an easy to understand by sending it in the Prophet's own language, so that people might remember and take the lesson from it. So the Prophet is told to wait and watch what happens, because the disbelievers too are waiting and watching for his end.

Then a new surah begins with the letters Ha, Meem. The revelation of this Book comes from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Indeed, within the heavens and the earth there are many signs for those who truly believe.

hardWords.m: extremely hot, able to burn skin
to take hold of suddenly and firmly
in a way that makes fun of someone
thick rich cloth with raised patterns

263.title: Signs Everywhere and Forgiving the Doubters

paragraphs.text: There are also signs in the creation of human beings and of the moving creatures that Allah spreads across the earth, for people of certain faith. The changing of night and day, the provision He sends down from the sky to bring the earth back to life after it was lifeless, and His directing of the winds are signs for people who use reason. These are Allah's verses, recited in truth; if people reject them, what will they believe?

Woe to every sinful liar who hears the verses of Allah recited to him and then continues in his pride, as if he had not heard them at all. Whenever he learns any of the verses, he mocks them, and such people face a humiliating punishment. Hell awaits them, and neither their earnings nor their chosen protectors will help. The Qur'an is true guidance, while those who reject it face a foul, painful punishment.

Allah has made the sea serve people, so that ships sail by His command and people seek His bounty and give thanks. He has made everything in the heavens and earth serve them, all as a gift from Him, and in this there are signs for those who reflect. The believers are told to forgive those who do not expect the days of Allah, since Allah will repay every people for their deeds. Whoever does good benefits himself, whoever does evil harms himself, and all will return to their Lord.

Allah gave the Children of Israel the Scripture, judgement and prophethood, provided them with good things, and preferred them over the worlds. He gave them clear proofs, yet they split only after knowledge reached them, out of envy among themselves, and Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Then He placed the Prophet on a clear way of religion, so he must follow it and not the desires of those without knowledge. Wrongdoers are allies of one another, but Allah is the protector of the righteous. This Qur'an is clear insight for mankind, and guidance and mercy for people who are certain.

hardWords.bn: তিলাওয়াত করা হয় / পাঠ করা হয়

hardWords.m: wanting what someone else has and disliking them for it
chose or liked one more than another

264.title: Every Nation Kneeling Before Its Record

paragraphs.text: Do evildoers think Allah will make them equal to believers who do good, in life and in death? How bad is their judgement! Allah created the heavens and earth in truth, so every soul is repaid fairly for what it earned. Consider one who worships his own desire: Allah has let him go astray knowingly, sealed his hearing and his heart, and covered his eyes. Who can guide him after Allah? Will people not remember?

The disbelievers claim there is only this worldly life, where they live and die and only time destroys them, but they are just assuming without knowledge. When the clear verses are recited, they only demand that their forefathers be brought back. The Prophet answers that Allah gives life, causes death, and will gather them for the certain Day of Resurrection, though most people do not know. The kingdom of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, and on the Day the Hour arrives, those who follow falsehood will lose.

On that Day every nation will be seen kneeling, and each will be called to its record. Their record will speak the truth about them, since all their deeds were written down. Those who believed and did good will enter their Lord's mercy, which is the clear success. The disbelievers will be reminded that Allah's verses were recited to them, but they acted arrogantly and became criminals. Told that Allah's promise is true and the Hour is certain, they said they only guessed and were not convinced. The evil results of their deeds will appear, and they will be surrounded by what they mocked. Today Allah will forget them as they forgot this Day, and the Fire will be their home with no helpers. They mocked Allah's verses and were fooled by worldly life, so they will never leave it or be allowed to make amends.
So all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth and Lord of the worlds. All greatness in the heavens and the earth is His, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

hardWords.m: a written account of what someone did
making up for a wrong one has done
the quality of being very great

265.title: Kindness to Parents and a Prayer at Forty

paragraphs.text: A new surah opens with Ha, Meem: the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. He created the heavens and earth in truth for a fixed term, yet the disbelievers ignore the warning. The Prophet challenges them to show what the things they worship have created, or to bring an earlier scripture or a trace of knowledge. No one is more astray than one who calls on beings who cannot answer him and are unaware of his calls; on the Day of gathering they become his enemies and deny his worship.

Hearing the verses, the disbelievers call the truth obvious magic or claim the Prophet invented it. He answers that they could not protect him from Allah if he had, and Allah is enough as a Witness. He is nothing new among the messengers, does not know what will happen to him or to them, and only follows revelation as a clear warner. A witness from the Children of Israel believed in something similar, while they stayed arrogant. The disbelievers say that if it were good, the believers would not have reached it first, calling it an old lie. Before it came the Scripture of Moses as guidance and mercy, which this Arabic Book confirms.

Those who say, 'Our Lord is Allah,' and stay firm will have no fear or grief, and will live in Paradise forever. Allah commands kindness to parents. A mother carries her child and gives birth with hardship, and carrying and weaning take thirty months. At forty, having reached maturity, he asks Allah to help him be grateful for His favors on him and his parents, to do pleasing deeds, and to make his children righteous, for he has repented and submitted. Allah accepts their best deeds and overlooks their sins.

Another son rudely says 'Uff' to his parents, asking how he could be raised when earlier generations are gone. They beg Allah for help and urge him to believe, but he calls it old stories. Such people, like earlier jinn and men, deserve the word of punishment and are losers.

hardWords.m: a very small sign or part left of something
very easy to see or understand
stopping a baby from drinking its mother's milk
the time of being fully grown
chooses not to punish a fault
in a way that is not polite

paragraphs.text: People receive degrees according to what they have done. Allah fully compensates everyone, and no one is wronged. Those exposed to the Fire are told that they used their worldly pleasures and are punished for arrogance and disobedience. The brother of Aad warned his people to worship Allah alone and feared a terrible day for them. They mocked his warning and demanded what he promised. He said knowledge of its time belongs only to Allah, while he had delivered his message. When they mistook an approaching cloud for rain, it was the painful wind they had challenged. By its Lord's command, it destroyed everything until only their homes remained. Aad had been given hearing, sight, and hearts, but these did not help them when they rejected Allah's signs. Nearby cities were also destroyed, yet their supposed deities could not help them. The people had strayed from those deities, and their claims were inventions. Their worldly enjoyment does not protect them from that humiliation. Their warning had come from a messenger, but they asked whether he would delude them away from their gods. They were impatient for the punishment they had been warned about. They behaved ignorantly when he explained that its timing was known only to Allah.

A few jinn listened quietly when they heard the Qur'an. Afterward, they returned to their people as warners. They said that the revealed Book confirmed what came before it and guided to truth and a straight path. They called their people to respond to Allah's Messenger, believe in him, and seek forgiveness and protection from painful punishment. Whoever refuses the Caller cannot escape Allah or find another protector. The passage asks whether the Creator of the heavens and earth can give life to the dead, and answers that He can. Those who denied the truth will acknowledge it when facing the Fire. The Messenger is told to be patient like the messengers of determination and not to hurry. When the promised day comes, worldly time will seem like only an hour. Only defiantly disobedient people will be destroyed.

Those who disbelieve and turn people away from Allah's path will have their deeds wasted. Those who believe, do righteous deeds, and accept what was sent down upon Muhammad will have their misdeeds removed and their condition improved. The passage contrasts falsehood with truth. It describes fighting, securing captives, and then releasing them by favor or ransom when the war has ended. Those killed in Allah's cause will not lose their deeds. Allah guides them, improves their condition, and admits them to Paradise. Believers are urged to support Allah, and He will support them and make their feet firm. By contrast, those who reject what Allah revealed lose their deeds. The passage points to the end of earlier peoples as a warning, and says that Allah protects believers while disbelievers have no protector. The passage explains that this testing lets some people be tested through others. Those killed in Allah's cause receive guidance and a better condition, and Paradise has been made known to them. The contrast is repeated: disbelievers face misery, while Allah is the protector of those who believe. The earlier cities show that strength alone did not save them.

Believers who do righteous deeds will enter gardens with rivers, while disbelievers enjoy life as grazing livestock do and face the Fire. Many cities stronger than Makkah were destroyed, with no helper for them. The passage asks whether someone guided by clear evidence is like someone who follows desires after evil work has seemed attractive. Paradise is described with rivers of water, milk, wine, and purified honey, fruit, and forgiveness from the Lord. This is compared with the Fire and scalding water. Some people listen to the Messenger, then ask others what he said; they follow their desires and have sealed hearts. Those who accept guidance receive more guidance and righteousness. The description also mentions that Allah increases the guided in guidance and gives them righteousness. It contrasts those on clear evidence with those led by desires, and asks whether their outcomes can be alike.

The Hour may come unexpectedly, though signs have already appeared. When it comes, remembrance will not benefit those who waited. The Messenger is told to know that there is no deity except Allah and to ask forgiveness for himself and for believing men and women. Allah knows where people move and rest. Some believers ask why a surah has not been sent down, but when a precise surah mentions fighting, hypocrites look as though death has overcome them. Obedience and good words would be better, and truthfulness before Allah would benefit them when a matter is decided. The passage warns against turning away, causing corruption, and severing family ties. Allah curses such people and blinds and deafens them. They are asked to reflect on the Qur'an rather than lock their hearts. Satan entices those who return to disbelief after guidance has become clear. They conceal what they intend, but Allah knows it. The passage also says those who turn away may sever their family relationships. Such people lose hearing and sight, and the question about locks upon hearts calls for reflection. Satan makes a return to disbelief seem appealing and lengthens hope. Some people agree secretly with those who dislike what Allah sent down, while Allah knows what they hide.

Angels take some people in death, striking their faces and backs. Their deeds become worthless because they pursued what angered Allah and disliked what earns His pleasure. Allah can expose hatred through speech and knows people's actions. Believers will be tested so that those who strive and those who are patient become evident. Those who oppose the Messenger and turn people from Allah's path cannot harm Allah; their deeds will be rendered worthless. Believers are commanded to obey Allah and the Messenger and not invalidate their own deeds. Those who die as disbelievers after turning others away from Allah's path will not receive forgiveness. Allah's test will make clear who strives for His cause and who remains patient. Their own deeds are lost. The believers are directly told to obey both Allah and the Messenger.

269.title: Faith, Giving, and a Clear Victory

paragraphs.text: Believers are told not to weaken or call for peace while they are superior, because Allah is with them and will not deprive them of their reward. Worldly life is amusement and diversion. If people believe and fear Allah, He gives their rewards without asking for their wealth. If He pressed them for it, their unwillingness would be exposed. They are invited to spend in Allah's cause, yet some hold back out of greed. Whoever withholds only harms himself; Allah is free of need, while people are needy. If they turn away, Allah will replace them with another people. Holding back is to a person's own detriment, because Allah has no need while people are needy.

Allah has given a clear conquest so that He may forgive the Messenger, complete His favor, guide him, and grant a mighty victory. He sent tranquillity into believers' hearts, increasing their faith. The forces of the heavens and earth belong to Allah, who is Knowing and Wise. He will admit believing men and women to gardens with rivers and remove their misdeeds. Hypocrite men and women, and polytheist men and women who assume evil about Allah, face punishment and Hell. Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.

The Messenger is sent as a witness, bringer of good tidings, and warner. People should believe in Allah and His Messenger, honor the Prophet, and exalt Allah morning and afternoon. Those who pledge allegiance to the Messenger are pledging to Allah. Breaking the pledge harms the breaker, while fulfilling it brings a great reward. Some Bedouins who stayed behind claim that family and property occupied them, but their tongues do not match their hearts. No one can prevent Allah from bringing harm or benefit. They wrongly thought the Messenger and believers would not return and became ruined by that assumption. Whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger faces a Blaze.

The dominion of the heavens and earth belongs to Allah. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and He is Forgiving and Merciful. Those who stayed behind ask to follow when the believers set out for booty, but they want to change Allah's words. They are told that they will not follow, and they accuse the believers of envy without understanding. The Bedouins will be called to face a people of great military might. Obedience brings a good reward, while turning away brings painful punishment. Blind people, lame people, and ill people are not guilty for staying behind. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger enters gardens with rivers; whoever turns away is punished. Allah was pleased with the believers who pledged allegiance beneath the tree. He knew their hearts, sent tranquillity, and rewarded them with a near conquest and much booty. He also promises future victories and guidance.

If the disbelievers of Makkah had fought the believers, they would have turned back without a protector or helper. Allah's established way does not change. At Makkah, He withheld both sides' hands after giving the believers victory. The disbelievers obstructed access to al-Masjid al-Haram and prevented the offering from reaching its place. Believing men and women whom the believers did not know were there; entering might have harmed them unknowingly. Allah admitted whom He willed to His mercy. Allah sent tranquillity to His Messenger and the believers and gave them the word of righteousness. The Messenger's vision was true: they would enter the Sacred Mosque safely, if Allah willed. Allah sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth. Muhammad is Allah's Messenger, and those with him are firm against disbelievers and merciful among themselves. They bow and prostrate, seeking Allah's bounty and pleasure. Allah promised forgiveness and a great reward to those who believe and do righteous deeds.
Believers are told not to put themselves ahead of Allah and His Messenger. They should fear Allah, who hears and knows.

271.title: Good Manners, Brotherhood, and True Faith

paragraphs.text: The believers are told not to raise their voices above the voice of the Prophet, and not to speak loudly to him as they do with one another. Otherwise, their good deeds could become worthless without them even noticing. Those who lower their voices before the Messenger of Allah are people whose hearts Allah has tested for righteousness, and they will receive forgiveness and a great reward. Most of those who called to him from behind his rooms did not use reason; waiting patiently would have been better.

If a disobedient person brings some news, the believers must investigate it first, so that they do not harm innocent people out of ignorance and then feel regret. Allah has made faith beloved and beautiful in their hearts, and disbelief hateful, as a favor from Him. If two groups of believers fight, others should make peace between them. If one group keeps oppressing the other, it must be resisted until it returns to Allah's command, and then peace should be made with justice. The believers are brothers, so they should repair the bond between them.

No group should mock another, because the mocked may be better in reality. Believers must not insult each other or use offensive nicknames. They should avoid much suspicion, since some suspicion is sin, and they must not spy or backbite. Backbiting is like eating a dead brother's flesh. Allah created mankind from a male and a female and made them peoples and tribes so that they may know one another. The most noble in Allah's sight is the most righteous.

Some bedouins claimed full faith, but they were told to say instead that they had submitted, because faith had not yet entered their hearts. True believers trust Allah and His Messenger without doubt and strive with their wealth and lives. Nobody should treat their Islam as a favor to the Prophet; rather, Allah has favored them by guiding them.

hardWords.m: to check carefully to find the truth
a sad feeling about something you did
thinking bad things about someone without proof
to say bad things about someone who is not there

272.title: Signs of Creation and the Promise of Return

paragraphs.text: The surah opens with the letter Qaf and an oath by the honored Qur'an. The disbelievers are surprised that a warner has come to them from among their own people, and they call this an amazing thing. They ask how they could possibly come back to life after they have died and turned into dust, and they consider such a return to be far from possible. However, Allah knows exactly how much of their bodies the earth takes away, and He keeps a record that preserves everything. Because they rejected the truth when it reached them, they are now in a state of confusion.

They are invited to look at the sky above them and reflect on how Allah built it and decorated it, without any cracks. He also spread out the earth, placed firm mountains on it, and caused every beautiful kind of plant to grow there. All of this gives insight and a reminder to every servant who turns back to Allah. He sends down blessed rain from the sky, which produces gardens, grain for harvest, and tall palm trees with fruit arranged in layers. These are provision for His servants, and through this rain He brings a dead land back to life. In the same way, the resurrection will happen.

Before these people, many others also denied the truth: the people of Noah, the companions of the well, Thamud, 'Aad, Pharaoh, the brothers of Lot, the companions of the thicket, and the people of Tubba'. All of them rejected the messengers, so Allah's warning came true against them. Allah did not fail in the first creation, yet they are still doubtful about a new creation.

Allah created man and knows even what his soul whispers to him, and He is closer to him than his jugular vein. Two recording angels sit with each person, one on the right and one on the left, receiving everything.

hardWords.m: food and things needed for life
coming back to life after death
the big blood vessel in the neck

273.title: Death, Judgment, and the Gift of Paradise

paragraphs.text: Every single word a person speaks is noted by an observer who is ready to record it. Then the stupor of death arrives and brings the truth, which is exactly what people were trying to escape. The Horn will be blown, and that will be the Day when the warning is carried out. Every soul will come forward with a driver and a witness. It will be said to each person that he was careless about this Day, but now his cover has been removed, so his sight has become sharp and clear.

His companion angel will say that the record is ready. Then Allah will command that every stubborn disbeliever be thrown into Hell. This includes anyone who prevented good, attacked others, and lived in doubt, and who set up another deity alongside Allah. Such a person will be thrown into the severe punishment.

His devil companion will try to defend himself, saying to Allah that he did not make the person go beyond limits, but that the person himself was already deeply lost. Allah will tell them not to argue before Him, since He had already sent them the warning in advance. His word does not change, and He is never unjust to His servants. On that Day, Allah will ask Hell whether it has been filled, and Hell will reply by asking whether there are still more to come.

In contrast, Paradise will be brought close to the righteous, so that it is not far away from them at all. They will be told that this is what was promised to everyone who kept turning back to Allah and guarded His covenant. These are the people who feared the Most Merciful even though they could not see Him, and who came with a heart that returned to Him in repentance. They will be welcomed with the words, "Enter it in peace," because this is the Day of Eternity, a life that never ends.

hardWords.m: a state like being half asleep and confused
a false god that people worship

274.title: Patience, Praise, and the Day of Rising

paragraphs.text: In Paradise, the righteous will have whatever they wish, and Allah has even more for them beyond that. Many generations before this time were destroyed, although they were mightier in power and had travelled widely through the lands. Yet none of them found any place to escape. In this there is a reminder for anyone who has a living heart, or who listens with full attention.

Allah created the heavens, the earth, and everything between them in six days, and no tiredness touched Him at all. Therefore the Prophet is told to be patient with what the disbelievers say. He should glorify his Lord with praise before sunrise and before sunset, during part of the night, and after the prostrations of prayer.

He is also told to listen for the Day when the Caller will call out from a place that is near. On that Day, people will hear the mighty blast in truth, and it will be the Day of coming out from the graves. It is Allah alone who gives life and causes death, and to Him is the final return. The earth will split open, and people will rush out quickly, because gathering them is easy for Him. Allah knows best what the disbelievers say. The Prophet is not a tyrant over them who forces them; his duty is to remind, through the Qur'an, those who fear Allah's warning.

The next surah begins with a series of oaths. Allah swears by the winds that scatter dust, by the clouds that carry heavy loads of water, by the ships that sail smoothly, and by the angels who distribute every matter. After these oaths comes the message: what people are promised is certainly true, and the recompense for deeds will definitely take place. These verses remind the reader that the Day of Judgment is not a story but a firm reality.

hardWords.m: groups of people living at the same time
bowing with the forehead on the ground
a cruel ruler who forces people
to throw or spread in many directions
payment or reward for what one did

275.title: The Heedless and the Pious Who Pray at Night

paragraphs.text: Allah swears by the sky that is full of pathways. People hold confused and conflicting opinions about the truth. Whoever is turned away from the Qur'an has truly been deceived. The liars who invent falsehood are condemned; they are drowning in a flood of confusion and remain careless about what lies ahead. They mockingly ask when the Day of Recompense will arrive. The answer is that it is the Day when they will be punished over the Fire, with no way to avoid it. They will be told to taste their torment, since this is the very thing they were so impatient to see.

The righteous, on the other hand, will live among gardens and springs, gladly accepting whatever their Lord gives them. This is because they were people who did good before that Day. Their way of life on earth is described in a beautiful manner, as an example for every reader to follow. They used to sleep only a small part of the night, and in the early hours before dawn they would ask Allah for forgiveness. In addition, from their wealth they gave a rightful share to the needy person who asked and to the deprived person who could not ask.

There are many signs on the earth for those who have firm faith, and there are signs within human beings themselves as well. People are asked whether they will not open their eyes and see these signs. In the heaven lies their provision, and also everything they have been promised. Finally, Allah swears by the Lord of the heaven and the earth that this promise is the truth. It is just as certain as the fact that people are able to speak. Just as no one doubts that they are speaking, no one should doubt this promise, because it comes from the Lord of everything.

276.title: Abraham's Guests and the Fate of Pharaoh

paragraphs.text: The surah tells the story of the honored guests who visited Abraham. When they came in, they greeted him with peace, and he returned the greeting, noting that they were people he did not know. He quietly went to his family and returned with a fat roasted calf. He placed it near them and politely asked them why they would not eat. When they did not eat, he felt fear of them. They told him not to be afraid and gave him good news of a boy who would be full of knowledge. His wife came forward with a cry of surprise, struck her face, and said that she was a barren old woman. The guests replied that this was what her Lord had said, and that He is the Wise, the Knowing.

Abraham then asked the messengers what their mission was. They explained that they had been sent to a criminal people, in order to send down upon them stones of hardened clay. These stones were marked by Allah for the transgressors who had gone beyond all limits. Before the punishment, Allah brought out the believers who lived in those cities. However, only a single house of Muslims was found among them. Allah left a sign in that place for those who fear the painful punishment, so that they can learn from what happened.

There was also a sign in the story of Moses, whom Allah sent to Pharaoh with clear authority and proof. Pharaoh, however, turned away arrogantly, relying on his supporters and his power. He called Moses either a magician or a madman. As a result, Allah seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea, while he was to blame for what he had done. These stories show that Allah keeps His promise both to reward and to punish.

hardWords.m: a special job someone is sent to do
people who break the limits set by Allah
in a proud way, thinking oneself better

277.title: Lessons of Past Nations and the Purpose of Creation

paragraphs.text: More signs are found in the stories of earlier nations. When Allah sent a barren, destructive wind against 'Aad, it turned everything it touched into crumbling ruins. The people of Thamud were told to enjoy themselves for a limited time, but they insolently rebelled against their Lord's command. So a thunderbolt seized them while they were watching, and they could neither stand up nor defend themselves. Before all of them, the people of Noah were also destroyed, because they were a people who stubbornly disobeyed.

Allah built the heaven with great strength, and He is continually expanding it. He spread out the earth, and He prepares it in an excellent way for His creatures. He created everything in pairs, so that people might remember and reflect. Therefore, the Prophet calls people to flee to Allah, and he declares that he is a clear warner sent from Him. He also warns them not to set up any other deity alongside Allah, repeating that he is a clear warner from Him.

This kind of rejection is nothing new. Every messenger who came to earlier peoples was called either a magician or a madman. It is as if they had passed this insult down to one another, though in fact they were simply a people who exceeded all limits. The Prophet is told to turn away from them, since he will not be blamed for their choices. Yet he should keep reminding, because reminding brings real benefit to the believers.

Then comes a central statement about the purpose of existence. Allah says that He created the jinn and mankind only so that they would worship Him. He does not need any provision from them, nor does He ask them to feed Him, since He is completely free of need. It is Allah alone who is the constant Provider of all creation, the Owner of firm and unshakable strength. Every living thing depends on Him, while He depends on nothing at all.

278.title: Oaths by the Mount and the Coming Punishment

paragraphs.text: Those who do wrong will receive a share of punishment like the share given to the wrongdoers who came before them. Therefore, they should not impatiently ask Allah to hurry it. Woe to the disbelievers because of the Day that has been promised to them, since it is certainly coming.

The next surah, called The Mount, opens with a series of solemn oaths. Allah swears by the mount, and by a Book that is written down on parchment spread open. He also swears by the frequented House, by the heaven raised high above, and by the sea that will be filled with fire. After these oaths, a firm statement follows: the punishment of the Lord will surely happen. No one and nothing will be able to prevent it or push it back, no matter how powerful they think they are.

On that Day, the sky will shake and sway in a circular motion, and the mountains will move away from their places and vanish. It will be a terrible Day for those who denied the truth. These deniers spent their lives in empty talk, playing and amusing themselves, without taking the message seriously. They treated warnings as a joke and never thought about where they were heading.

On that Day, they will be pushed violently toward the fire of Hell. Then the angels will say to them that this is the very Fire which they used to deny when they lived on earth. They will be asked a sharp question: is this magic, as they used to claim about the message, or are they simply unable to see? In the world, they called the truth magic and refused to look at it honestly. Now the reality stands directly in front of them, and they can no longer pretend that it is an illusion or a trick. What they mocked as a story has now become the place where they must stay.

hardWords.m: old material for writing, made from animal skin
to move from side to side
something that looks real but is not

279.title: Delights of Paradise and the Prophet's Reminder

paragraphs.text: The people of the Fire will be told to enter and burn in it. Whether they bear it patiently or complain, it makes no difference for them, because they are only being paid back for what they used to do.

The righteous, in contrast, will live in gardens and delight, enjoying what their Lord has given them, and He has protected them from the punishment of Hellfire. They will be invited to eat and drink with satisfaction as a reward for their deeds. They will recline on thrones arranged in rows, and Allah will marry them to fair companions with large, beautiful eyes. Those who believed, and whose children followed them in faith, will have their descendants joined with them, while nothing will be reduced from their own deeds. Every person is held responsible for what he earned. They will receive fruit and meat of whatever they desire. They will pass a cup among themselves that leads to no foolish talk and no sin, and young servants, like protected pearls, will move around them.

The people of Paradise will turn to one another and talk about their past. They will remember that, while living among their families, they were fearful of displeasing Allah. Because of this, Allah showed them His favor and saved them from the scorching Fire. They will add that they used to call upon Him in prayer before, and that He is truly the Beneficent, the Merciful.

The Prophet is told to continue reminding people. By his Lord's favor, he is neither a fortune-teller nor a madman. Some say he is merely a poet and that they are waiting for some misfortune to strike him. He is told to answer that they may wait, and he too will wait along with them. The passage then asks whether their own minds truly lead them to such claims, or whether they are simply a people who go beyond limits.

hardWords.m: a person who claims to know the future

paragraphs.text: Some disbelievers claim that the Prophet invented the Qur'an himself, but the real reason is that they refuse to believe. They are challenged to produce a statement like it, if they are truthful. Then a series of powerful questions follows. Were they created from nothing, or did they create themselves? Did they create the heavens and the earth? In fact, they have no certainty at all. Do they own the treasures of their Lord's provision, or are they in control of them? Do they have a ladder into the sky so they can listen to what is said there? If so, their listener should bring clear proof.

The questions continue. Does Allah have daughters while they have sons? Is the Prophet asking them for payment, so that they feel heavily burdened by debt? Do they have knowledge of the unseen, which they write down for themselves? Are they planning a scheme against him? If so, it is the disbelievers themselves who will fall into a plan. Or do they have some deity other than Allah? Allah is exalted far above everything they associate with Him.

Their stubbornness is so deep that even if they saw a piece of the sky falling down, they would simply say it was only clouds piled up. So the Prophet is told to leave them until they meet their Day, when they will be struck unconscious. On that Day, their scheming will not benefit them in any way, and no one will help them. Moreover, the wrongdoers will face a punishment even before that Day, but most of them do not realize it.

The Prophet is told to wait patiently for his Lord's decision, because he is always under Allah's watchful care. He should glorify his Lord with praise when he rises, during part of the night, and as the stars fade away.

hardWords.m: made up something that is not true
not awake, not able to feel or know

281.title: The Prophet's Vision and the Lote Tree

paragraphs.text: The surah called The Star begins with an oath by the star as it goes down. Allah declares that the people's companion, Muhammad, has not gone astray, nor has he made a mistake. He does not speak from his own desire or personal wishes. What he speaks is nothing except revelation that is sent down to him. In this way, the opening verses defend the Prophet against those who accused him of lying or of inventing the message.

He was taught by one who is very strong and mighty, one of soundness, who rose to his true form while he was on the highest part of the horizon. Then he came closer and came down, until he was at a distance of two bow lengths, or even nearer. At that moment, Allah revealed to His Servant what He revealed. The Prophet's heart did not deny or misunderstand what he saw; it was a real and truthful experience. Therefore, the listeners are asked how they can possibly argue with him about something he saw with his own eyes.

The Prophet also saw him on another occasion, during a second descent. This took place at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, near which lies the Garden of Refuge. At that time, the Lote Tree was covered by whatever covered it, something too great to describe. Throughout this amazing scene, the Prophet's sight did not turn aside, and it did not go beyond its limit. He looked steadily and with full attention, without being distracted and without overstepping. In this way, the passage reassures the reader that what the Prophet saw was real and true, because neither his heart nor his eyes were deceived about it. He certainly saw it, just as the verses describe, at that high and honored tree near the Garden of Refuge.

hardWords.m: the line where the sky seems to meet the earth
a particular time when something happens
makes someone feel calm and sure

282.title: False Idols, Mere Guesswork, and Allah's Wide Forgiveness

paragraphs.text: The Prophet saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord. Then the idol-worshippers are asked to think about their idols al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third one. Do they keep sons for themselves while giving daughters to Allah? That would be an unfair division. These idols are only names that they and their forefathers invented, and Allah sent down no authority for them. Such people follow only guesswork and the desires of their souls, even though guidance has already reached them from their Lord.

A person cannot simply have whatever he wishes, because both the Hereafter and this first life belong to Allah. There are many angels in the heavens, yet their intercession will not help anyone at all, unless Allah first gives permission to whom He wills and approves. Those who do not believe in the Hereafter give the angels female names, though they have no knowledge about it. They follow only assumption, and assumption is useless against the truth.

The Prophet is told to turn away from anyone who ignores Allah's message and wants nothing except the worldly life. That is the full extent of their knowledge. Allah knows best who strays from His path and who is rightly guided. Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him, so that He may repay evildoers for what they did and reward those who do good with the best reward.

Those who do good stay away from major sins and shameful deeds, apart from small faults. The Lord is vast in forgiveness. He knew people completely when He brought them out of the earth and when they were still unborn in their mothers' wombs. So they should not praise themselves as pure, because He knows best who fears Him. The passage then points to a man who turned away, who gave a little and then stopped.

hardWords.m: statues or things worshipped instead of Allah
ancestors, people of past generations of a family
asking for help or pardon for someone else

283.title: Each Soul Carries Its Own Burden

paragraphs.text: The passage continues to question the man who turned away and gave only a little. Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he can see what is hidden? Has he not been told about what was written in the scriptures of Moses and of Abraham, who faithfully fulfilled his duties? These scriptures contain several important principles. First, no soul that carries a burden of sin will carry the burden of another soul. Second, a person will have nothing except the good for which he has worked hard. Third, his effort will certainly be seen, and afterwards he will be repaid for it with the fullest and most complete reward.

The verses then list a number of truths about Allah's power, each beginning with the words "and that." The final end and return of everything is to the Lord. It is He who makes people laugh and makes them weep, and it is He who causes death and gives life. He creates the two kinds, male and female, from a small drop of fluid when it is released. It is His responsibility to bring about the next creation after death. He is the One who makes people rich and gives them enough, so that they are satisfied. He is also the Lord of Sirius, the bright star in the sky, so even the stars are under His control.

Finally, the verses remind the listeners of what happened to earlier nations who rejected the truth. Allah destroyed the first people of 'Aad, and He also destroyed Thamud, leaving none of them remaining. Their fate shows that the same Lord who gives life and wealth is also able to take them away completely when people persist in wrongdoing. Taken together, these verses teach that every person is responsible for his own deeds, that no effort is lost, and that all power belongs to Allah alone, from the first creation until the final return to Him.

284.title: The Approaching Hour and the Split Moon

paragraphs.text: Before 'Aad and Thamud, Allah destroyed the people of Noah, who were even more unjust and more oppressive. He also overturned the towns that were turned upside down and hurled them to the ground, covering them with whatever He covered them with. After recalling these events, the listener is asked which of the Lord's favors he still doubts. The Prophet is a warner just like the warners who came before him, bringing the same message about Allah and the final return, and the listeners should not treat his words as something strange or new.

The Approaching Day has now come close. Besides Allah, no one can remove it or delay it. The listeners are asked whether they are amazed at this message. Instead of weeping at such a serious warning, they laugh at it, and they spend their time proudly playing and amusing themselves, as if nothing important were coming. Their reaction shows how careless they have become about the most serious matter of all. The surah ends with a clear command: bow down in prostration to Allah and worship Him alone. This final instruction calls on everyone who hears it to respond with humility, not with pride.

The next surah, The Moon, begins by announcing that the Hour has drawn near and that the moon has split in two. Yet whenever the disbelievers see a miracle, they turn away and dismiss it as passing magic. They deny the truth and follow their own desires, although every matter will reach its settled end at its appointed time. News has already reached them that should be enough to hold them back from evil. It contains deep and complete wisdom, but warnings are of no use to them because they refuse to listen. Therefore, the Prophet is told to leave them. A Day is coming when the Caller will call people to something terrible, something they have never known before.

hardWords.m: an amazing event that only Allah can cause
not paying attention to what matters

285.title: Noah's Flood, 'Aad, and an Easy Qur'an

paragraphs.text: On the Day of the Caller, people will come out of their graves with lowered eyes, spreading everywhere like a cloud of locusts. They will rush toward the Caller, and the disbelievers will cry out that this is a hard and difficult Day.

Long before these deniers, the people of Noah also denied the truth. They rejected Allah's servant, called him a madman, and drove him away with threats, refusing to listen to his call. So Noah called upon his Lord, saying that he had been overpowered and asking for help. In response, Allah opened the gates of the sky with pouring rain and made the earth burst open with springs. The waters from above and below met for a purpose that had already been decided. Allah carried Noah on a vessel made of planks and nails, which sailed under His watchful care as a reward for the one who had been rejected. Allah left this event as a sign for later generations, and the listener is asked whether anyone will take a lesson from it. Indeed, how severe were His punishment and His warnings.

Then comes a sentence that is repeated several times in this surah: Allah has made the Qur'an easy to remember, so is there anyone who will remember? Next, the people of 'Aad also denied the truth. Allah sent against them a roaring, screaming wind on a day of continuous disaster. It pulled people out of their places, as if they were the trunks of palm trees torn up from their roots. Again the listener is reminded how severe His punishment and warnings were, and again it is repeated that the Qur'an has been made easy for remembrance.
After 'Aad, the people of Thamud also denied the warnings that came to them, and their story begins here.

hardWords.m: insects that fly in very large groups

286.title: Thamud's She-Camel and the People of Lot

paragraphs.text: The people of Thamud refused to follow their messenger. They asked whether they should follow a single human being from among themselves, claiming that doing so would lead them into error and madness. They wondered why the message had been sent down to him alone, and they accused him of being an arrogant liar. Allah replied that tomorrow they would find out who the arrogant liar really was. He was sending a she-camel as a test for them, so the messenger was told to watch them and remain patient. He was also told to inform them that the water must be shared, with each side drinking on its own turn. However, they called their companion, who boldly attacked and crippled the she-camel. How severe were Allah's punishment and warnings! He sent upon them a single blast from the sky, and they became like dry, broken twigs used for an animal pen. Once again, it is repeated that the Qur'an has been made easy to remember, so is there anyone who will remember?

The people of Lot also denied the warnings. Allah sent upon them a storm of stones, but He rescued the family of Lot just before dawn, as a favor from Him. This is how He rewards those who are grateful. Lot had already warned them about Allah's mighty strike, yet they kept arguing about the warnings. They even demanded that he hand over his guests to them, so Allah blinded their eyes and told them to taste His punishment and warnings. Early in the morning, a lasting punishment came upon them, and they were told again to taste what they had been warned about. As with the earlier stories, this passage closes with the same repeated reminder: Allah has made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will take heed? The repetition invites the reader to pause after each story and think seriously about its lesson before moving on.

hardWords.m: said that someone did something wrong
badly injured so it could not walk
small thin pieces of a branch

287.title: Pharaoh's End, Written Records, and the Most Merciful

paragraphs.text: Warnings also came to the people of Pharaoh, but they denied every one of Allah's signs. So Allah seized them, with the seizure of One who is Exalted in Might and Perfect in Ability, and none of them could escape.

The disbelievers being addressed are then asked a direct question. Are they any better than those earlier nations, or have they been given some protection written in the scriptures? Perhaps they say that they are a united group who will support one another. But this group will be defeated, and they will turn their backs and run away. Moreover, the Hour is their real appointment, and the Hour will be far more disastrous and more bitter than any defeat in this world. The criminals are lost in error and madness. On the Day when they are dragged into the Fire on their faces, they will be told to taste the touch of Saqar.

Allah has created everything according to a precise measure and decree. His command is carried out with a single word, as quickly as the blink of an eye. He has already destroyed others like them in the past, so is there anyone who will remember? Everything that people do is kept in written records, and every matter, whether small or great, is recorded. In contrast to the criminals, the righteous will live among gardens and rivers. They will sit in a seat of honor in the presence of a Sovereign who is Perfect in Ability. This is the final picture of the surah: a place of truth, nearness, and great respect for those who were mindful of their Lord.

The following surah begins with one of Allah's beautiful names, the Most Merciful. The first thing mentioned about Him is that He taught the Qur'an, showing that this teaching is itself one of His greatest gifts to people.

hardWords.m: the act of grabbing with force
an order or plan set by Allah
a supreme king who rules over all

288.title: Which of Your Lord's Favors Would You Deny?

paragraphs.text: The Most Merciful created man and taught him how to speak clearly and express himself. The sun and the moon move according to an exact calculation, never going off their course. The stars and the trees bow down in prostration to Him. He raised the sky high and set up the balance, so that people would not go beyond limits in it. Therefore, they must weigh with justice and must never cheat by giving less than the right measure.
