In this way, the order of the universe is connected with the honesty that people must show in their daily dealings.

Allah spread out the earth for all His creatures. On it there are fruits, and palm trees whose dates grow inside covers. There is also grain with its husks and plants with sweet smells. After describing these blessings, the surah asks for the first time a question that it will repeat many times: "So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" It invites the reader to stop and count the many good things he enjoys every day.

Allah created man from dry clay like that used for pottery, and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire. Again the question is asked: which of the Lord's favors would they deny? He is the Lord of the two sunrises and the Lord of the two sunsets, so both the beginning and the end of each day are in His hands. Once more, the same question follows, inviting each listener to look honestly at all he has been given.

Allah also released the two seas, so that they meet side by side. This passage continues in the following verses, but already the reader sees how every part of nature, from the sky to the earth and the seas, is presented as a favor that no one can truly deny.

hardWords.m: to show thoughts and feelings in words
the dry outer covering of seeds

289.title: The Seas, the Ships, and Everything That Perishes

paragraphs.text: The two seas that meet side by side have a barrier between them, so that neither of them crosses over into the other. From both of them come pearls and coral, beautiful treasures that people take out of the water. The ships, with their sails raised high in the sea like mountains, also belong to Allah, and they travel only by His permission. After each of these blessings, the refrain returns: "So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" The repeated question keeps reminding the reader that every one of these gifts comes from the same Lord.

Everyone living on the earth will one day perish and pass away. What will remain forever is the Face of the Lord, the Owner of Majesty and Honor. Nothing else lasts, but He continues without end. Every creature in the heavens and the earth asks Him for what it needs, and every day He is busy with some new matter, bringing about what He wills. Again the listeners are asked which of their Lord's favors they would deny.

Then the tone becomes more serious. Allah announces that He will soon turn His attention to the two important kinds of beings, jinn and mankind. They are challenged: if they are able to escape beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then let them try. However, they will never pass through except with authority from Allah. If they try, a flame of fire and smoke will be sent against them, and they will be unable to protect themselves. Each warning is followed by the same question about the Lord's favors, so the reader is reminded of the Lord's favors even in the middle of these warnings. Finally, the passage begins to describe the Day of Judgment, when the sky will be torn open and turn rose-red, like oil.

hardWords.m: a hard, colorful material formed in the sea
a line that is repeated many times
areas or parts of a large place

290.title: Two Fates: Scalding Water or Two Gardens

paragraphs.text: The refrain continues: "So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" On the Day when the sky is split open, no man or jinni will need to be questioned about his sins, because everything will already be clear. The criminals will be recognized by the marks on them, and they will be grabbed by their forelocks and their feet. It will be said that this is the Hell which the criminals used to deny. They will move back and forth between the Fire and scalding water that has been heated to the greatest degree. After each of these frightening scenes, the same question is asked again, so that the listener keeps thinking about his Lord's favors.

In contrast, for anyone who feared standing before his Lord, there will be two gardens. Such a person was aware, during his life, that one day he would stand before Allah, and this awareness guided his actions. His two gardens have wide, spreading branches. In each of them, two springs flow freely, and in each there are two kinds of every fruit. The people there will recline on beds lined with thick silk brocade, while the fruit of the two gardens hangs low, close enough to pick easily. Between each of these descriptions, the refrain comes back again and again: which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? The rhythm of the passage is very powerful. A short description is given, then the question is repeated, then another description follows. This pattern makes the reader stop after every single blessing and think about it, instead of rushing past it. In this way, the passage calls the reader to gratitude for every favor of his Lord, the Most Merciful.

hardWords.m: hair on the front of the head
thick cloth with raised designs, often of silk

291.title: Pure Companions and Two More Green Gardens

paragraphs.text: After each blessing, the familiar question returns: "So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" In the two gardens there will be women who keep their glances modest and lowered, whom no man or jinni has touched before. They are described as if they were rubies and coral, shining with beauty. Then comes a simple but deep question: is the reward for doing good anything other than good? This short verse sums up the whole idea of the passage. Those who did good will be repaid with good.

Below the first two gardens, there are two other gardens, slightly lower in rank. They are dark green in color, deep and rich in color. In each of them, two springs gush out with water. In both there are fruits, palm trees, and pomegranates, all of which are good to eat and pleasant to see. So this passage describes four gardens in all: two higher ones and two below them, each pair with its own springs and its own fruits. In these gardens there are also good and beautiful women. As before, every short description is followed by the same refrain, asking which of the Lord's favors anyone could deny. The constant repetition makes the reader feel the great number of blessings, one after another, as if they were being counted one by one. By the end of the passage, the answer to the repeated question seems obvious. No honest person could deny such favors, because they are so many, so clear, and so generous. The passage therefore invites the reader not only to admire these gardens, but also to thank Allah for His favors now, and to do good so that he may be among those who receive the reward of good.

hardWords.m: humble and decent, not showing off
to flow out quickly and strongly
hardWords.bn: উথলে ওঠা / ফোয়ারার মতো বের হওয়া

hardWords.m: round red fruits with many seeds
giving a lot, more than expected

292.title: The End of The Most Merciful and the Occurrence

paragraphs.text: In the gardens there are fair companions kept safely in pavilions, whom no man or jinni has touched before. The people of Paradise will recline on green cushions and beautiful, fine carpets. Between each of these images, the refrain is repeated once more: "So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" The surah then closes with words of praise. Blessed is the name of the Lord, the Owner of Majesty and Honor. After so many favors have been listed, the surah ends by turning the reader's attention back to the One who gave them all.

The next surah, called The Occurrence, begins by describing the Day of Judgment. When the great Occurrence finally takes place, no one will be able to deny it any longer. It will bring some people down low and raise others up high, on the Day when every matter is settled. The earth will be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains will be crushed into pieces until they become scattered dust in the air.

On that Day, people will be divided into three groups. The first group is the companions of the right, and the surah asks, in a way that shows their high status, who the companions of the right are. The second group is the companions of the left, and the same kind of question is asked about them, this time in a way that warns of their terrible state. The third group is the forerunners, those who were foremost, and they will be foremost again. The following verses go on to describe each of these three groups in detail, starting with those who are brought near.

hardWords.m: soft pillows for sitting or leaning
those who go ahead of others

293.title: Rewards of Those Brought Near to Allah

paragraphs.text: The forerunners are the ones who are brought near to Allah. They will live in the Gardens of Pleasure, and they will include a large group from the earlier peoples and a smaller number from the later peoples. In this way, the surah begins to describe in detail the first and highest of the three groups that were mentioned before.

These honored people will sit on thrones decorated with fine ornament, reclining on them and facing one another in friendship and comfort. Young servants who never grow old will move among them, carrying bowls, jugs, and a cup filled from a flowing spring. This drink will not give them any headache, nor will it make them lose their minds. They will also be offered any fruit they choose, and the meat of birds, whatever they desire. Nothing that they wish for will be kept away from them, and everything will be served to them with honor.

They will also have fair companions with large, beautiful eyes, who are like pearls that have been carefully protected and kept hidden. All of this is given to them as a reward for what they used to do in their lives. In those gardens, they will never hear foolish talk or any words that lead to sin. The only speech they hear will be the greeting of "Peace, peace." Their gardens are full of calm and respectful words.

After finishing the description of the forerunners, the surah turns to the second group. It asks again, in a way that raises their honor, who the companions of the right are. This question prepares the reader for the description of their reward, which is given in the verses that follow. Like the first group, they too will receive great blessings from their Lord.

hardWords.m: containers with handles for pouring drinks
a small part or fact; 'in detail' means fully

294.title: Companions of the Right and of the Left

paragraphs.text: The companions of the right will live among lote trees whose thorns have been removed, and among trees layered with fruit. They will enjoy shade that stretches far and wide, and water that is poured out freely. They will have fruit in great amount and variety. This fruit is never limited to one season, and it is never forbidden or kept away from them. They will rest on beds that are raised high, adding to their comfort and honor. Each part of this description shows a life free from hardship, where everything good is close at hand and easy to reach.

Allah has created the women of Paradise in a new creation, making them virgins, loving toward their husbands, and of the same age. All of this is for the companions of the right. This group will include a large company from the earlier peoples and a large company from the later peoples. So, unlike the forerunners, whose number from the later peoples is described as small, the companions of the right come in large numbers from both the earlier and the later generations.

Then the surah turns to the third group and asks, in a way that warns of their terrible state, who the companions of the left are. They will be in scorching fire and boiling water. Over them will be a shade made of black smoke. This shade is very different from the wide, pleasant shade enjoyed by the companions of the right, because it is neither cool nor beneficial in any way. It gives no rest and no relief. By placing these two scenes side by side, the passage makes the difference between the two groups very clear. One group enjoys shade, water, and fruit without end, while the other finds only fire, scalding water, and smoke. The contrast helps the reader understand how serious the final outcome is, and how much depends on the way a person lives in this world.

hardWords.m: women who have never been married or touched
the end of pain or worry
a clear difference between two things

295.title: Fate of the Deniers and the Power to Create

paragraphs.text: Before this punishment, the companions of the left lived in luxury and comfort. They kept insisting on the great sin, refusing to stop. They used to ask with doubt whether, after they had died and turned into dust and bones, they would truly be raised back to life. They even asked whether their forefathers from long ago would also be brought back.

The Prophet is told to answer them clearly. Both the earlier and the later peoples will be gathered together at the appointed time of a known Day. Then those who went astray and denied the truth will eat from the trees of zaqqum, filling their bellies with it. On top of that, they will drink scalding water, and they will drink it like thirsty camels that cannot stop drinking. This will be the place prepared for them on the Day of Recompense, the Day when every deed is repaid.

After describing these outcomes, the surah turns to logical reasoning. Allah created people, so why do they not believe in Him? He asks them to think about the drop of fluid from which human beings are formed. Is it they who create it, or is He the Creator? Allah has decreed death for everyone, and no one can overcome Him or escape His plan. He is fully able to change their forms and to create them again in a shape that they do not know. These questions are meant to make the deniers think carefully. If Allah was able to create them the first time from a simple drop, then bringing them back to life after death is not difficult for Him at all. In this way, the passage answers the doubt that the deniers expressed at the start of the day's reading, when they asked how dust and bones could possibly live again. The answer is found in their own creation, which they can see and understand, and which they did not make themselves.

hardWords.m: thinking in a clear, sensible way

296.title: Seeds, Water, Fire, and a Noble Qur'an

paragraphs.text: People already know how the first creation happened, so why do they not take a lesson from it? Allah then asks them to think about the seeds they plant in the ground. Is it they who make them grow, or is He the One who causes them to grow? If He wished, He could turn the crops into dry, broken pieces. Then the farmers would be left in shock, crying out that they are now in debt and that they have been deprived of everything they hoped for.

Next, the surah asks people to consider the water they drink every day. Did they bring it down from the clouds, or is Allah the One who sends it down? If He willed, He could make it bitter and unfit for drinking. So why are they not thankful for such a basic and necessary blessing?

People are also asked to think about the fire that they light. Did they produce the tree from which its wood comes, or is Allah the One who produced it? He has made fire a reminder of His power and a useful provision for travelers. Because all of these blessings come from Him alone, the Prophet is told to glorify the name of his Lord, the Most Great.

Allah then swears by the places where the stars set, and He states that this is a very great oath, if people only knew its true weight. The subject of this mighty oath is the Qur'an. It is a noble and honored Qur'an, kept safely in a well-protected Register. Each of these questions about seeds, water, and fire leads the reader toward the same conclusion: the One who controls food, drink, and fire is the One who sent down this noble Book, and He deserves to be praised.

hardWords.m: plants grown on farms for food
a sudden feeling of great surprise or upset
an official book where things are recorded

297.title: The Moment of Death and the True Certainty

paragraphs.text: No one touches the protected Register except those who have been purified. The Qur'an is a revelation sent down from the Lord of the worlds. Yet some people treat this message lightly and are indifferent to it. Instead of being thankful for the provision they receive, they respond by denying the One who gives it to them.

The surah then describes the moment of death in a very powerful way. When a dying person's soul reaches the throat, the people around him are only able to watch. At that moment, Allah's angels are closer to the dying person than those around him, but they cannot see the angels. Then a challenge is given. If people truly believe that they will not be held accountable, why do they not bring the soul back into the body? They should do it, if they are truthful. Of course, no one can do this, which shows how helpless human beings are before death.

After death, each person's fate depends on which of the three groups he belongs to. If the dead person was one of those brought near to Allah, he will have rest, blessings, and a garden of pleasure. If he was one of the companions of the right, he will be greeted with the words, "Peace be upon you, for you are one of the companions of the right." But if he was one of the deniers who had gone astray, his welcome will be scalding water and burning in Hellfire.

The passage ends with a firm statement: this is the absolute truth, the true certainty. In this way, the surah returns to the three groups that were introduced at its beginning, but now it connects their fate directly to the moment of death. The reader is reminded that every human being will face this moment, that no one can delay it, and that what follows it is not a guess or an assumption but a certain reality made clear by the Lord of the worlds.

hardWords.m: responsible and must answer for one's actions
not able to do anything to help oneself

298.title: Allah's Greatness, Spending, and the Light of Believers

paragraphs.text: The surah The Occurrence ends by telling the Prophet to glorify the name of his Lord, the Most Great.

The next surah opens by declaring that everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. The kingdom of the heavens and the earth is His; He gives life, causes death, and has power over everything. He is the First and the Last, the Highest and the Nearest, and He knows all things. He created the heavens and earth in six days and then rose above the Throne. He knows what enters and leaves the earth and the sky. He is with people wherever they are and sees all they do. He makes night pass into day and day into night, and He knows what lies within hearts.

People are called to believe in Allah and His Messenger and to spend from the wealth He has entrusted to them, since a great reward awaits those who believe and spend. Why not believe, when the Messenger invites them and Allah has their pledge? He sends clear verses to bring them out of darkness into light, because He is Kind and Merciful. Those who spent and fought before the conquest are higher in rank than those who did so later, though all are promised the best. Whoever lends Allah a good loan will have it multiplied.

On that Day, the believers' light will shine ahead of them and on their right, and they will receive good news of eternal gardens. The hypocrites will beg them to wait so they can borrow some light, but they will be told to go back and search for it. A wall with a door will separate them, with mercy inside and torment outside. They ruined themselves through doubt and false hopes, deceived by the Deceiver. No ransom will be accepted, and the Fire will be their home.
Believers are asked whether it is time for their hearts to become humble at Allah's remembrance, and not to harden like some earlier people of Scripture.

hardWords.m: given to someone to look after
people who show faith outwardly but hide disbelief
a payment to set someone free

299.title: The World's Short Pleasures and a Wide Garden

paragraphs.text: Allah revives the earth after it has died, and He makes His signs clear so that people may understand. Men and women who give charity, lending Allah a good loan, will have it multiplied and receive a noble reward. Those who believe in Allah and His messengers stand among the truthful and the martyrs, with their reward and their light, while the deniers belong to Hellfire. Worldly life is only play, distraction, decoration, boasting, and competing for more wealth and children. It is like rain that produces plants which please the farmers, then dry up, turn yellow, and become broken stalks. In the Hereafter there is severe punishment, but also forgiveness and approval from Allah. So people should race toward forgiveness and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth.

Every disaster that happens on earth or to people is written in a record before it occurs, and this is easy for Allah. Knowing this, people should not grieve too much over what they lose, nor become proud over what they receive. Allah does not love the arrogant and boastful, who are stingy and order others to be stingy. Allah is free of need and worthy of praise.

Allah sent His messengers with clear proofs, the Scripture, and the balance so people would live justly. He also sent down iron, which has great strength and many benefits. He gave prophethood and scripture to the descendants of Noah and Abraham, and later sent Jesus, son of Mary, with the Gospel. His followers were given compassion and mercy, but they invented monasticism and did not observe it properly. Believers who fear Allah will receive a double share of His mercy, a light to walk by, and forgiveness. All bounty is in Allah's hand.

Allah heard the woman who argued with the Prophet about her husband and complained to Allah. Men who declare thihar do not make their wives their mothers; the text calls this a false statement. To take it back, one must free a slave, or fast two months in a row, or feed sixty poor people.

hardWords.m: people who die for Allah's cause
not willing to give or spend
deep kindness for others who suffer

300.title: Secret Talks, Good Manners, and Allah's Party

paragraphs.text: Those who oppose Allah and His Messenger will be disgraced, just as earlier opponents were disgraced, and a humiliating punishment awaits the disbelievers. On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will inform them of all they did. He recorded everything, even what they forgot. He knows all that is in the heavens and the earth. Whenever three people talk secretly, He is the fourth, and when five talk, He is the sixth. Whether they are fewer or more, He is with them in knowledge wherever they are.

Some people were forbidden from secret talk, yet they returned to it, whispering about sin, aggression, and disobeying the Messenger. They even greeted him with words Allah does not use, and wondered why they were not punished. Hell is enough for them. Believers should never whisper about such evil, but only about righteousness and piety. Secret talk of this kind comes from Satan to sadden believers, though he cannot harm them without Allah's permission.

When believers are asked to make room in gatherings, they should do so, and Allah will make room for them. When told to rise, they should rise. Allah raises the believers and those given knowledge by degrees. Before speaking privately with the Messenger, they were told to give charity. Those who could not afford it were forgiven, and they were told to pray, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger.

Some people take as allies those with whom Allah is angry. They belong to neither side and knowingly swear false oaths, using them as a shield to block others from Allah's way. Their wealth and children will not help them. Even on the Day of Resurrection, they will swear falsely to Allah. Satan has overpowered them and made them forget Allah, so they are the party of Satan, the losers.
Those who oppose Allah will be among the most humbled. Allah has decreed that He and His messengers will surely prevail.

301.title: The Party of Allah and the Exiled Opponents

paragraphs.text: True believers in Allah and the Last Day will not love those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if those opponents are their own fathers, sons, brothers or relatives. Allah has written faith in their hearts and strengthened them with a spirit from Him. They will live forever in gardens with flowing rivers. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. They are the party of Allah, and that party is the one that succeeds.

A new surah opens: everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah, the Mighty and Wise. He drove the disbelievers among the People of the Scripture out of their homes at the first gathering. They thought their fortresses would protect them from Allah, but His decree came from where they never expected. He threw terror into their hearts, so they ruined their own houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. People with insight should take a lesson. Had Allah not decreed exile for them, He would have punished them in this world, and the Fire still awaits them, because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. Even the palm trees cut down or left standing were by Allah's permission.

The believers rode no horses or camels to gain the property Allah returned to His Messenger. It is for Allah, the Messenger, his relatives, orphans, the poor and the stranded traveler, so that wealth does not circulate only among the rich. Believers must take what the Messenger gives and avoid what he forbids. A share also goes to the poor emigrants driven from their homes, and to the people of Madinah who loved them and preferred them over themselves, even in hardship. Those saved from their own greed are successful. Later believers pray for those before them and ask Allah to remove any resentment from their hearts.

The hypocrites promised their disbelieving brothers to leave or fight beside them, but Allah declares them liars. They would run away instead. They fear the believers more than Allah, and although they seem united, their hearts are divided. They are like Satan, who tells a person to disbelieve and then abandons him, and both end up in the Fire forever.

hardWords.m: the power to see and understand deeply
to move around from person to person
a bitter, angry feeling toward someone
leaves someone alone with no help

302.title: Allah's Beautiful Names and Abraham's Example

paragraphs.text: The believers are told to fear Allah and to let every soul think carefully about what it has sent ahead for tomorrow, since Allah knows everything they do. They must not be like those who forgot Allah, so that He made them forget their own selves. The people of the Fire and the people of Paradise can never be equal, and only the people of Paradise truly succeed. If this Qur'an had been sent down on a mountain, the mountain would have bowed low and split apart out of fear of Allah. The surah then closes with a list of Allah's names. There is no deity except Him, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Entirely and Especially Merciful. He is the Sovereign, the Pure, the Giver of faith, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller and the Superior. He is the Creator, the Inventor and the Fashioner, and to Him belong the best names.

A new surah warns the believers not to take Allah's enemies as close friends and show them affection, because those enemies rejected the truth and drove the Prophet and the believers out simply for believing in Allah. Allah knows what they hide and what they reveal. If such enemies gained power over the believers, they would harm them with hands and tongues and wish them to disbelieve. On the Day of Resurrection, relatives and children will be of no benefit. Abraham and those with him are an excellent model. They openly separated themselves from their people and their idols until those people believed in Allah alone, while relying completely on their Lord. Yet Allah may one day place affection between the believers and some of their enemies, for He is Forgiving and Merciful.

Allah does not forbid kindness and fairness toward those who have not fought the believers because of religion or driven them from their homes. He only forbids taking as allies those who did fight and expel them. When believing women come as emigrants, the believers should test them, although Allah knows their faith best. If they are believers, they must not be sent back to the disbelievers, and fair arrangements must be made concerning what was spent on marriage. This is Allah's judgement.

hardWords.m: a feeling of love and liking
the one who gives everything its shape
to force someone to leave a place
people who leave their home to live elsewhere

303.title: Women's Pledge, Lines in Battle, and Ahmad

paragraphs.text: If a believer's wife leaves for the disbelievers, he should later be given the equivalent of what he had spent on her. When believing women come to the Prophet and pledge not to associate anything with Allah, not to steal, not to commit adultery, not to kill their children, not to invent slander, and not to disobey him in what is right, he should accept their pledge and ask Allah to forgive them. The surah ends by warning the believers not to befriend people with whom Allah is angry, since those people have lost all hope of the Hereafter.

The next surah opens with the glorification of Allah by everything in the heavens and the earth. It asks the believers why they say what they do not do, which is very hateful to Allah. In contrast, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in firm rows, standing together like a single solid building.

Moses once asked his people why they hurt him when they knew he was Allah's messenger, and when they turned away, Allah turned their hearts away too. Jesus, the son of Mary, told the Children of Israel that he was Allah's messenger, confirming the Torah before him and bringing good news of a messenger after him named Ahmad. But when this messenger came with clear proofs, they called it obvious magic. No one is more unjust than a person who invents lies about Allah while being invited to Islam. Such people want to put out Allah's light with their mouths, but Allah will complete His light even though the disbelievers hate it. He sent His Messenger with guidance and the true religion to make it prevail over all religions.

Allah offers the believers a profitable trade that will rescue them from a painful punishment: to believe in Allah and His Messenger and to strive in His cause with their wealth and their lives. In return He will forgive their sins and give them pleasant homes in everlasting gardens, along with help from Allah and a victory that is near. The believers are asked to be supporters of Allah, just as the disciples of Jesus answered his call. Some of the Children of Israel believed and others disbelieved, and Allah supported the believers until they won.

hardWords.m: a false statement that hurts someone's name
praising someone as great and perfect
to win and be stronger than others

304.title: Friday Prayer and the Masks of the Hypocrites

paragraphs.text: Everything in the heavens and on the earth glorifies Allah, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Mighty and the Wise. He sent to an unlettered people a Messenger from among themselves, who recites His verses to them, purifies them and teaches them the Book and wisdom, although before that they were clearly lost. This favor also reaches others who have not yet joined them. It is Allah's bounty, which He gives to whomever He wills.

Those who were given the Torah but did not carry out its teaching are compared to a donkey loaded with heavy books that it cannot benefit from. How bad is the example of people who deny Allah's signs! If some Jews claim that they alone are Allah's allies, they are challenged to wish for death if they are truthful. They will never wish for it, because of the deeds they have sent ahead. The death they run from will certainly meet them, and then they will return to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, who will tell them what they did.

When the call to prayer is made on Friday, the believers should hurry to the remembrance of Allah and leave their business, because that is better for them. Once the prayer is finished, they may spread through the land, seek Allah's bounty and remember Him often. Yet some people, seeing a trade deal or some entertainment, rushed toward it and left the Prophet standing. What Allah holds is far better than any amusement or business, and He is the best provider.

The next surah exposes the hypocrites. They come to the Prophet and swear that he is Allah's Messenger, and although Allah knows he truly is, He declares that the hypocrites are lying. They use their oaths as a shield while turning people away from Allah's path. They believed and then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed. Their appearance may impress you and their speech may attract you, yet they are like pieces of wood propped against a wall, and they fear that every shout is aimed at them. They are the real enemy, so beware of them. When they are invited to let the Messenger ask forgiveness for them, they turn their heads away in arrogance. Whether he asks or not, Allah will never forgive them.

hardWords.m: not able to read or write
shows the hidden truth about someone
something used for protection or to hide behind
held up by leaning on something

305.title: Spend Before Death and the Day of Loss

paragraphs.text: The hypocrites tell others not to spend on the companions of the Messenger so that they will scatter, not realizing that the treasures of the heavens and the earth belong to Allah. They also boast that when they return to Madinah, the more powerful will drive out the weaker. But all honor belongs to Allah, His Messenger and the believers. The believers are warned not to let their wealth and children distract them from remembering Allah, since those who do so are the losers. They should spend from what Allah has given them before death arrives, when a person might beg for a short delay so that he could give charity and become righteous. Allah never delays a soul once its appointed time has come.

A new surah begins with everything in creation glorifying Allah, to whom belong all rule and all praise. He created human beings, yet some of them disbelieve while others believe. He created the heavens and the earth with truth, shaped people and made their forms beautiful, and all will return to Him. He knows what they hide and what they show, and even what lies within their hearts. Earlier nations disbelieved and tasted the bad result of their choices. When their messengers brought clear proofs, they asked whether mere human beings could guide them, and so they turned away. Allah did not need them at all, for He is Free of need and Praiseworthy.

The disbelievers insist that they will never be raised again, but the Prophet is told to swear by his Lord that they certainly will, and that they will be informed of their deeds, which is easy for Allah. Therefore people should believe in Allah, His Messenger and the Qur'an. The Day of Gathering will be a day of mutual loss and gain, when believers who did good will have their sins removed and enter eternal gardens, while those who denied Allah's verses will live in the Fire forever. No disaster happens without Allah's permission, and He guides the heart of whoever believes. The duty of the Messenger is only to deliver the message clearly.

hardWords.m: to take attention away from something
to say something strongly and firmly

306.title: Trial of Family and the Rules of Divorce

paragraphs.text: There is no deity except Allah, so the believers should rely on Him. Some of their spouses and children may act as enemies to them, so they must be careful; yet if they pardon, overlook and forgive, Allah too is Forgiving and Merciful. Wealth and children are only a test, while Allah holds a great reward. Believers should fear Allah as much as they can, listen, obey and spend, for this is better for them, and whoever is saved from his own greed is truly successful. If they lend Allah a good loan, He will multiply it and forgive them, because He is Most Appreciative and Patient.

The next surah gives guidance about divorce. Men should divorce at the start of the waiting period, count it carefully and fear Allah. Women should not be driven out of their homes during this time, nor should they leave, unless they commit clear immorality. These are Allah's limits, and whoever crosses them wrongs himself, for perhaps Allah will bring about a new situation afterward. When the term is nearly over, the husband should either keep his wife kindly or part from her kindly, and two just witnesses should be present. Whoever fears Allah, He will make a way out for him and provide for him from where he never expected. Allah is enough for anyone who trusts Him.

For women who no longer menstruate, or who have not yet menstruated, the waiting period is three months, and for pregnant women it lasts until they give birth. Allah makes matters easy for whoever fears Him and increases his reward. Divorced women must be housed according to the husband's means and must not be harmed. If they nurse the child, they should be paid fairly. Each person spends according to what Allah has given, and Allah will bring ease after hardship.

Many towns rebelled against the command of their Lord and His messengers, so Allah held them to a strict account, and their final outcome was loss. People of understanding should therefore fear Him. He has sent down a reminder and a Messenger who recites clear verses, in order to bring the believers out of darkness into light and admit them into gardens forever.

hardWords.m: to choose not to notice a mistake
the money and resources a person has
refused to obey and fought against

307.title: Lessons for the Prophet's Household and Sincere Repentance

paragraphs.text: Allah created seven heavens and a similar number of earths, and His command comes down among them, so that people may know that He has power over everything and that His knowledge surrounds all things.

A new surah gently asks the Prophet why he forbade himself something Allah had made lawful, in order to please his wives, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. Allah has already given a way to release oneself from such oaths. The Prophet once told one of his wives a secret, but she shared it, and Allah informed him. When he mentioned part of it to her, she asked who had told him, and he replied that the Knowing and Aware had informed him. The two wives are invited to repent, since their hearts had leaned away. If they support each other against him, then Allah, Gabriel, the righteous believers and the angels are his helpers. If he divorced them, Allah could give him better wives who are believing, obedient, repentant and devoted to worship.

Believers must protect themselves and their families from a Fire fueled by people and stones, guarded by stern angels who never disobey Allah. On that Day the disbelievers will be told not to make excuses. Believers are called to sincere repentance, so that Allah may erase their sins and admit them to gardens. Their light will shine before them, and they will pray for it to be completed. The Prophet is told to strive firmly against the disbelievers and hypocrites.

The wives of Noah and Lot are examples for the disbelievers: although married to righteous servants, they betrayed them, and their husbands could not save them from the Fire. The wife of Pharaoh is an example for the believers, for she asked Allah for a house near Him in Paradise and for rescue from Pharaoh and the wrongdoers. Mary, daughter of 'Imran, guarded her chastity and believed in her Lord's words.

The next surah praises Allah, in whose hand is all rule. He created death and life to test who is best in deeds. He made seven heavens in layers, and however often you look, you will find no flaw, and your tired eyes will return humbled.

hardWords.m: keeping oneself pure from unlawful relations

308.title: The Raging Fire and the Signs of Mercy

paragraphs.text: Allah has decorated the nearest sky with stars, which He has also made into missiles against the devils, and He has prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze. Those who reject their Lord will face Hell, a terrible place to end up. When they are thrown into it, they will hear its dreadful roaring breath as it boils, and it will nearly burst with fury. Each time a group is thrown in, its keepers will ask whether a warner never came to them. They will admit that a warner did come, but they denied him and claimed that Allah had revealed nothing and that he was badly mistaken. They will wish that they had listened or used their minds, so that they would not be among the people of the Fire. They will confess their sin, but they will be kept far away from mercy.

In contrast, those who fear their Lord without seeing Him will receive forgiveness and a great reward. Whether people hide their words or speak them openly, Allah knows what is inside their hearts. How could the One who created not know, when He is the Subtle and the Aware?

Allah made the earth smooth and easy for people, so that they can walk through its paths and eat from His provision, and to Him they will be raised. Yet people should not feel safe from Him. He could make the earth swallow them while it shakes, or He could send a storm of stones upon them, and then they would understand how serious His warning was. Earlier nations denied the truth, and His rejection of them was severe.

Have they never looked at the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings? Nothing keeps them up in the air except the Most Merciful, who sees everything. Who else could act as an army to help people besides the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are only fooling themselves. And who could feed them if He held back His provision? Still they continue in pride and in running away from the truth.

hardWords.m: objects thrown or shot at a target
to admit that one did wrong
knowing even the smallest, hidden things

309.title: Hearing, Sight, Water, and the Prophet's Character

paragraphs.text: The surah asks a powerful question: who is better guided, a person who stumbles along with his face to the ground, or one who walks upright on a straight path? The Prophet is told to remind people that it is Allah who brought them into being and gave them hearing, sight and hearts, yet they show very little gratitude. He is also the one who spread them across the earth, and to Him they will all be gathered on the final Day.

The disbelievers mockingly ask when this promised Day will come, if the Prophet is telling the truth. He is told to answer that its knowledge is with Allah alone, and that his own task is only to warn them clearly. However, when they actually see it coming close, the faces of the disbelievers will become dark with distress, and they will be told that this is exactly what they used to demand so impatiently.

The Prophet is told to ask them to think carefully. Whether Allah causes him and his companions to die, or shows them mercy, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment? The believers have faith in the Most Merciful and depend on Him, and soon everyone will know who is clearly lost. Finally he asks them another question: if their water sank deep into the ground, who could bring them fresh flowing water? The answer, of course, is no one except Allah.

The next surah begins with the letter Nun and an oath by the pen and by what people write with it. Allah assures the Prophet that, by the grace of his Lord, he is not insane, as his enemies claim. He will have a reward that never ends, and he possesses a truly great moral character. Soon he will see, and his opponents will also see, which side is really affected by madness. His Lord knows best who has wandered from His path and who is rightly guided, so the Prophet should not obey those who deny the truth, however much they press him.

hardWords.m: tells someone firmly so they stop worrying
mad; not having a healthy mind

310.title: The Slanderer and the Owners of the Garden

paragraphs.text: The surah continues to guide the Prophet in dealing with those who reject the message. The deniers would like him to compromise a little, so that they could also soften their position toward him. But he is told firmly not to obey a certain kind of person, whose bad qualities are listed one after another. This person is worthless and swears oaths constantly. He mocks others and walks around spreading harmful gossip. He blocks good from reaching people, goes beyond the limits and is full of sin. He is cruel, and on top of that he has a doubtful claim to his place among his people. He behaves this way only because he owns wealth and has many sons. Whenever Allah's verses are recited to him, he dismisses them as old stories of earlier peoples. Allah declares that He will brand him on the nose, as a mark of disgrace.

Allah then explains that He is testing these deniers just as He once tested the owners of a garden. These owners swore that they would harvest its fruit early in the morning, and they did not add any exception such as "if Allah wills." While they were sleeping, a disaster from their Lord came over the garden during the night. By morning it looked as if it had already been completely harvested, with nothing left on the trees.

Unaware of what had happened, the owners called out to one another at dawn. They told each other to go out early to their crop if they really wanted to collect the fruit. So they set off together, whispering quietly among themselves so that no one would overhear their plan. They agreed that not a single poor person should be allowed to enter the garden that day and ask them for a share. They left early with strong determination, fully believing that they had the power to carry out their plan exactly as they wished. They did not know that their Lord had already decided the matter while they slept, and that the garden they were rushing toward was no longer what they expected to find.

hardWords.m: to give up part of what you believe to agree
talk about other people's private matters
a strong will to do something

311.title: The Ruined Garden and Questions for the Deniers

paragraphs.text: When the owners finally reached their garden and saw that it had been completely destroyed, they first thought they had lost their way. Then they looked again, realized the truth and cried that they had been deprived of everything they had hoped to gather. The most balanced person among them reminded them that he had told them to glorify Allah. At once they declared that their Lord is exalted and admitted that they had been wrongdoers. They turned to one another and began to blame each other. Then they cried out in sorrow that they had truly gone beyond the limits. They expressed hope that their Lord would give them something better in its place, and said that they now turned to Him with longing. Such is the punishment in this world, but the punishment of the Hereafter is far greater, if only people knew.

For the righteous, there are Gardens of Pleasure with their Lord. Allah asks whether He would treat those who submit to Him in the same way as the criminals. What is wrong with these deniers, and how do they make such judgments? Do they have a scripture which teaches them that they will get whatever they choose? Or have they received oaths from Allah, lasting until the Day of Resurrection, that they will get whatever they decide? The Prophet is told to ask them which of them will guarantee such a claim. Or do they have partners beside Allah? If so, let them bring those partners, if they are truthful. Each question leaves the deniers without an answer, because they have no book, no promise from Allah and no partners who could support their claim. Their hopes are built on nothing but their own wishes.
A scene from the Last Day follows. On the Day when the shin will be uncovered, people will be called to bow down in prostration. However, the disbelievers will not be able to do so.

hardWords.m: decisions or opinions about what is right
to promise firmly that something is true
bowing down with the forehead on the ground

312.title: Patience Like Jonah and the Inevitable Reality

paragraphs.text: On the Last Day, the eyes of the disbelievers will be lowered and humiliation will cover them, because in this life they were invited to bow down in prayer while they were healthy and able, and they refused. Allah tells the Prophet to leave the matter of those who deny the Qur'an to Him. He will lead them step by step toward their punishment in ways they do not notice, and He will give them time, because His plan is firm and cannot fail. The surah then asks two questions. Is the Prophet asking them for some payment, so that they feel weighed down by debt? Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, which they are able to write down? Clearly, neither is true.

The Prophet is told to wait patiently for his Lord's decision and not to be like the companion of the fish, who called out to his Lord while he was full of distress. If a favor from his Lord had not reached him, he would have been thrown onto a bare, empty shore while blamed for his action. Instead, his Lord chose him and placed him among the righteous. The disbelievers stare at the Prophet so sharply when they hear the message that their looks could almost make him slip, and they call him mad. Yet the Qur'an is nothing other than a reminder for all the worlds.

A new surah opens with a name for the Last Day: the Inevitable Reality. It asks three times what this Reality is, and what could make anyone understand it, which shows how great and serious it is. Then it recalls two ancient nations, Thamud and 'Aad, who denied the Striking Calamity. Thamud were destroyed by an overwhelming blast. 'Aad were destroyed by a screaming, violent wind, which Allah sent against them for seven nights and eight days without stopping. Anyone watching would have seen the people lying fallen on the ground like the hollow trunks of palm trees.

hardWords.m: certain to happen; cannot be avoided

313.title: The Blowing of the Horn and Two Records

paragraphs.text: The surah asks whether anyone can now see any trace remaining of those destroyed nations, whose homes once stood strong. None of them is left. Pharaoh, the peoples before him and the overturned cities also committed sin and disobeyed the messenger sent by their Lord, so Allah seized them with an extremely severe grip. When the flood waters rose high, Allah carried the ancestors of humanity in the sailing ship. He did this so that the event would become a reminder, and so that ears which listen with attention would remember it and keep it.

The surah then describes the end of the world. The Horn will be blown, and a single blast will be enough. The earth and the mountains will be lifted up and crushed flat with one blow. On that Day, the great Event will take place. The sky will split apart, because on that Day it will be weak and fragile. The angels will stand at its edges, and eight of them will carry the Throne of the Lord above them. On that Day, every person will be presented for judgement, and not one secret will stay hidden, no matter how carefully it was concealed before.

Whoever receives his record in his right hand will be filled with joy and will say to others, "Here, come and read my record!" He will explain that during his life he was always sure that he would one day meet his account and stand before his Lord. He will enjoy a pleasant, satisfying life in a high and lofty garden, where clusters of fruit hang low and are easy to pick. The people there will be told to eat and drink happily, as a reward for the good deeds they sent ahead in the days that have passed.

But whoever receives his record in his left hand will speak with deep regret. He will cry that he wishes he had never been given his record at all. His sorrow on that Day stands in sharp contrast to the joy of the one who received his record in his right hand.

hardWords.m: a very small sign that something was there
people in your family who lived long ago

314.title: Regret of the Lost and the Noble Word

paragraphs.text: The person who receives his record in his left hand will continue to cry out in regret. He will wish that he had never learned what his account contained. He will wish that his death had been the final end, so that he never had to be raised again. He will complain that his wealth has not helped him in the least, and that all his power and authority have disappeared from him. The wealth and power that he trusted and relied on during his life, and that made him feel safe in this world, will be of no use to him at all on that Day.

Then the command will be given: seize him and put chains on him. Drive him into the Hellfire, and then bind him in a chain seventy cubits long. The reason is made clear. He did not believe in Allah, the Most Great, and he did not encourage others to feed the poor. Therefore on that Day he will have no loyal friend there to help him. He will have no food except the discharge from wounds, which only the sinners will eat. This fearful description shows the result of rejecting faith and ignoring the needs of the poor.

Allah then swears by everything that people can see and by everything that they cannot see. By this oath He declares that the Qur'an is truly the word of a noble Messenger. It is not the speech of a poet, although the deniers claimed it was, and yet they believe very little. It is not the speech of a fortune-teller either, and yet they reflect very little. In this way the surah rejects the false labels that the disbelievers placed on the Qur'an and on the one who brought it. The noble Messenger is only the one who delivers the words, and the people who heard him had every reason to believe and to remember, if only they had been willing to listen with open hearts.

hardWords.m: power to control and give orders
an old measure of length, about the length of a forearm
liquid that comes out of a wound
a person who claims to know the future

315.title: A Revelation Beyond Doubt and the Long Day

paragraphs.text: The Qur'an is a revelation sent down from the Lord of the worlds. To show how serious this is, Allah explains what would happen if the Prophet had invented any false sayings and claimed they came from Him. Allah would have seized him by the right hand and then cut his main artery, and no one among the people would have been able to stop Him. This makes it clear that the message is not the Prophet's own invention, but comes from Allah, and that every word he delivered was exactly what he received from his Lord.

The Qur'an is a reminder for those who are conscious of Allah. Allah knows well that some people deny it, and on the Last Day it will become a source of deep regret for the disbelievers. It is the certain truth, beyond any doubt, and nothing that the deniers say can change that fact. Therefore the Prophet is told to glorify the name of his Lord, the Most Great. With this command the surah comes to its end, leaving the reader with a call to praise Allah.

A new surah begins by mentioning someone who asked for a punishment that is sure to happen. It will fall upon the disbelievers, and nobody can push it away. It comes from Allah, the Owner of the ways of ascent. The angels and the Spirit rise up to Him on a Day whose length is fifty thousand years. Because of this, the Prophet is told to be patient with a beautiful, graceful patience that does not complain. The disbelievers think that this Day is far away and will never come, but Allah sees it as near. The difference between how they see it and how Allah sees it is a warning: what seems distant to human beings may in fact be very close. The believer is therefore asked to remain calm and patient, trusting that Allah's promise will certainly come at its time.

hardWords.m: a message sent down from Allah
a big tube that carries blood from the heart

316.title: No Ransom on That Day and the Restless Soul

paragraphs.text: The surah continues to describe the Day that the disbelievers think is far away. On that Day the sky will look like dark, murky oil, and the mountains will become as light and loose as tufts of wool. No close friend will ask about another friend, even though they will be able to see each other clearly. Each person will be busy with his own situation. The criminal will wish that he could pay a ransom to escape the punishment of that Day. He would gladly offer his own children, his wife and his brother, the relatives who used to shelter and protect him, and even everyone on the whole earth, if only that could save him from what is coming.

But this wish will never be granted. What awaits him is the Flame of Hell, a fire that strips away the skin. It calls out to the person who turned his back on the truth and walked away from obedience to Allah. It calls the one who gathered wealth, stored it up and held it tightly, refusing to use it in the right way. The very things he spent his life collecting will not help him in the slightest, once he stands before the Flame that calls him.

Next the surah describes human nature. Man was created anxious and restless. When something bad touches him, he becomes impatient and complains loudly. When something good touches him, he becomes stingy and keeps it for himself instead of sharing it with others. However, there is an important exception to this description. It does not apply to those who pray regularly and remain constant in their prayer, never giving it up. It also does not apply to those who recognize that, in their wealth, there is a known and fixed right that belongs to others. Such people are not ruled by anxiety and greed, and the following ayahs continue to list their good qualities in more detail.

hardWords.m: not willing to give or spend
not able to stay calm or still

317.title: Qualities of Those Honored in the Gardens

paragraphs.text: The list of good qualities continues. The known right in their wealth is given to the one who asks for help and to the one who is in need but does not ask. These believers also have firm faith in the Day of Recompense, when everyone will be paid back for their deeds. They live with a healthy fear of their Lord's punishment, because they understand that nobody can feel completely safe from it. They do not treat the warning lightly or assume that they are already saved. Instead, they hold on to both hope and fear, and this keeps them careful in what they say and do.

They guard their private parts and keep themselves chaste, except with their wives or those whom their right hands possess, and for this they are not blamed. Anyone who seeks anything beyond that has crossed the limits set by Allah. The believers also look after the trusts placed in their care and keep their promises faithfully. They stand firm and honest when they give testimony, never changing the truth. Finally, they carefully protect their prayers and perform them properly at their times, without neglecting them or treating them as unimportant. It is worth noticing that this description both begins and ends with prayer, which shows how central prayer is to their lives. Such people will live in gardens, surrounded by honor and respect.

The surah then turns to the disbelievers around the Prophet. What is wrong with them, that they hurry toward him and gather in scattered groups on his right and on his left? Does every one of them really hope to enter a garden of pleasure without believing or doing good? Certainly not. Allah created them from a substance that they know well, so they have no reason to be proud. He swears by the Lord of all the places where the sun rises and sets that He is fully able to replace them with people better than they are, and that nothing can ever stop Him or defeat His will.

hardWords.m: in a loyal and honest way
a statement that something is true, given as a witness
the material something is made of

318.title: Noah Calls His People Day and Night

paragraphs.text: The surah ends with a final instruction. The Prophet is told to leave the disbelievers to their empty talk and their games, and to let them enjoy themselves for a while, until they finally meet the Day they have been promised. On that Day they will come out of their graves quickly, rushing forward as if they were racing toward an idol set up for them. Their eyes will be lowered in shame, and humiliation will cover them. That is the very Day they were warned about again and again.

A new surah tells the story of Noah. Allah sent him to his people with the instruction to warn them before a painful punishment reached them. Noah obeyed. He stood before his people and told them plainly that he had come to them as a clear warner, hiding nothing of the message. He called them to worship Allah, to fear Him and to obey him as their messenger. If they did so, Allah would forgive their sins and allow them to live until a time already fixed. But he also reminded them that when the time set by Allah arrives, it can never be delayed, if only they understood.

Later Noah turned to his Lord in prayer and described his long struggle with his people. He said that he had called his people night and day, but his call only made them run further away. Every time he invited them so that Allah might forgive them, they pushed their fingers into their ears, wrapped themselves in their clothes, refused stubbornly and showed great arrogance. He tried every method. He called them openly in public, he made announcements, and he also spoke to them privately in secret. He told them to ask forgiveness from their Lord, because He is always ready to forgive. In return, Allah would send them plentiful rain from the sky, increase their wealth and children, and give them gardens and rivers. Noah then asked them why they did not show Allah the respect and greatness He deserves, when He had created them in stages, one after another.

hardWords.m: an image or object that people worship
an order or guidance telling what to do
public statements to tell people something
more than enough; in large amounts

319.title: Noah's Final Prayer and the Jinn Who Listened

paragraphs.text: Noah continued to point his people toward the signs of Allah. He asked them whether they had not noticed how Allah created seven heavens in layers, one above another. He placed the moon among them as a light and made the sun a shining lamp. Allah made human beings grow from the earth like plants, and He will return them into it and then bring them out again on the Day of Resurrection. He also spread the earth out wide like a carpet, so that people could travel along its broad paths and roads.

Yet Noah's people rejected all of this. Noah told his Lord that they had disobeyed him and followed leaders whose wealth and children only increased them in loss. These leaders made a huge plot and told the people never to abandon their idols, naming Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr. They had already led many people astray. Noah asked Allah to let the wrongdoers only increase in error. Because of their sins, they were drowned and then entered into the Fire, and they found no helpers at all besides Allah.

Noah prayed that Allah would not leave a single disbeliever living on the earth. He explained that if they were left, they would mislead Allah's servants and would only bring up children who were wicked and stubborn in disbelief. Then he asked forgiveness for himself, his parents, everyone who entered his house as a believer, and all believing men and women, and he asked that the wrongdoers receive nothing but destruction.

The next surah begins with the Prophet being told to announce something revealed to him: a group of jinn listened to the Qur'an. They said that they had heard an amazing recitation which guides to the right way, so they believed in it and promised never to associate anyone with their Lord. They also declared that the majesty of their Lord is high above everything, and that He has not taken any wife or son.

hardWords.m: levels placed one on top of another
a secret plan to do something bad
reading aloud, especially of the Qur'an

320.title: What the Jinn Discovered and Declared

paragraphs.text: The jinn who listened to the Qur'an continued to speak among themselves. They admitted that the foolish one among them used to say outrageous things about Allah that went far beyond the truth. They had assumed that neither human beings nor jinn would ever dare to tell a lie about Allah, so they had believed what they heard. They also mentioned that some men used to seek protection from certain jinn, but this only increased those men in burden and fear. Those men, like some of the jinn, had thought that Allah would never send anyone as a messenger.

The jinn described how things had changed in the sky. They had tried to reach the heaven, but they found it full of powerful guards and burning flames. In the past they used to sit in certain places up there in order to overhear, but now anyone who tries to listen finds a blazing flame waiting to strike him. Because of this change, they confessed that they did not know whether harm was intended for the people of the earth, or whether their Lord intended to guide them to the right path.

The jinn were honest about themselves. Some of them are righteous, they said, while others are not, and they have followed different paths. They had become certain that they could never defeat Allah on earth, nor escape from Him by running away. When they heard the guidance, they believed in it, and whoever believes in his Lord need not fear any loss or injustice. Some of them have submitted to Allah, and those have searched for and found the right course. But those who are unjust will become fuel for Hell.

Allah also revealed that if people had kept firmly to the straight path, He would have given them plentiful water and provision, in order to test them through it. Whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord will be put into a punishment that keeps growing harder. The places of prayer belong to Allah, so no one should be called upon alongside Him. When the Servant of Allah stood up to pray, the crowds nearly pressed upon him in a tight mass. The Prophet is told to say that he calls only upon his Lord and associates no one with Him.

hardWords.m: material that is burned in a fire

321.title: Knower of the Unseen and Rising at Night

paragraphs.text: The Prophet is told to make his position clear to the people. He must say that he has no power either to harm them or to guide them by his own will. No one could protect him from Allah if he disobeyed, and he could find no place of safety except with Him. His only role is to convey what comes from Allah and to deliver His messages. Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger will face the fire of Hell, remaining there forever. The disbelievers will continue in their ways until they actually see what they were promised. Only then will they realize who is truly weaker in supporters and fewer in number.

The Prophet is also told to say that he does not know whether the promised punishment is near, or whether his Lord has set a longer time before it comes. Allah alone is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not reveal His secrets to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has chosen and approved. Even then, He sends guards in front of that messenger and behind him, so that it becomes known that the messengers have truly delivered their Lord's messages. Allah surrounds everything they have with His knowledge, and He has counted every single thing precisely.

A new surah addresses the Prophet as the one who has wrapped himself in his garments. He is told to stand in prayer at night, except for a small part of it: perhaps half of the night, or a little less than half, or a little more. During this prayer he should recite the Qur'an slowly and carefully, with measured recitation. Allah is about to give him a heavy and weighty message. Prayer during the night is more effective in bringing the heart and tongue together, and words spoken then are more fitting and clear. During the day he has long hours of busy work. So he should remember the name of his Lord and devote himself to Him completely. Allah is the Lord of the East and the West, and there is no deity except Him, so the Prophet should take Him as the One who manages all his affairs.

hardWords.m: to pass a message to others
to give fully to someone or something

322.title: Patience, Easier Night Prayer, and Arise and Warn

paragraphs.text: The Prophet is told to bear with patience what the disbelievers say, and to stay away from them in a gracious way without arguing. Allah tells him to leave the deniers who enjoy comfortable lives to Him, and to give them a little time. With Allah there are heavy chains and a burning fire for them, along with food that chokes and a painful punishment. That will happen on the Day when the earth and the mountains shake violently, and the mountains become like heaps of loose sand pouring down.

Allah has sent a Messenger to the people as a witness over them, just as He once sent a messenger to Pharaoh. Pharaoh disobeyed that messenger, so Allah seized him with a crushing grip. How then can the disbelievers protect themselves from a Day so terrible that it will turn children's hair white? On that Day the sky will break apart, and Allah's promise will certainly be fulfilled. This is a reminder, so whoever wishes may take a path to his Lord.

Allah knows that the Prophet and a group of his companions stand in prayer for nearly two thirds of the night, sometimes half of it or a third of it. Allah measures the night and the day exactly. He knew that they would not be able to keep up such long prayer, so He turned to them with mercy and told them to recite whatever is easy from the Qur'an. He knew that some would be sick, some would travel to seek His bounty, and some would fight in His cause. So they should recite what is easy, establish prayer, give zakah and lend Allah a good loan. Every good deed they send ahead will be found with Allah, better and greater in reward. They should seek His forgiveness, for He is Forgiving and Merciful.

The next surah calls the Prophet as the one covered in a cloak. He is told to rise and warn, to glorify his Lord, to keep his clothing pure, to stay away from uncleanness, and not to do favors for others in the hope of getting more in return.

323.title: The Trumpet and the Man Who Turned Away

paragraphs.text: The list of instructions given to the Prophet ends with one more command. He is told to be patient for the sake of his Lord, whatever difficulties he may face and whatever the people may say to him. Then the surah turns to the future. When the trumpet is blown, that Day will be extremely hard. For the disbelievers in particular, it will not be easy in any way at all, and there will be no relief for them on that Day. This short warning prepares the reader for the story that follows, which describes a man who heard the message clearly and still rejected it.

Allah tells the Prophet to leave to Him the man whom He created alone, with nothing. Allah then gave this man wide and plentiful wealth, and sons who stayed close beside him. He smoothed his life and made everything easy and comfortable for him. Yet even after all these blessings, the man still greedily wanted Allah to give him more. Allah answers firmly that this will not happen, because the man has been stubbornly hostile toward Allah's verses. Instead of more favors, he will be made to climb a hard and exhausting path of torment.

The surah describes the man's behavior very closely, step by step, almost as if the reader were watching him. When he heard the message, he thought carefully and planned what he would say about it. Allah condemns him for the way he planned, and then condemns him once again, because his plan was meant to oppose the truth. He looked around once more and considered the matter again. Then his face changed: he frowned and scowled with displeasure. Finally, he turned his back on the message and behaved with arrogance, refusing to accept what he had heard. His careful thinking did not lead him to faith; it only led him to pride. His story shows how a person can receive many gifts from Allah, hear His verses with full understanding, and still choose to turn away from them.

hardWords.m: a horn that is blown to make a loud sound
pulled the face into an angry look

324.title: Saqar, Its Nineteen Keepers, and a Warning

paragraphs.text: The man who turned away in arrogance finally gave his verdict about the Qur'an. He claimed that it was nothing but magic copied from others, and nothing more than the words of a human being. In response, Allah declares that He will throw him into Saqar. The surah then asks what could make anyone understand what Saqar really is. It is a fire that leaves nothing remaining and lets nothing escape untouched. It scorches and blackens the skin completely. Over it are nineteen guardians appointed to watch over it.

Allah explains that the keepers of the Fire are angels, and that He has mentioned their number only as a test for the disbelievers. Through it, those who were given the Scripture can become convinced, and the believers can grow stronger in faith. Neither the People of the Scripture nor the believers should have any doubt about it. At the same time, those with hypocrisy in their hearts and the disbelievers will mockingly ask what Allah means by such an example. In this way Allah lets go astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. Nobody knows the full number of the soldiers of the Lord except Him, and the description of the Fire is simply a reminder for humanity.

Then comes a firm denial of the disbelievers' claims, followed by several oaths. Allah swears by the moon, by the night as it passes away, and by the morning as it grows bright. He declares that the Fire is one of the greatest of all calamities. It stands as a clear warning to humanity, to every person among them who chooses either to move forward toward good or to fall behind. The choice is placed before each individual.

Every soul will be held responsible and kept in pledge for what it has earned through its own deeds. The only exception will be the companions of the right hand, those who receive their record in their right hands. They will be living in gardens, comfortable and safe, and they will ask one another questions about the criminals and what happened to them.

hardWords.m: people who watch over and protect
fully sure that something is true

325.title: Why They Entered Saqar and the Fleeing Donkeys

paragraphs.text: The people of the gardens will ask the criminals what brought them into Saqar. The criminals will give four answers. First, they will say that they were not among those who prayed. Second, they did not feed the poor. Third, they used to join others in empty, useless talk, mocking the truth along with those who mocked it. Fourth, they used to deny the Day of Recompense. They continued living in this careless way, without changing, until the certainty finally came to them and it was too late. On that Day, the intercession of any intercessor will not help them at all, no matter who tries to speak for them.

The surah asks what is wrong with these people, that they turn away from the reminder. Their behavior is compared to frightened donkeys running wildly away from a lion. They do not stop to think or listen; they simply flee from the message. In fact, each one of them wishes that he personally would be handed open scriptures of his own before he believes. But this demand is rejected. The true problem is not a lack of proof. The real reason is that they do not fear the Hereafter.

The Qur'an is certainly a reminder. Whoever wishes may remember it and take benefit from it. Yet no one will remember except if Allah wills. He alone deserves to be feared, and He alone is worthy to grant forgiveness. With these words the surah closes, placing before the reader both a serious warning and an open door to forgiveness.

The next surah begins with two solemn oaths. Allah swears by the Day of Resurrection, the Day when all people will be brought back to life. He also swears by the self-blaming soul, the soul that criticizes itself and blames its owner after he does wrong. These two oaths prepare the reader for the main subject of the surah, which is the certainty that every person will be raised again and will stand before Allah.

hardWords.m: speaking to someone on behalf of another
to run away quickly from danger

326.title: Bones Gathered Again and No Escape

paragraphs.text: The surah asks whether man really thinks that Allah will not be able to gather his bones after they have crumbled and scattered. The answer is clear: of course He will. Allah is fully able to put them back together, and He is even able to shape and restore the tips of his fingers perfectly, down to the smallest detail. The real problem, however, is not a lack of evidence. Man wants to continue doing wrong in the time ahead of him, without any check on his behavior. So he asks with mockery when this Day of Resurrection will actually come.

The answer describes the frightening events of that Day. The eyes will be dazzled and confused, the moon will lose its light, and the sun and the moon will be brought together. On that Day man will cry out, asking where he can run to. But there will be no place to hide and no shelter at all. On that Day the final place of settlement will be with the Lord alone. Man will be told about everything he sent ahead and everything he left behind, both his good and bad actions. In truth, a person will be a witness against himself and will know his own deeds well, even if he offers all kinds of excuses to defend himself.

In the middle of these warnings comes a personal instruction to the Prophet about receiving the Qur'an. He is told not to move his tongue quickly in order to hurry with its recitation while it is being revealed. Allah promises that it is His responsibility to gather the Qur'an in the Prophet's heart and to make it possible for him to recite it. So when Allah has recited it to him, the Prophet should follow its recitation attentively. After that, it is also upon Allah to make its meaning clear to him. These ayahs reassure the Prophet that he does not need to worry about forgetting any part of what is revealed, since Allah Himself has taken responsibility for preserving it and explaining it.

hardWords.m: to bring back to the original state
unable to see clearly because of strong light or shock
a place where one stays finally
to make someone feel calm and less worried

327.title: Radiant Faces and the Moment of Death

paragraphs.text: The surah returns to the subject of the deniers and speaks to them directly with a firm denial. People are told plainly that their real weakness is their love for the life of this world, which is quick and close at hand, while they abandon and neglect the Hereafter. Yet on the Day of Resurrection people will be divided into two groups. Some faces on that Day will shine with brightness and joy, and they will be looking at their Lord. Their joy will be complete on that Day. Other faces will be twisted and gloomy with fear, because their owners will expect that something crushing, something that breaks the back, is about to happen to them.
