Then the surah describes the moment of death in vivid detail. When the soul has risen up to the collar bones, the people standing around the dying person will ask who can save him and whether there is anyone able to cure him. The dying man himself will realize with certainty that this is the moment of parting from this world and from everything he knew. One leg will be twisted around the other leg as life leaves the body. On that Day the journey of every soul will be driven toward its Lord, and there will be no turning back.

The surah then describes a person who rejected the truth during his life. He neither believed nor prayed. Instead, he denied the message and turned away from it. After that, he went back to his own people walking proudly, full of himself, as though he had done something great by rejecting the truth that came to him. A strong warning is then repeated: woe to him, and again woe; and once more, woe to him, and woe. The repetition makes the warning sound even more serious and urgent. Finally, the surah asks a question that every reader should think about: does man really believe that he will be left alone, without any purpose, responsibility or accountability for what he did?

hardWords.m: to fail to take care of something
very clear and full of detail
having to explain and answer for what you did

328.title: From a Drop to a Garden of Silk

paragraphs.text: The surah ends by reminding man of his own beginning. Was he not once only a small drop of fluid? Then he became a clinging clot, after which Allah created him, shaped him and gave him a balanced form. From this same beginning, Allah made the two kinds, male and female. The final question follows naturally from this description: is the One who did all of this not able to give life to the dead? The answer is clearly yes.

A new surah opens with another question about human origins. Was there not a long period of time when man was nothing worth mentioning at all? Allah created him from a mixed drop in order to test him, and gave him the abilities of hearing and seeing. Allah then showed him the right way, leaving him free to be either grateful or ungrateful. For those who choose disbelief, He has prepared chains, iron collars and a blazing fire.

The righteous, by contrast, will drink from a cup mixed with Kafur, from a spring that the servants of Allah will make flow abundantly wherever they wish. The surah then describes the qualities that earned them this reward. They fulfill their vows and fear a Day whose evil will spread far and wide. Although they love food themselves, they give it to the needy, the orphan and the captive. They say that they feed them only to seek the face of Allah, and that they want no reward or thanks in return. They explain that they fear from their Lord a Day that will be grim and full of distress.

Because of this, Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and grant them brightness on their faces and happiness in their hearts. As a reward for their patience, He will give them a garden and garments of silk. They will recline there on decorated couches, and they will feel neither the burning heat of the sun nor bitter cold. Everything about their new home will be comfortable, peaceful and pleasant, a fitting reward for those who were patient, generous and sincere in this life.

hardWords.m: to lean back and rest comfortably

329.title: Delights of Paradise and Steady Remembrance

paragraphs.text: The description of Paradise continues in rich detail. Its shades will be close above the people, and its fruits will hang low, easy to reach whenever they wish. Silver vessels and cups as clear as glass will be passed around among them, made of silver and filled to the exact measure they desire. They will be given a drink mixed with ginger, from a spring in Paradise called Salsabeel. Young servants who will never grow old will move around among them, so beautiful that anyone seeing them would think they were scattered pearls. Wherever one looks there, one will see delight and a great kingdom. The people of Paradise will wear green garments of fine silk and rich brocade, and they will be adorned with silver bracelets. Their Lord will give them a pure drink. Then they will be told that this is their reward, and that their efforts in the world have been accepted and appreciated.

Allah reminds the Prophet that it is He who has sent down the Qur'an to him in stages, part after part. Therefore he should wait patiently for his Lord's decision and should not obey any sinner or ungrateful person among the people. He is told to remember the name of his Lord in the morning and in the evening, to bow down to Him during part of the night, and to glorify Him through a long portion of the night.

The disbelievers love the short life of this world and leave behind them, without thought, a heavy and serious Day. Yet it was Allah who created them and made their bodies strong, and whenever He wills, He can replace them completely with others like them. This surah is a reminder, so whoever wishes may take a path to his Lord. Still, no one can will anything unless Allah wills it, for Allah is always Knowing and Wise. Human choice is real, but it always remains within the will of Allah, who understands every heart and every situation perfectly.

330.title: Oaths by the Winds and the Day of Judgement

paragraphs.text: The surah closes with a final statement about the two possible outcomes for human beings. Allah admits into His mercy whomever He wills, and no one can stop His mercy from reaching those He chooses. But for the wrongdoers, He has prepared a painful punishment. Both outcomes are in His hands, and both are based on His perfect knowledge and wisdom.

A new surah opens with a series of powerful oaths. Allah swears by the winds that are sent out one after another in gusts, and by the winds that blow with great violence. He swears by the winds that spread the clouds far and wide. He also swears by the angels who bring the criterion that separates truth from falsehood, and by those who deliver a message from their Lord. This message comes either to remove every excuse or to give a warning. After these oaths, Allah declares the main point: what people have been promised will certainly happen, without any doubt.

The surah then describes when this promise will be fulfilled. It will happen when the stars lose their light and are wiped out, when the sky is split open, and when the mountains are blown away and scattered. It will happen when the appointed time for the messengers finally arrives. For which Day has all this been delayed? For the Day of Judgement, when everything will be decided. The surah asks what could possibly make anyone truly understand what the Day of Judgement is, showing how great and serious it is. Then comes a short warning that will be repeated again and again throughout the surah: woe on that Day to those who deny.

To support this warning, Allah asks a question that points to history. Did He not destroy the earlier peoples who rejected the truth? The answer is clear, since their stories are well known, and their end serves as a lesson for anyone who denies the message after them.

hardWords.m: something that separates right from wrong

331.title: Signs in Creation and the Shadow of Smoke

paragraphs.text: Allah declares that just as He destroyed the earlier peoples, He will make the later ones follow them in the same way. This is how He deals with criminals in every age, without exception. Then the warning that runs through the whole surah is heard again: woe on that Day to the deniers. Each time it returns, it reminds the reader that rejecting the truth carries a heavy cost.

Next the surah turns to the creation of human beings. Did Allah not create people from a fluid that seems weak and of little value? He placed it in a secure resting place inside the mother, where it stayed for a known and fixed period of time. Allah measured and planned every stage of this process, and He is the best of those who determine and decide. Human beings did not design themselves; every step of their growth was arranged by Allah. Yet many still deny Him, and so the warning is repeated: woe on that Day to the deniers.

The surah then points to the earth itself. Did Allah not make the earth a place that holds and gathers both the living and the dead? The living walk on its surface, and the dead rest within it. He placed on it tall, firmly fixed mountains, and He gave people fresh, sweet water to drink. These are clear signs of His power and care, which everyone can see every day. Still, the warning comes once more: woe on that Day to the deniers.

Finally, the surah describes what the deniers will be told on the Day of Judgement. They will be ordered to go forward to the very thing that they used to deny. They will be told to proceed to a shadow of smoke rising in three columns. This shadow will not give any cool shade, and it will offer no protection at all against the flames. The Fire will throw out sparks as huge as fortresses, and these sparks will look like a herd of yellowish camels. This picture shows how terrible that place will be for those who denied it.

hardWords.m: a case that does not follow the rule
to decide or fix something exactly
the top or outer layer of something
small pieces of fire that fly out

332.title: Silence of the Deniers and Rewards of the Righteous

paragraphs.text: Once again the surah repeats its warning: woe on that Day to the deniers. On that Day they will not be able to speak, and they will not even be allowed to offer any excuses for what they did. All their clever arguments from this life will be useless, and they will stand silent before their Lord. The warning is heard again. Allah declares that this is the Day of Judgement, when He has gathered together the present generation and all the earlier peoples. Then He issues a challenge to them: if they have any plan or trick, let them use it against Him now. Of course, no plan will succeed against Allah. And once more comes the warning: woe on that Day to the deniers.

In clear contrast, the righteous will be living among cool shades and flowing springs. They will have any fruits they desire, as much as they wish. They will be told warmly to eat and drink with pleasure and satisfaction, as a reward for the good deeds they used to do in the world. Allah explains that this is how He rewards those who do good. Then, once more, the reader hears the repeated warning: woe on that Day to the deniers. The two pictures, one of silence and helplessness and the other of comfort and joy, stand side by side so that the reader can compare them.

Then the surah speaks directly to the disbelievers. They are told to eat and enjoy themselves for a little while in this world, because they are criminals, and their enjoyment will soon end. Woe on that Day to the deniers. When they are told to bow down in prayer, they refuse to bow. Woe on that Day to the deniers. The surah ends with a powerful question: if they do not believe in the Qur'an, then in what other message, after this one, will they ever believe? The question is left for every reader to answer honestly for himself, and the surah ends there, with its repeated warning still sounding in the ears of those who hear it.

hardWords.m: reasons given to prove a point
people living at the same time
a call to try to do something difficult
a feeling of being pleased and content

333.title: The Great News and Signs of Allah's Care

paragraphs.text: A new surah opens with a question. What are the people asking one another about? They are asking about the great news, the matter over which they disagree and argue among themselves. It is a matter so important that it fills their conversations. The surah answers with a firm denial of their doubts: no, they will soon come to know the truth. And then it repeats this warning for emphasis: no, they will certainly come to know. The repetition shows that the truth they argue about will one day become clear to all of them, whether they accept it now or not.

Then the surah presents a long list of Allah's blessings, each one introduced as a question to make the reader think. Has Allah not made the earth a comfortable resting place, spread out for people to live on? Has He not made the mountains like pegs that hold it firm? He created human beings in pairs, male and female. He made sleep a means of rest for their tired bodies, made the night like a covering garment that wraps them in darkness, and made the day a time for earning a living and seeking provision. Each of these is a sign that people experience every single day, often without noticing it.

The list continues with the sky and the rain. Allah built above people seven strong heavens, and He placed in them a bright, burning lamp that gives light and heat. He sends down plentiful water pouring from the heavy rain clouds, so that through it He can bring out grain and plants of many kinds, as well as gardens thick with trees whose branches are twisted together. Every one of these gifts reaches people from Allah, and together they describe a world that is carefully ordered for their benefit.
Finally, the surah states its central message clearly. The Day of Judgement has a fixed and appointed time. It will not come early or late, but exactly when Allah has decided.

hardWords.m: special force given to show importance
short pieces of wood or metal that hold something in place
to go through or feel something
turned and wrapped around each other

334.title: The Horn, the Fire, and the Righteous

paragraphs.text: This passage opens with a powerful picture of the Day when the Horn is blown. On that Day, people will not come out alone; they will come forth in multitudes, great crowds, one group after another. The whole universe will change in ways that are hard to imagine. The heaven will be opened, and it will become like many gates. The mountains, which seem so solid and permanent to us now, will be removed, and they will become nothing more than a mirage, like the false image of water that a traveler sees in the desert heat.

Then the ayahs turn to Hell, which has been lying in wait, as if watching for those who crossed the limits. It will be their place of return, and they will stay in it for ages without end. There they will find no coolness to comfort them and nothing pleasant to drink. They will taste only scalding water and foul pus, which is a fitting recompense for what they did. The reason is made clear: they never expected that they would have to give an account of their deeds, and they denied Allah's verses with strong, stubborn denial. However, nothing was forgotten, because Allah has counted and recorded everything in writing. They will be told to taste the penalty, and they will be given nothing more except greater torment. These words are a serious warning, and they remind the reader that every action is written down and that denial does not make the account disappear.

After this frightening scene, the passage gives a very different picture for the righteous, who were mindful of Allah. For them there is real success and attainment. They will have gardens and grapevines, companions of equal age, and a cup that is always full. The contrast between the two groups is sharp and clear. One group meets burning water and endless pain, while the other receives gardens, fellowship and plenty. In this way, the ayahs invite the reader to think carefully about which path he is choosing in this life, while there is still time to prepare for that Day.

hardWords.m: a false picture of water seen in hot deserts
payment or result for what someone did

335.title: The True Day and the Oaths by Angels

paragraphs.text: The description of the righteous continues. In the gardens they will hear no evil talk and no lies, because everything there is pure. All of this is a reward from their Lord, a generous gift that is given in full measure. It comes from the Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything between them, the Most Merciful. Even so, no one has the authority to speak to Him on his own. On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows, none will speak except the one whom the Most Merciful allows, and he will say only what is right. That is the True Day, which will certainly come. So whoever wishes may take a path of return to his Lord. Allah has warned people of a punishment that is near. On that Day, every person will see what his own hands have sent ahead. The disbeliever, full of regret, will cry out that he wishes he were only dust. This final picture of the surah is short, but it is deeply moving and leaves a strong impression on the heart.

A new surah begins with a series of oaths. Allah swears by angels who extract with violence, and by those who remove gently and with ease. He swears by those who glide along as if they were swimming, by those who race ahead of one another, and by those who arrange every matter by His command. These oaths draw attention to something important that is about to be described.

That important event is the Day when the blast of the Horn will shake all of creation, and a second blast will follow after it. On that Day, hearts will tremble with fear, and eyes will be lowered in humility. Yet in this world, the deniers keep asking in doubt whether they will truly be brought back to their former life. They wonder how this could happen to them after they have become decayed, crumbling bones. Their question shows how far they are from believing in the meeting with their Lord.

hardWords.m: the right or power to do something
a sad feeling about something you did
rotten and broken down over time

336.title: Moses, Pharaoh, and the Raised Heaven

paragraphs.text: The deniers mock the idea of being raised again. They say that if such a return were real, it would be a losing return for them. But the answer is simple and direct. It will take only one shout, and suddenly they will find themselves awake and alert on the surface of the earth. What they thought was impossible will happen in a single moment.

Next, the passage asks whether the story of Moses has reached the reader. His Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa and gave him a mission. He told him to go to Pharaoh, because Pharaoh had crossed all limits. Moses was to ask him whether he would like to purify himself, and to offer to guide him to his Lord so that he might fear Him. Moses then showed him the greatest sign. However, Pharaoh denied it and disobeyed. He turned his back and worked hard against the truth. He gathered his people and called out to them, and in his pride he declared, "I am your most exalted lord." So Allah seized him with an exemplary punishment because of his first and his last transgressions. In this story there is a clear warning for anyone who fears Allah, since it shows how arrogance and denial end.

After the story, the ayahs ask people a question that makes them think. Which is harder to create: human beings, or the heaven? Allah built the heaven. He raised its ceiling high above us and made it perfectly balanced in every part. He made its night dark, and He brought out its daylight and brightness. When people look at the vast sky above them, they can understand that bringing them back to life is not difficult for the One who made all of this. The question is not asked to gain information, but to wake people up. It invites them to compare their own small size with the huge creation around them, and to see the power of their Creator clearly.

hardWords.m: to laugh at someone or something unkindly
an important job someone is sent to do
serving as a lesson for others
too much pride; thinking you are better than others

337.title: The Spread Earth and the Coming Hour

paragraphs.text: The passage continues to describe Allah's work in creation. After creating the heaven, He spread out the earth and made it ready for life. He brought out from it its water and its pasture, so that plants could grow. He also set the mountains firmly in their places. All of this was made as provision for human beings and for their grazing animals. In other words, the ground we walk on, the water we drink and the food we eat are all gifts that Allah has prepared for us.

Then the ayahs speak about the greatest Overwhelming Calamity, the event that will cover everything. On that Day, every person will remember what he worked and struggled for during his life. Hellfire will be brought out and shown clearly to everyone who can see. At that time, people will be divided into two groups. The first group is made up of those who crossed the limits and chose the life of this world over the Hereafter. For them, Hellfire will be their final refuge and home. The second group is made up of those who feared standing before their Lord and held their souls back from following wrong desires. For them, Paradise will be their refuge. The message is simple but powerful, because it shows that the choices people make each day lead them toward one of these two endings.

The surah ends by answering a question that people asked the Prophet Muhammad. They wanted to know about the Hour and exactly when it would arrive. The reply makes clear that this is not his matter to mention, because knowledge of its final time belongs to his Lord alone. His role is only to warn those who fear it. When people finally see that Day, it will feel to them as though they had stayed in the world for no longer than one afternoon or one morning. This shows how short life in this world really is, even if it feels long while we are living it. Therefore, the wise person does not waste time asking when the Hour will come, but prepares for it instead.

hardWords.m: land with grass for animals to eat
a terrible event that causes great harm
a place to stay or shelter
to come to a place or time

338.title: The Blind Man and the Honored Pages

paragraphs.text: This surah begins with a gentle lesson given to the Prophet himself. The ayahs say that he frowned and turned away, because a blind man came to him and interrupted him. Then the Prophet is asked a question that makes him reflect: how could he know that this man might be purified, or that he might be reminded and benefit from the reminder? The passage then compares two kinds of people. On one side is the person who thinks he needs nothing, and to him the Prophet was giving his attention, even though it would not be his fault if that person refused to be purified. On the other side is the man who came eagerly, striving for knowledge while he feared Allah, and yet the Prophet was distracted from him. Through this comparison, the ayahs teach that a sincere heart which seeks guidance deserves care and attention, whatever his situation may be. The lesson is told openly and honestly, and it shows how carefully the Quran guides the way people should be treated.

Then comes a firm "No!" which marks a change of direction. These verses are a reminder, and anyone who wishes may remember them and take benefit from them. They are recorded in honored sheets, which are exalted and kept pure. They are carried by the hands of messenger-angels who are noble and dutiful. These descriptions show how precious and protected the message is. It is not ordinary speech, but something carefully preserved from its source until it reaches people. For this reason, a reader should approach it with respect and with a willing heart.

The passage ends this section with a strong statement about human beings. Man is cursed, and how great is his disbelief! After hearing about such a noble reminder, carried in such a respected way, many people still refuse to believe. This short ayah expresses amazement at how ungrateful and stubborn a person can be when the truth is placed right in front of him. It also prepares the reader for the next part of the surah, which will remind man of where he came from and of the many blessings he has been given. In this way, the ayahs move from a personal lesson to a lesson for all of humanity.

hardWords.m: stopped someone while they were speaking
hardWords.bn: বাধা দিল / কথার মাঝে ঢুকে পড়ল

hardWords.m: honest and true from the heart
always doing what one must do
kept safe from change or loss

339.title: From a Drop to the Deafening Blast

paragraphs.text: The ayahs now ask man to think about his own beginning. From what substance did Allah create him? He created him from a small drop of fluid and then decided his measure and his path. After that, He made the way easy for him, so that he could live and move through the world. Then, at the time Allah has set, He causes him to die and gives him a grave to rest in. Later, whenever He wills, He will raise him back to life again. This short journey, from a drop to the grave and then to resurrection, shows that every stage of a person's life is in Allah's hands. Yet in spite of all this, the passage says with a firm "No!" that man has still not fulfilled what Allah commanded him to do.

Next, people are invited to look at something very ordinary that they see every day: their food. Allah poured down water in heavy torrents. Then He split the earth open, and from it He caused grain to grow. He also brought out grapes and green plants, olive trees and palm trees, gardens full of thick bushes, and fruit and grass. All of this was made as enjoyment for human beings and for their grazing animals. When a person sits down to eat, he rarely thinks about the long process behind each bite. These ayahs remind him that rain, soil and every plant are part of Allah's careful plan, and that they should lead him to gratitude rather than forgetfulness. The list is long and detailed on purpose, because each item is another blessing that a thankful heart should notice.

Finally, the passage turns suddenly to the end of the world. When the Deafening Blast comes, everything will change. On that Day, a man will run away even from his own brother. This sharp image prepares the reader for the next ayahs, which describe how every person will be busy with his own situation. The calm picture of food and gardens is replaced by a scene of fear and escape, showing how quickly the comfort of this world can disappear.

hardWords.m: the material something is made of
being brought back to life after death
so loud that one cannot hear

340.title: Bright Faces, Dark Faces, and the Folded Sun

paragraphs.text: The scene of the Last Day continues. A man will not only flee from his brother, but also from his mother and father, and from his wife and children. Every person on that Day will have a matter of his own that is enough to keep him fully busy. The people closest to him in this world will not be able to help him, and he will not even look for them. The ayahs name the people a man is usually closest to, his brother, his mother, his father, his wife and his children, and yet each one of them is left behind. Then humanity will be divided by the look on their faces. Some faces on that Day will be bright, laughing and rejoicing at the good news they have received. Other faces will be covered with dust, and darkness will spread over them. These are the disbelievers, the wicked ones. The contrast between light and darkness on the faces shows the difference between the final outcome of faith and the final outcome of denial.

A new surah begins with a series of shocking events, each introduced by the word "when". When the sun is wrapped up in darkness, and when the stars fall and scatter. When the mountains are moved away, and when she-camels that are about to give birth are left without care. When the wild animals are gathered together, and when the seas are filled with flame. When the souls are paired, and when the baby girl who was buried alive is asked for what sin she was killed. This last image is especially powerful. The question is put to the innocent victim herself, which shows how serious this crime is and how clearly the guilty will be exposed. Each of these events breaks the normal order of the world that people are used to. Things that seem fixed, such as the sun, the stars and the mountains, will lose their place. Even the wild beasts will be gathered together, and the seas themselves will burn. Through this list, the ayahs make the reader feel how complete and overwhelming the change on that Day will be.

hardWords.m: very great and too strong to resist

341.title: A Soul Will Know, and a Noble Messenger

paragraphs.text: The list of events continues. When the pages of deeds are spread open for all to see, and when the sky is stripped away. When Hellfire is made to blaze, and when Paradise is brought close. At that time, every soul will know exactly what it has brought with it. This is the conclusion of the long series that began the surah. All the shaking of the universe leads to one personal moment: each person will face the truth about his own actions. Nothing will remain hidden, and no one will be able to pretend that he did not know what he had done.

Then Allah swears by several signs in nature. He swears by the stars that pull back, which travel in their courses and then disappear from sight. He swears by the night as it falls and grows dark, and by the dawn when it breathes, as if the day were taking its first breath. These oaths lead to an important truth: the Quran is a word brought by a noble messenger. This messenger has great power and holds a secure position with the Owner of the Throne. He is obeyed in the heavens and is completely trustworthy. In this way, the ayahs explain that the message came through a reliable and honored path.

Next, the passage defends the Prophet Muhammad, who is described as "your companion", someone the people knew well. He is not mad at all. He truly saw Gabriel on the clear horizon. He does not hold back any knowledge of the unseen that was given to him; he passes it on. The Quran is also not the word of a devil who was driven away. After clearing away these false claims, the ayahs ask a simple but searching question: so where are you going? If the message is true and the messenger is honest, then turning away from it leads nowhere. The question invites each reader to stop and think about the direction of his own life.

hardWords.m: the line where the sky seems to meet the earth

342.title: A Reminder, the Split Sky, and Noble Recorders

paragraphs.text: The surah ends by explaining the purpose of the Quran. It is nothing other than a reminder for all the worlds, meant for anyone among people who wishes to follow a straight and right course. Yet the final ayah adds an important balance: people cannot will anything unless Allah, the Lord of the worlds, wills it. Human choice is real, but it always remains within the will of Allah. These three short ayahs therefore combine an open invitation with a reminder of Allah's complete control over everything.

A new surah opens, once again, with a description of the end of the world. When the sky breaks apart, and when the stars fall and scatter. When the seas burst forth, and when the graves are turned over and their contents scattered. At that moment, every soul will know what it sent ahead and what it left behind. The pattern is similar to the previous surah: great changes in the universe lead to a single, very personal moment of truth, in which each person discovers the real value of what he did and what he failed to do.

Then Allah speaks directly to all of mankind with a moving question: what has deceived you about your Lord, the Generous? He is the One who created you, shaped you in due proportion and made you balanced. He put you together in whatever form He willed. The question is gentle but serious, because it reminds people of the care that went into their creation and asks why they would be careless toward the One who gave them so much. Then comes a firm "No!", since the real problem is that people deny the Day of Recompense. Yet they are not left unwatched. Over them are appointed keepers, noble ones who record everything. These keepers know whatever people do, so no action, large or small, is missed.

This section ends with two clear and balanced statements. The righteous will certainly be in pleasure and delight. The wicked, on the other hand, will certainly be in Hellfire. Placed side by side, these two short ayahs summarize the final result of everything that has come before. The record kept by the noble writers will lead each person to one of these two places, according to what he has done.

hardWords.m: the reason for which something exists

343.title: The Day of Recompense and Cheating in Measure

paragraphs.text: The fate of the wicked is described further. They will enter the Fire and burn in it on the Day of Recompense, and they will never be absent from it. Then the question is asked twice, to show how great the matter is: what can make you know what the Day of Recompense is? The answer follows. It is the Day when no soul will have any power to help another soul in any way. On that Day, the command will belong entirely to Allah. In this world, people may depend on family, friends or powerful leaders, but on that Day all such help will disappear completely.

A new surah begins with a strong warning about dishonesty in trade. Woe to those who give less than what is due! When they take a measure from other people, they make sure to receive the full amount. However, when they measure or weigh for others, they give less and cause them loss. The ayahs then ask a searching question: do these people not think that they will be raised again for a tremendous Day? It is the Day when all mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds. The link is clear. A person who truly believed that he would stand before Allah would never cheat others, even by a small amount, because he would know that every unfair measure will be judged.

Then comes another firm "No!". The record of the wicked is kept in a place called sijjeen. Once again, a question is asked to show its importance: what can make you know what sijjeen is? It is a register that is written and fixed, in which their destination is recorded. Woe on that Day to those who deny, who deny the Day of Recompense. And no one denies it except every sinful person who goes beyond the limits. These ayahs show that denial of the Day is not simply a matter of opinion. It grows from sin and from crossing the limits that Allah has set. When a person keeps doing wrong, it becomes easier for him to reject the idea that he will one day be called to account. This warning is repeated so that the reader will not take it lightly, and so that he will examine both his trade and his beliefs.

hardWords.m: to rely on someone for help

344.title: Stained Hearts and the Record of the Righteous

paragraphs.text: The description of the deniers continues. When Allah's verses are recited to such a person, he dismisses them, saying that they are only legends of earlier peoples. But the answer is a firm "No!". The real reason for his reaction is that a stain has covered the hearts of these people because of what they kept earning through their deeds. Their wrong deeds have gathered until the heart can no longer recognize the truth. As a result, on that Day they will be separated and blocked from their Lord. Then they will enter and burn in Hellfire. Finally, it will be said to them: this is the very thing that you used to deny. What they called a legend will become their reality.

Then the ayahs turn to the opposite picture. The record of the righteous is kept in 'illiyyun, a high and honored place. Again a question is asked to show its greatness: what can make you know what 'illiyyun is? It is a written register, which is witnessed by those who are brought near to Allah. The righteous will be in pleasure, sitting on decorated couches and looking around. You will recognize the glow of happiness in their faces. They will be given a pure drink that is sealed, and the last of it will be musk. For this kind of reward, those who wish to compete should compete. The drink is mixed with water from Tasneem, a spring from which those brought near to Allah drink. This passage invites believers to direct their effort and their sense of competition toward what truly lasts, rather than toward the passing things of this world.

The final ayah of this section looks back at life in this world. Those who committed crimes used to laugh at the believers. This short statement prepares for the next scene, which will describe how the mockers behaved and how the situation will finally be reversed. It reminds the reader that the laughter of the wrongdoers is not the end of the story.

hardWords.m: refuses to think about something seriously
old stories that are not true
a dark mark that is hard to remove
to know someone or something when you see it
to try hard to do better than others

345.title: The Mockers Mocked, and the Obedient Sky

paragraphs.text: The ayahs describe in detail how the criminals treated the believers in this world. Whenever they passed by them, they would exchange looks of contempt with each other. When they went back to their own people, they would return joking and pleased with themselves. When they saw the believers, they would say that those people were truly lost. Yet they had never been sent as guardians to watch over the believers or to judge them. Then the scene changes completely. Today, on the Day of Judgment, it is the believers who are laughing at the disbelievers, while they sit on decorated couches and look on. The surah closes with a question: have the disbelievers not been repaid for what they used to do? The answer is clearly yes, and the reversal is complete.

A new surah begins by describing the end of the world in a new way. When the sky splits open, it listens and obeys its Lord, as it is bound to do. When the earth is stretched out, it throws out everything that is inside it and becomes empty. It too listens and obeys its Lord, as it must. The picture is of the whole creation responding to Allah's command without any delay or resistance. Even the sky and the earth, which are so huge and powerful, submit completely to Him.

Then Allah speaks to all of mankind. O human being, you are working hard and struggling toward your Lord, and you will meet Him. Every effort in life, whether good or bad, is a step on this journey. Then people will receive their records in different ways. Whoever is given his record in his right hand will be judged with an easy account. He will go back to his people full of happiness. But as for the one who is given his record behind his back, his situation will be very different, and the next ayahs describe what will happen to him. The contrast reminds the reader that the effort of this life will one day be measured, and that the way the record is received will show the final result. Each person, therefore, should think carefully about what he wants written in his own book.

hardWords.m: a feeling that someone is worthless
people who watch over and protect others
trying very hard with great effort
checked to find the size or amount

346.title: State After State, and the Sky of Great Stars

paragraphs.text: The ayahs now describe the person who receives his record behind his back. He will cry out for destruction, wishing for an end to his suffering, and he will enter and burn in a Blaze. The reason for this is explained clearly. In this world he used to live among his people happily, enjoying himself without care. He believed that he would never have to return to Allah. But the answer is "Yes!", because his Lord was always watching him and seeing everything he did. His careless happiness was built on a false idea, and that idea will collapse on the Day of Judgment.

Next, Allah swears by several signs that people can see in the sky. He swears by the soft red glow that appears after sunset, and by the night and everything that it covers and gathers. He swears by the moon when it grows full. These oaths lead to a clear statement about human life: you will certainly pass through one stage after another. Life does not stay the same, as the evening light fades and the moon changes; a person moves through different conditions, one following another, until he meets his Lord.

After this, the surah asks with surprise: what is wrong with them, that they do not believe? When the Quran is recited to them, they do not bow down to Allah. Instead, those who disbelieve simply keep on denying. But Allah knows best what they hide inside themselves. So they are to be given news of a painful punishment. There is, however, an important exception. Those who believe and do righteous deeds will receive a reward that never stops and is never cut off. The surah ends with this message of hope for the faithful.

A new surah begins with oaths. Allah swears by the sky that holds great stars, and by the promised Day which is certain to come. These opening words create a sense of greatness and seriousness. They prepare the reader for a story and a warning that will follow in the next ayahs, which will describe a terrible injustice and its consequences.

hardWords.m: something not included in a rule

paragraphs.text: The opening oaths continue as Allah swears by the witness and by what is witnessed. Then the ayahs tell of the companions of the trench, who are cursed. They had a pit filled with fire, packed with fuel, and they sat beside it. They were watching what they were doing to the believers, fully aware of their own actions. The only reason they hated these believers was that they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy. He is the One to whom the kingdom of the heavens and the earth belongs, and Allah is a Witness over everything. This means that although the cruel people were watching the believers suffer, there was a greater Witness watching them. Their crime was based on nothing except hatred of faith, and that makes it even more shameful.

Then the ayahs make the outcome clear. Those who torture believing men and believing women and do not repent afterward will face the punishment of Hell, and they will face the punishment of the Burning Fire. The door of repentance is mentioned, which shows that even great wrongdoers are given a chance to turn back. In contrast, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have gardens with rivers flowing beneath them. That is the great success. The believers who suffered may have seemed to lose in this world, but in the end they are the true winners.

Next, the surah describes Allah's qualities. The vengeance of your Lord is truly severe. It is He who begins creation and then repeats it. At the same time, He is the Forgiving and the Affectionate, the honorable Owner of the Throne, who does whatever He intends. This balance between severe punishment and loving forgiveness is a strong reminder to both the guilty and the faithful. Then a question is asked: has the story of the soldiers reached you, the armies of Pharaoh and Thamud? These were mighty armies that stood against the truth. Yet those who disbelieve still remain in constant denial, refusing to take a lesson from such stories.

hardWords.m: a long, deep hole dug in the ground
causing pain to others on purpose
to cause great pain on purpose
to feel sorry and turn back from sin

348.title: The Night Comer and the Decisive Word

paragraphs.text: The surah ends with three short but powerful ayahs. Allah surrounds the deniers from behind, so they cannot escape His power, even if they think they are free. In contrast to their denial stands the honored Quran, which is written in a Preserved Slate. In this way, the surah places the weakness of the deniers next to the permanence and honor of Allah's word.

A new surah opens as Allah swears by the sky and by the night comer. Then comes a question: what can make you know what the night comer is? It is the piercing star, which shines brightly through the darkness. This oath leads to an important truth: there is no soul that does not have a protector watching over it. Then man is told to look at what he was created from. He was created from a fluid that is poured out, which comes from between the backbone and the ribs. The One who created him in this way is certainly able to bring him back to life. That will happen on the Day when all secrets will be tested and brought into the open. On that Day, man will have no power of his own and no helper to support him. The argument is simple and strong: if a person accepts that he was made from such a humble beginning, he should not find it hard to believe that Allah can create him again.

Next, Allah swears by the sky that sends back rain again and again, and by the earth that splits open for plants to grow. These two oaths lead to a firm statement: the Quran is a decisive word that separates truth from falsehood. It is not a joke or a light amusement. It is serious speech that deserves serious attention. The ayahs then reveal what the deniers are doing. They are making a plan against the truth, working quietly to oppose it. However, as the next ayahs show, their plan will not be the only one, and they will not have the final word. The section reminds the reader that the Quran must be heard with an open and serious heart.

hardWords.m: is on every side of something

349.title: Glorify Your Lord, the Most High

paragraphs.text: The surah ends with Allah's answer to the plans of the disbelievers. They are planning a plan, but He too is planning a plan. Because of this, the Prophet is told to give the disbelievers time and to leave them for a while. There is no need to hurry, since their plan cannot defeat the plan of Allah. These final ayahs bring calm and confidence to the believer in the face of opposition.

A new surah begins with a command: exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High. He is the One who created everything and gave it the right shape and balance. He is the One who set a measure for each thing and then guided it to its purpose. He is the One who brings out the green pasture, and then turns it into dark, dry stubble. These descriptions remind the reader that Allah is in control of every stage of life, from creation and guidance to growth and decay.

Then Allah gives a promise to the Prophet Muhammad. He will make him recite, and he will not forget, except what Allah wills. Allah knows what is spoken openly and what is hidden. He will also ease the Prophet toward the easy way. So the Prophet is told to remind people, if the reminder will be of benefit. The one who fears Allah will accept the reminder and take lessons from it. However, the most unfortunate person will avoid it. He is the one who will enter the greatest Fire, where he will neither die nor truly live. This painful state, between life and death, shows how terrible it is to turn away from the reminder.

Finally, this section describes the one who truly succeeds. He is the person who purifies himself, who remembers the name of his Lord, and who prays. These are simple actions, but they have great value. Purification of the self, remembrance of Allah and prayer together form a path that anyone can follow. This short passage shows that success is not measured by wealth or position, but by the condition of a person's heart and his relationship with his Lord. It gives the reader a clear and hopeful goal, one that he can work toward every single day.

hardWords.m: a strong feeling of trust and certainty
short, dry stems left after plants die

350.title: The Lasting Hereafter and the Overwhelming Event

paragraphs.text: The surah ends with a gentle but honest warning. People prefer the life of this world, even though the Hereafter is better and lasts much longer. The ayahs show that what is near and quick attracts the heart, even when what is later is far better and permanent. The ayahs then add that this message is not new. It is found in the earlier scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. In other words, the same truth about the value of the Hereafter has been taught to people again and again throughout the ages.

A new surah begins with a question: has the report of the Overwhelming event reached you? On that Day, some faces will be humbled and lowered. They will be working hard and completely worn out, and they will enter and burn in a Fire that is intensely hot. They will be given water to drink from a boiling spring. Their only food will come from a poisonous, thorny plant. This food will neither nourish them nor satisfy their hunger. The picture is one of endless tiredness and need. Effort without reward, and eating without benefit, describe a life in which nothing brings relief, which is the opposite of what people hope for.

Then the surah describes the other group. Other faces on that Day will be full of joy. They will be satisfied with the effort they made in their earthly life, because now they can see its result. They will live in a high garden, where they will hear no foolish or unsuitable speech. In it there is a flowing spring, and there are couches raised up high for them to rest on. The contrast with the first group is very clear. While one group is exhausted and hungry, the other is calm, satisfied and honored. Their effort in this life was not wasted, and their reward is pleasant to every sense: what they hear, what they see and where they rest. These ayahs encourage the reader to make his effort now, in this life, so that he may be among the satisfied faces on that Day, rather than among the faces that are tired and humbled.

hardWords.m: containing something that harms or kills
to give the food needed for health
the ending of pain or worry

351.title: Look at the Camels, and By the Dawn

paragraphs.text: The description of the elevated garden continues with more details of comfort. In it, cups are placed ready for the people of Paradise. Cushions are arranged neatly in rows, and fine carpets are spread out everywhere. Each detail shows how carefully everything has been prepared for those who are honored there. Nothing is missing, and nothing has to be searched for.

Then the surah turns to the world around us and asks people to look and think. Do they not look at the camels, and how they were created? And at the sky, and how it was raised up high? And at the mountains, and how they were set up firmly? And at the earth, and how it was spread out? These are four things that people saw every day. The questions invite them to stop taking such familiar things for granted. If a person looks carefully at the animal he rides, the sky above him, the mountains around him and the ground beneath his feet, he will see signs of the One who made them all.

After this invitation to reflect, the Prophet is given clear instructions. He is told to remind, because his role is only to be a reminder. He is not a controller over people, and he cannot force anyone to believe. However, whoever turns away and disbelieves will be punished by Allah with the greatest punishment. The surah ends with two firm statements: to Allah is their return, and upon Him is their account. These final ayahs place the matter in its proper place. The messenger delivers the message, and Allah alone is responsible for the final judgment of every person.

A new surah begins with a set of oaths. Allah swears by the dawn, and by ten nights. He swears by the even and the odd, and by the night when it passes away. These short oaths name moments of time and simple numbers, and they call the reader to pay close attention to what will be said next. The rhythm of these opening ayahs is calm and steady, but it prepares the reader for serious lessons about past nations and about human behavior.

hardWords.m: soft bags for sitting or leaning on
well known from seeing it often
one who has power over others
a regular, repeated pattern of sound

352.title: Fallen Nations and the Test of Wealth

paragraphs.text: The ayahs ask whether these oaths are not enough for a person of understanding. Then they remind the reader of how Allah dealt with earlier powerful nations. There was 'Aad, the people of Iram, who had tall pillars, and whose like had never been created in any land. There was Thamud, who carved homes out of the rocks in the valley. There was Pharaoh, the owner of the stakes. All of them acted unjustly in the lands and spread great corruption there. So Allah poured upon them a whip of punishment. These nations were strong, skilled and proud, yet none of their strength could protect them. The section ends with a strong reminder: your Lord is always watching. Nothing that people do escapes His observation, whether they are weak or mighty.

The surah then describes a common mistake in human thinking. When Allah tests a person by being generous to him and giving him blessings, he says, "My Lord has honored me." But when Allah tests him by limiting his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me." Both reactions are wrong, because wealth and poverty are both tests, not signs of honor or disgrace. The answer is a firm "No!". The real problem lies in how people behave. They do not honor the orphan, and they do not encourage one another to feed the poor. They eat up inheritance greedily, taking all of it for themselves. They love wealth with an enormous love. These ayahs move the focus from what a person receives to what he does with what he has, which is the true test.

Then comes another "No!", this time leading to a picture of the end. When the earth is leveled, pounded and crushed again and again, everything that people built and gathered will be gone. This ayah prepares the reader for the scenes of the Day of Judgment that follow, when all the wealth that people loved so much will no longer have any value.

hardWords.m: tall, strong posts that hold up a building
property received from someone who died
very great in size or amount

353.title: The Reassured Soul and the Path of Hardship

paragraphs.text: The scene of the Day of Judgment continues. Your Lord will come, and the angels will come with Him, standing rank upon rank. Hell will be brought close, so that it can be seen. On that Day, man will finally remember, but his remembering will not help him at all. He will say, "I wish I had sent ahead some good for my life." He will realize too late what he should have prepared while he still had time. On that Day, no one will punish as Allah punishes, and no one will bind as He binds. Then the tone changes completely. To the righteous it will be said: "O soul that is at peace, return to your Lord, well pleased and pleasing to Him. Enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise." These beautiful words end the surah with a picture of complete peace and acceptance, offering hope to everyone who strives to please Allah.

A new surah begins with an oath. Allah swears by this city, Makkah, while the Prophet is free of restriction in it. He also swears by a father and the one who is born of him. These oaths lead to a clear statement about human life: man has been created to face hardship and struggle. Life is not meant to be completely easy. Every person will meet difficulties, and how he responds to them is part of his test.

Next, the ayahs describe the attitude of a proud person. Does he think that no one will ever have power over him? He boasts, saying that he has spent a great deal of wealth. Does he think that no one has seen him? These questions show how foolish his pride is. Allah has always been aware of him and of everything he does. Then a question reminds him of Allah's gifts: did We not give him two eyes? With these eyes he can see the world, and he should also be able to see the truth. The ayahs remind the reader that every ability a person has is a gift, and that it should lead him to gratitude rather than pride.

hardWords.m: a row or line, often of soldiers
the feeling or mood of speech
the way a person thinks and feels

354.title: The Difficult Pass and the Shining Sun

paragraphs.text: The list of Allah's gifts to man continues. Allah gave him a tongue and two lips, so that he can speak and express himself. He also showed him the two ways, the way of good and the way of evil, so that he can choose between them. Yet in spite of all these gifts, man has not attempted to climb the difficult pass. The image is of a steep and narrow mountain road that requires effort and courage to cross.

Then a question is asked to make the reader curious: what can make you know what the difficult pass is? The answer is practical and clear. It is freeing a slave, or feeding someone on a day of severe hunger. That someone may be an orphan who is a near relative, or a needy person lying in misery. On top of these actions, a person should be among those who believe, who advise one another to be patient, and who advise one another to show compassion. In other words, the difficult pass is not climbed by words alone, but by real sacrifice for others combined with faith and mutual encouragement. Those who do this are the companions of the right. But those who disbelieve in Allah's signs are the companions of the left, and over them there will be a fire closed in on every side. This section gives a very concrete picture of what true goodness looks like in daily life, and it shows that helping the weak is one of the hardest and most valuable paths a person can take.

A new surah begins with a series of oaths taken from the natural world. Allah swears by the sun and its morning brightness, and by the moon when it follows the sun. He swears by the day when it reveals the sun's light, and by the night when it covers it. He also swears by the sky and by the One who built it. These oaths move between light and darkness, between day and night, in a beautiful and balanced pattern. They prepare the reader for an important statement about the human soul that will come in the next ayahs.

hardWords.m: kindness and care for those who suffer
shared by two or more people
real and clear, not just an idea

355.title: The Soul, Thamud, and Different Efforts

paragraphs.text: The oaths continue. Allah swears by the earth and the One who spread it out, and by the soul and the One who shaped it in perfect balance. He placed within the soul an understanding of what is wicked and what is righteous. After this long series of oaths, the main point is finally stated. Whoever purifies his soul has truly succeeded, and whoever corrupts it has failed. This is the central message of the surah. Each person has been given the ability to know right from wrong, and his success or failure depends on what he does with his own soul.

Then the surah gives an example from history. The people of Thamud denied their prophet because they crossed all limits in their transgression. The most wicked among them rose up to do evil. The messenger of Allah, Salih, warned them to leave the she-camel of Allah alone and not to stop her from drinking. But they called him a liar and cut the legs of the she-camel. So their Lord brought destruction upon them because of their sin, and He made it fall equally on all of them. Allah does not fear the consequences of what He does. This story is a clear example of a people who corrupted their souls and therefore failed, just as the earlier ayahs warned.

A new surah begins with more oaths. Allah swears by the night when it covers everything, and by the day when it shines. He swears by the One who created the male and the female. These pairs of opposites lead to a statement about human beings: your efforts are diverse, and people work toward very different goals. Then the surah begins to describe two kinds of people. The first kind is the person who gives generously, who fears Allah, and who believes in the best reward. For such a person, Allah promises to make the path easy, leading him toward ease. This is a very encouraging promise. It shows that generosity, mindfulness of Allah and true belief open the door to an easier path in life and in the Hereafter. The ayahs that follow will describe the second, very different kind of person.

356.title: The Giver, the Withholder, and the Morning Light

paragraphs.text: The second kind of person is now described. He is the one who holds back his wealth, who thinks he needs nothing from anyone, and who denies the best reward. For this person, Allah will ease the way toward difficulty. In the end, what use will his wealth be to him when he falls to ruin? The money he refused to share will not protect him. This picture stands in sharp contrast to the generous person described just before.

Next, the surah makes two important statements. It is Allah's role to provide guidance, and to Him belong both the Hereafter and this first life. So people have been warned of a blazing Fire. No one will burn in it except the most wretched person, the one who denied the truth and turned away from it. However, the righteous person will be kept far away from it. He is the one who gives from his wealth in order to purify himself. He does not give in order to repay a favor that someone did for him, or to win something from people. He gives only because he seeks the face of his Lord, the Most High. And such a person will certainly be satisfied. These ayahs teach that the value of giving lies in its intention. A gift made sincerely for Allah, without expecting anything back from people, leads to true satisfaction. The surah therefore closes with a powerful lesson about pure motives in charity.

A new surah begins with words of comfort for the Prophet Muhammad. Allah swears by the brightness of the morning, and by the night when it becomes still and dark. Then He assures the Prophet that his Lord has not left him and has not become displeased with him. The image of morning light following the darkness of night gives a gentle feeling of hope and reassurance. These ayahs show Allah's care for His messenger, and they also give comfort to any believer who feels alone or forgotten during a dark time in life. The surah will go on to list more of Allah's favors.

hardWords.m: what one plans or means to do
tells someone firmly to remove doubt

357.title: Favors Remembered and Ease with Hardship

paragraphs.text: The comfort to the Prophet continues. The Hereafter will be better for him than this first life, and his Lord will give him so much that he will be satisfied. Then Allah reminds him of three favors from his past. Did He not find him an orphan and give him shelter? Did He not find him lost and guide him? Did He not find him poor and make him free of need? Because of these blessings, the Prophet is given three instructions. He must not treat the orphan harshly. He must not drive away the one who asks. And he should speak about the favor of his Lord. There is a clear link between the favors and the instructions: the one who was once an orphan should care for orphans, the one who was once in need should be kind to those who ask, and the one who has been blessed should be grateful by sharing the news of that blessing.

A new surah continues this theme of comfort. Allah asks: did We not open up your chest for you? Did We not remove the heavy burden that was weighing upon your back? And did We not raise your reputation high? Then come two very hopeful ayahs: truly, with hardship comes ease; truly, with hardship comes ease. The repetition makes the promise even stronger. Difficulty is never alone, because ease always comes with it. Then the Prophet is told that when he has finished his duties, he should stand up for worship, and he should turn all his hopes and longing toward his Lord. This short surah gives every believer a lesson in patience and hope, and it reminds him that after work there should be worship.

A new surah opens with an oath. Allah swears by the fig and the olive. The fig and the olive are two well-known plants, and the oath taken by them prepares the reader for an important statement about human beings that will be made in the following ayahs.

hardWords.m: in a cruel or unkind way
what people think and say about someone

358.title: The Best Stature and the First Command

paragraphs.text: The oaths continue. Allah swears by Mount Sinai, and by this secure city of Makkah. These oaths lead to a clear statement: Allah created man in the best stature, giving him a fine form and shape. Yet He then returns him to the lowest of the low. There is, however, an important exception. Those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward that never stops. So the surah asks the human being: after all this, what makes you deny the Day of Recompense? Is Allah not the most just of all judges? The surah is short, but its argument is complete. Man was given an excellent beginning, and his final state depends on his faith and his deeds. Because Allah is perfectly just, the righteous will not be treated like the wicked, and every person will receive what he truly deserves.

A new surah begins with a powerful command: recite in the name of your Lord who created. He created man from a clinging substance. Recite, for your Lord is the Most Generous. He is the One who taught by means of the pen, and who taught man what he did not know. These ayahs place great value on reading, writing and learning, and they connect all knowledge to Allah, the Creator and Teacher. Every piece of knowledge a person has is a gift from Him. Then the tone changes with a firm "No!". Man truly goes beyond the limits when he sees himself as free of need. A person who forgets that his knowledge, his life and his wealth all come from Allah easily becomes proud and rebellious. But the ayahs remind him that to his Lord is the final return. No matter how independent he feels, he will one day go back to Allah.

Next, the surah begins to describe a specific kind of wrongdoer. It asks the reader: have you seen the one who forbids a servant of Allah when he prays? The question expresses surprise and disapproval. Preventing someone from praying to his Lord is a serious crime, and the following ayahs will explain how Allah views such a person and what will happen to him. The section invites the reader to think about how strange it is for anyone to stand in the way of worship.

hardWords.m: the form and height of a body
people who decide what is right in a case
a feeling that something is wrong

359.title: The Forelock, the Night of Decree, and Clear Evidence

paragraphs.text: The questions about the one who forbids prayer continue. What if the servant he stops is on true guidance, or is calling people to righteousness? And what if the forbidder himself denies the truth and turns away? Does he not know that Allah sees everything? Then comes a strong warning. If he does not stop, Allah will drag him by the forelock, the front part of his head, which is a lying and sinful forelock. Let him call his group of supporters for help, and Allah will call the angels of Hell. The surah ends with a clear instruction to the believer: do not obey him. Instead, bow down in prostration and come closer to Allah. In this way, the surah that began with the command to recite ends with the command to worship.

The next surah describes a very special night. Allah sent the Quran down during the Night of Decree. A question is asked to show its greatness: what can make you know what the Night of Decree is? The answer is that this one night is better than a thousand months. During it, the angels and the Spirit come down by the permission of their Lord for every matter. That night is full of peace until the dawn appears. These five short ayahs give the believer a strong reason to value this blessed night and to hope for its goodness.

Another surah begins by speaking about two groups: the disbelievers among the People of the Scripture, and the polytheists. They were not going to leave their disbelief until clear evidence came to them. That clear evidence is a Messenger from Allah, who recites purified scriptures. In those scriptures are writings that are correct and upright. The ayahs explain that Allah did not leave people without proof. He sent a messenger with a clear and pure message, so that people would have no excuse. When the truth comes so clearly, each person must decide whether he will accept it or reject it, and the next ayahs describe how these groups responded.

hardWords.m: the hair at the front of the head
bowing down with the forehead on the ground
people who worship more than one god

360.title: Sincere Religion, an Atom's Weight, and the Chargers

paragraphs.text: The surah continues. Those who were given the Scripture did not become divided until after clear evidence had come to them. Yet they had been commanded only to worship Allah sincerely, devoting their religion to Him alone, turning away from falsehood, establishing prayer and giving zakah. That is the correct and upright religion. The disbelievers among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell forever, and they are the worst of creatures. Those who believe and do righteous deeds are the best of creatures. Their reward with Allah will be gardens of lasting residence with rivers flowing beneath them, where they will stay forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. This is for whoever fears his Lord.

The next surah describes the great earthquake at the end of the world. The earth will be shaken with its final shaking, and it will throw out its heavy burdens. Man will ask in confusion what is happening to it. On that Day, the earth will report its news, because Allah has commanded it to speak. People will then come out in separate groups to be shown the results of their deeds. The surah ends with two unforgettable ayahs. Whoever does even an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does even an atom's weight of evil will see it. Nothing is too small to be counted. This teaches the believer never to look down on any small good deed, and never to treat any small sin as unimportant.

Another surah opens with vivid oaths. Allah swears by the racers that run panting, by those that strike sparks as they go, and by those that charge forward at dawn. They stir up clouds of dust and rush together into the center as one group. The scene is full of speed, noise and energy, and it captures the reader's attention completely. These powerful oaths lead to an important statement about human nature in the following ayahs.

hardWords.m: very clear and full of life

361.title: Ungrateful Man and the Striking Calamity

paragraphs.text: After the dramatic oaths about the racers, the main point of the surah is stated. Man is truly ungrateful to his Lord. He himself is a witness to this, because his actions show it clearly. He is also intense in his love of wealth. Then the surah asks a serious question: does he not know what will happen when the contents of the graves are scattered, and when what is hidden in people's chests is brought out into the open? On that Day, their Lord will be fully aware of them and of everything they did. The message is that a person may forget the favors of Allah and chase after money, but on the Day of Judgment all his hidden thoughts and intentions will be exposed, and nothing will be kept secret from his Lord.

The next surah begins by repeating the name of a terrifying event: the Striking Calamity. What is the Striking Calamity? And what can make you know what the Striking Calamity is? The repetition builds a sense of fear and expectation. Then the answer is given in two unforgettable images. It is the Day when people will be like moths scattered in every direction, flying around in confusion. And the mountains will be like wool that has been fluffed up, light and soft, without any weight or strength. People will look as small and weak as insects, and the mountains that once seemed so strong will be as light as wool.

Then the surah describes the weighing of deeds. As for the one whose scales are heavy with good deeds, he will live a pleasant and satisfying life. But as for the one whose scales are light, his home will be an abyss. And what can make you know what that is? It is a Fire that is intensely hot. These ayahs show that on that Day, the only thing that will matter is the weight of a person's deeds. Wealth, power and fame will have no weight at all. This should encourage every reader to add good deeds to his scale while he still has the chance, so that his scale is heavy when the time comes.

hardWords.m: exciting and full of strong action
flying insects that come out at night
a very deep hole or pit

362.title: Distracted by Increase, Time, and the Crusher

paragraphs.text: This surah begins by describing a very common human weakness. Competing with one another for more and more worldly things keeps people busy and distracted, until they finally visit the graveyards. Then comes a firm warning, repeated twice for emphasis: no, you are going to know; then no, you are going to know. If only people knew with real certainty, they would live very differently. They will surely see the Hellfire. Then they will see it with the eye of certainty, so that no doubt remains. Finally, on that Day, they will be asked about every pleasure and blessing they enjoyed. The surah reminds the reader that the race for more possessions does not last, and that every comfort a person enjoys today will be the subject of a question tomorrow.

The next surah is very short, yet it carries a complete message. Allah swears by time. Indeed, all mankind is in a state of loss. There is only one exception: those who believe, do righteous deeds, advise one another to hold on to the truth, and advise one another to be patient. These four qualities together describe the people who are saved from loss. Two of them are about a person's own faith and actions, and two are about how believers help one another. Every passing moment of time is either a step toward loss or a step toward success, depending on how a person uses it.

The following surah begins with a strong warning: woe to every person who insults others and mocks them. Such a person gathers wealth and counts it again and again. He imagines that his money will make him live forever. But the answer is a firm "No!". He will surely be thrown into the Crusher. A question is then asked to show how terrible it is: what can make you know what the Crusher is? It is the fire of Allah, kept burning without end. The surah shows the connection between greed, arrogance toward others and a false sense of security. A person who trusts in his wealth and looks down on people forgets that his money cannot keep him alive, and that he will one day face the consequences of his behavior. These ayahs teach the reader to treat people with respect and not to treat wealth as a guarantee of safety.

hardWords.m: special force given to show importance
a firm promise that something will happen

363.title: The Elephant, the Quraysh, and Small Kindness

paragraphs.text: The description of the Crusher continues. This fire rises up and reaches the hearts. It will be closed down over its people, who will be held in long, extended columns. These ayahs complete the picture of the punishment for the mocker who trusted in his wealth. The fire reaches the very place where his pride and greed began, which is his heart.

The next surah asks the Prophet Muhammad whether he has considered how his Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant. Allah turned their plan into failure and confusion. He sent against them birds in flocks, which struck them with stones of hard clay. In the end, He made them like straw that has been eaten. The story shows that even a powerful force with a great animal on its side cannot succeed against Allah's will. A plan made against Him is turned into nothing, and the mighty become as weak and useless as chewed straw.

The following surah speaks about the tribe of Quraysh. They were used to security and safety, especially in their regular caravan journeys in winter and in summer. Because of these blessings, they are told to worship the Lord of this House. He is the One who fed them and saved them from hunger, and who made them safe and saved them from fear. The surah connects two basic human needs, food and safety, with the duty of worship. When a person enjoys enough food and peace of mind, he should remember who gave them to him and respond with gratitude and worship.

Another surah begins with a question: have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? He is the one who pushes the orphan away roughly, and who does not encourage others to feed the poor. The ayahs show that denial of the Day of Judgment is not only a belief in the mind; it appears in a person's harsh treatment of the weak. Then comes a surprising warning: woe to those who pray, but who are heedless of their prayer. Prayer that is done carelessly, without real attention, does not protect a person from this warning. These ayahs teach that true faith must be seen in sincere worship and in kindness to those who are in need, and that the two cannot be separated. The next ayahs will add more details about these careless people.

hardWords.m: a group of travelers moving together with goods

paragraphs.text: The surah ends by describing the careless people more fully. They do their deeds only to be seen by others, and they refuse to give even simple help to people who need it. Their prayer is for show, and their hands are closed to small acts of kindness.

The next surah brings good news to the Prophet Muhammad. Allah has granted him al-Kawthar, a gift given to him by his Lord. In response to this gift, he is told to pray to his Lord and to offer sacrifice to Him alone. The surah ends by saying that it is his enemy, and not he, who is the one cut off. These three short ayahs carry comfort, a command to worship, and a firm promise.

The following surah gives the Prophet words to say clearly to the disbelievers. He declares that he does not worship what they worship, and they do not worship what he worships. He will never worship what they worship, and they will not worship what he worships. Finally he says: for you is your religion, and for me is my religion. The repetition makes the separation between true worship and false worship completely clear. There is no mixing or compromise in the matter of who is worshipped. At the same time, the message is calm and simple, without anger or insult.

Next comes a surah about victory. When the help of Allah and the conquest arrive, and the Prophet sees people entering the religion of Allah in large groups, he is told to glorify his Lord with praise and to ask Him for forgiveness. Indeed, Allah always accepts repentance. This surah teaches an important manner for times of success: instead of becoming proud, the believer should turn to Allah with praise and humility, and seek His forgiveness.

The final surah of this day speaks about Abu Lahab by name. May his hands be ruined, and he is ruined. His wealth and everything he earned will not help him at all. He will enter and burn in a Fire of blazing flame. The ayahs show that wealth and status cannot save anyone who stands against Allah's message.

hardWords.m: an agreement where each side gives up something

paragraphs.text: The surah about Abu Lahab ends by mentioning his wife as well. She is described as the carrier of firewood, and around her neck will be a rope of twisted fiber. Husband and wife are mentioned together, and the same end awaits them both.

The next surah is a short but complete statement of Allah's oneness. The Prophet is told to say: He is Allah, the One. Allah is the Eternal Refuge, the One whom all creation needs, while He needs no one. He does not have children, and He was not born from anyone. And there is nothing at all that is equal or comparable to Him. In just four ayahs, this surah removes every false idea about Allah and describes Him with perfect clarity. It teaches the reader that Allah is unique in every way, completely independent and without any partner or equal.

The following surah teaches the believer how to seek protection. He is told to say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak from the evil of what He has created. He also seeks protection from the evil of darkness when it settles, from the evil of those who blow on knots, and from the evil of an envious person when he envies. Each kind of evil is named one by one, and for each one the believer turns to the same Lord. This surah reminds the believer that he does not need to face hidden dangers alone; he can always turn to his Lord for safety.

The final surah of the Quran also teaches the believer to seek refuge. He says: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the One whom mankind should worship. He seeks protection from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws and hides, who whispers evil into the hearts of people. This whisperer may come from among the jinn or from among mankind. In this way, the Quran ends with a prayer for protection from hidden evil within the heart. After a full year of reading, the reader finishes with a reminder that Allah is the Lord, King and only true object of worship, and that every believer should turn to Him for protection each day of his life.

hardWords.m: the only one of its kind
one who speaks very quietly into the ear
